articles.title: Travis Kelce: Kansas City Chiefs tight end agrees three-year $54.7m contract extension
articles.summary: Three-time Super Bowl-winning tight end Travis Kelce recently confirmed he is staying with the Kansas City Chiefs for a 14th season in the NFL despite having been linked to retirement this offseason; Kelce has now signed a three-year extension with the organisation
articles.body:
Travis Kelce has officially signed a three-year $54.7m contract extension with the Kansas City Chiefs after recently confirming he is staying with the team.

The veteran tight end quashed retirement speculation earlier this offseason as he committed to remaining in Kansas City for at least another season.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Monday that he has agreed a $54.735m deal potentially worth up to $57.735m.

"Chiefs Kingdom, let's go baby! It's official, excited for 2026 and just excited to put on the Chiefs uniform in front of you guys again," Kelce said on Instagram. "Let's get Arrowhead rockin' baby, we'll see you in a few months!"

  • Dolphins release QB Tagovailoa in record $99m cap hit
  • Commanders and Jags to play 2026 NFL London games

The length of the deal should give Kelce some flexibility on his future moving forward as the Chiefs wait on the return of Patrick Mahomes from a serious knee injury that saw him undergo surgery late last season. Should Mahomes' recovery stretch into the opening weeks of the 2026 campaign, Kelce would still potentially have the opportunity to play another full campaign with his star quarterback.

Kelce has won three Super Bowl rings during his 13 campaigns with the team as one of the leading faces of Andy Reid's Chiefs dynasty alongside Mahomes, with whom he has formed one of the league's most prolific tandems.

The 36-year-old helped Kansas City reach the Super Bowl in five of six seasons from 2019-2024 while breaking NFL records in postseason receptions, Super Bowl receptions and postseason touchdown catches by a tight end.

Kelce, a third-round pick for the Chiefs in 2013, finished the 2025 campaign with 76 catches for 851 yards through the air as the Chiefs fell to a 6-11 finish while missing out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014.

Despite a disappointing season, Kelce still managed to become the third tight end in NFL history to reach 13,000 receiving yards, doing so in a record time of just 192 games.

The Chiefs bolstered their offense during free agency by acquiring Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III on a three-year $45m deal. Kansas City also added quarterback Justin Fields as Mahomes continues his recovery.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback says he will retire after 2026 NFL season - 'This is it'
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has confirmed 2026 will be his last season in the NFL; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Rodgers is heading into his 22nd season; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports; get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has confirmed the 2026 season, his 22nd in the NFL, will be his last as he is set to retire.

"This is it," Rodgers said when the four-time NFL MVP was asked if this would be his final year.

The 42-year-old did not expand on why he came to that conclusion when making his first public comments since signing a one-year deal to return to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Monday.

  • Download the Sky Sports App to see the full 2026 NFL schedule
  • Record nine NFL games to be played abroad in 2026 season
  • Raiders select Fernando Mendoza with No 1 pick at NFL Draft

Rodgers had originally arrived in Pittsburgh in the wake of two disappointing seasons with the New York Jets, the first of which saw him suffer a year-ending Achilles injury four plays into his debut.

His decision to stay with the Steelers means he will have a reunion with first-year Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.

The two spent 13 seasons together in Green Bay earlier in their careers, and Rodgers pointed to McCarthy's hiring as Mike Tomlin's replacement as a major factor in his decision to run it back one last time.

"It is like a (bunch of) 'pinch me' moments that have happened in the last few days," he said following the second day of Pittsburgh's voluntary organised team activities.

McCarthy and Rodgers won a Super Bowl together at Green Bay after the 2010 season, and they remained in frequent contact over the winter and into the spring as Rodgers weighed up whether he wanted to put his body through the rigors of a 17-game season.

Rodgers ultimately landed on 'yes', hoping for the rarest of exits: one he can dictate on his own terms.

articles.title: NFL pre-season: Aaron Donald teases return, Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson battle for Browns quarterback spot - talking points
articles.summary: Sky Sports analyses three key storylines ahead of the first full week of NFL season; defensive great Aaron Donald is flirting with a return to the Rams; Shedeur Sanders is battling with Deshaun Watson for a starting quarterback berth; No 1 pick Fernando Mendoza makes his professional debut
articles.body:
All 32 teams are in action as the first full week of NFL pre-season gets underway live on Sky Sports - here are three key storylines to look out for ahead of the new season...

Donald return to Rams in the balance

The name on everyone's lips heading into the 2026 NFL season is that of Aaron Donald - despite the fact that the Rams legend retired well over two years ago.

Donald - widely regarded as one of the greatest defensive players of all time - has been flirting with a return to his former team after the acquisition of last season's NFL sack leader Myles Garrett in a trade with the Cleveland Browns, giving fans hope of a tantalising combination in the Rams' front four.

The three-time defensive player of the year worked out with the Rams in August, but is yet to make his return official, with Rams head coach Sean McVey keen to relieve any pressure on Donald ahead of a decision.

"He looked great, and he's still continuing to go through his process," McVay said. "No new news on that front. ... We've had a plan in place for a while, and the workout was one of those things.

"He's feeling good, but we're not to where we're able to say that he is or isn't ready to do it. But he's doing great, and he looked outstanding, as I think all of us would expect."

There are just four weeks to go until the beginning of the regular season - and Donald still has fans on tenterhooks as he weighs up making a remarkable comeback to the sport.

Sanders and Watson battling for Browns' quarterback berth

Perhaps the most high-profile positional battle in the NFL is that of the struggle between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson for the role of Cleveland's starting quarterback.

New head coach Todd Monken has awarded Watson the start in the Browns' pre-season opener against the Bears in Chicago, with Sanders taking the reins in the second half.

Monken, though, confirmed that Sanders will start their next pre-season game against the Bills, indicating that it's still anyone's guess as to who will start when it counts in week one.

"We're going to see both of them," said Monken. "One's going to start this week and one's going to start next week."

Watson and Sanders are at different ends of their respective career spectrums.

The 30-year-old Watson's tenure with the Browns has been mired by injuries and turmoil. Cleveland acquired him in 2022 and signed him to a fully guaranteed $230m contract, but he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury in 2023 and came back the next season only to twice rupture his Achilles tendon.

The former Texan was also suspended 11 games by the NFL in 2022 after being accused of sexual assault and misconduct by two dozen massage therapists while playing in Houston. Watson strongly denied the allegations and an NFL investigation found 'insufficient evidence to support a finding of a violation of the personal conduct policy'.

Watson's snaps against Chicago will be his first since October 20, 2024, a span of 22 months.

Sanders - son of NFL Hall-of-Famer Deion Sanders - showed promise while starting seven games as a rookie in 2025, but posted middling numbers of 1,400 passing yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, well off Watson's peak in 2020, when he led the NFL in passing yards with 4,823, notching 33 touchdowns and 7 interceptions to boot.

Cleveland's next four pre-season games are crucial in deciding their starting quarterback for 2026, and - by and large - potentially the future career trajectory of both Sanders and Watson.

No 1 pick Mendoza in hunt to displace Cousins

Kirk Cousins has a tall task on his hands to remain the starting quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders, with 2026 NFL draft No 1 pick Fernando Mendoza breathing down the veteran's neck.

Cousins is entering his 15th NFL season and has been running the first-team offence so far this summer. The four-time pro-bowler is expected to be the starter when the Raiders open their season on September 13 against the Miami Dolphins.

Mendoza was the No 1 overall pick in this year's draft and won the Heisman Trophy after leading Indiana to their first national championship but looks to be starting the season as the backup, working with the second-team offence throughout training camp.

"[Mendoza] is continuing to grow," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said. "It's been a really impressive training camp as far as how he's prepared, and then he goes out there to practice.

"Things don't happen on the paper, the playbook, exactly how they do on the field. I think he's done a good job of adjusting."

Cousins joins the Raiders off the back of an injury-affected season with the Atlanta Falcons in which he posted a decent return of 1,721 passing yards, with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions.

He has a decent chance of lasting the season as the Las Vegas starter - but the long-term future of the franchise is in the hands of Mendoza, and this pre-season will give the Indiana phenomenon his first taste of professional action.

articles.title: Kylie Kelce gets emotional recalling the miscarriage that made her terrified to try again
articles.summary: NFL News: A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby.
articles.body: A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kylie Kelce admits the fear of trying again after her miscarriage never really went awayKelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again.According to Kelce, getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it. In early pregnancy, she found herself checking survival odds on a near-weekly basis, and by the later stages of her second trimester, that worry shifted into wondering whether a baby born that day could make it. She's been candid that this obsessive tracking wasn't necessarily a healthy habit, just one that helped her get through it, and one that carried into her later pregnancies too.Why she keeps returning to this storyKelce didn't have to revisit this topic; she's already raising four young daughters, and the loss happened years ago.But her reasoning for continuing to talk about it is straightforward. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. It's a message that fits her reputation for being unusually direct about hard topics, and one she's now delivered twice, in two different ways, likely for the benefit of anyone quietly sitting with the same fear.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Backfields Shaping Up to Be 2026 Fantasy Football Nightmares
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football season is inching closer by the day. With several weeks of training camp practices and the initial slate of NFL preseason games in the books, there's plenty of new intel for managers to sift through.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football season is inching closer by the day. With several weeks of training camp practices and the initial slate of NFL preseason games in the books, there's plenty of new intel for managers to sift through.

While these practices and exhibition contests have shuffled fantasy rankings, the running back position still looks as top-heavy as ever.

With only a small handful of high-volume, matchup-proof stars to choose from—all of whom will be drafted in the first few rounds—managers will undoubtedly find themselves sifting through heaps of unproven young players, past-their-prime veterans and injury-prone talents with the goal of finding the best possible options for their fantasy lineups.

While some of these unheralded prospects will break out early and certain older vets will find a way to stave off Father Time for at least one more season, a few backfield configurations already look doomed before the season even kicks off.

Whether they're too crowded, don't have a strong supporting cast or simply lack talent, these platoons won't have a strong fantasy impact in 2026.

With that in mind, let's highlight a few of these nightmarish backfields and point out why you should try to avoid drafting the running backs who comprise them.

Fantasy points, rankings, average draft position (ADP) and other metrics courtesy of FantasyPros using PPR data.

The Arizona Cardinals finished the 2025 campaign as the second-worst rushing team in football, an issue they prioritized fixing with the selection of Jeremiyah Love at No. 3 overall.

While Love provides Arizona with one of the most exciting running back prospects to enter the league in years—and the earliest drafted since Saquon Barkley went No. 2 overall in 2018—there is real potential for the Notre Dame product to underwhelm in fantasy.

Love already suffered a scary injury in the preseason, a high-ankle sprain that is likely to keep him sidelined until the 2026 opener. The rebuilding Cardinals may opt to further protect their prized investment by limiting Love's snaps and leveraging the immense amount of backfield depth the club has accumulated.

With Tyler Allgeier and James Conner working behind Love, the Cardinals have one of the NFL's deepest backfields. The coaching staff will likely choose to spread the touches around as often as possible, keeping each of these players in the mix on a weekly basis.

While Conner is coming off a major injury ahead of an age-31 season—his 10th in the NFL—he boasts a solid 4.4 yards per carry average for his career and seems to have some tread left on his tires.

Allgeier opened his career with a 1,000-yard rushing season with the Atlanta Falcons before sliding into a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson. Despite working behind one of the game's best running backs, Allgeier still garnered at least 150 touches, 600 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns in each of the last three seasons.

Even Arizona's RB4 spot is far more competitive than most. Regardless of whether Trey Benson—a third-round pick in 2024—or Bam Knight (an eight-game starter for the Cards last year) wins the job in training camp, Arizona will end up with a surprisingly competent fourth option rounding out the backfield.

Because of this platoon approach, it's unlikely that any member of Arizona's backfield will truly stand out in 2026. There aren't enough touches to go around, especially if the Cardinals find themselves playing from behind and abandoning the run as they often did last year.

The Carolina Panthers' ground game was average at best last year, but they at least had a clear-cut fantasy standout with Rico Dowdle leading the way.

With Dowdle departing in free agency, this unit has little clarity and could be one of the toughest to figure out in 2026.

The main candidates to carry the rock this season are Chuba Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks. Each has a fair share of red flags that should give any manager pause before selecting them near their current ADPs.

While Hubbard is only a year removed from finishing as fantasy's RB14, he plummeted to RB32 over the first eight weeks of 2025 before being replaced by Dowdle in the starting lineup and seeing his workload significantly decrease. He tallied a meager 52.4 fantasy points the rest of the way and comes into 2026 with real concern about his ability to return to form.

Brooks is an even riskier option, as injuries have been the unfortunate story of his NFL career. A series of ACL injuries have limited him to just three games in total and his production in those contests was almost non-existent.

Despite missing all of 2025 while recovering from yet another surgery, Brooks is set to see plenty of action in 2026 if he can stay healthy.

It remains to be seen which back will open Week 1 as Carolina's starter. Hubbard seemed to have the inside track due to his experience, but is now dealing with a tricky hamstring injury . That ailment, coupled with Brooks' clean bill of health and a vote of confidence from head coach Dave Canales, gave the backup some momentum heading into the preseason opener.

Expectations should be tempered following Brooks' ugly three-carry, five-yard rushing performance against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday. While he did catch his lone target for nine yards, Brooks has yet to show he's capable of living up to the hype surrounding him when he became the first RB off the board in the 2024 draft.

Given Hubbard's regression last year and recent hamstring injury, along with Brooks' longstanding injury concerns, it's best to avoid this backfield altogether in your fantasy draft.

The Minnesota Vikings backfield is one that managers will want to avoid during their draft. While top options Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason are both lingering until the ninth round or later in most formats, neither profiles as a viable fantasy starter this year.

Jones turned back the clock when he came over from the rival Green Bay Packers in 2024 before struggling last season. The nine-year vet dealt with several injuries that ultimately sidelined him for five games. He was ineffective in the contests he did suit up for, with a 9.9-point average only ranking 33rd at the RB position.

Mason was far healthier last year than his aging counterpart, but he still failed to move the needle. After landing in the Twin Cities following a trade from the San Francisco 49ers, Mason managed to tally just 128.9 points across 16 games. His 8.1 points-per-game average ranked 45th among RBs.

This two-man platoon has an even lower ceiling this season. Jones capped out with a high of 15.7 points in the 2025 opener, while Mason had just one game with more than 12.6 points last year despite being the team's clear lead back in five contests.

No Vikings running back posted a top-five weekly result. Mason's RB7 performance in Week 3 was the unit's only top-10 finish.

While the Vikings opted against making any significant acquisitions to improve their backfield this offseason, sixth-round rookie Demond Claiborne does have a chance to steal some playing time away from the veterans ahead of him on the depth chart. If Minnesota's top backs get injured or are ineffective, he could get some run as the team tries to find a spark.

Consider Claiborne a decent late-round dart throw in deeper leagues, but stay away from the established entities in this backfield unless they slip well past their current ADP.

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

The Washington Commanders have several intriguing running backs on their roster, but none project as more than bye-week and injury fill-ins for fantasy purposes.

While the Commanders did rank a stellar No. 4 in rushing last year, the team didn't have a single back finish inside the top-30 at the position in fantasy.

Rookie seventh-rounder Jacory Croskey-Merritt was the most productive with 140.3 points on the year, but his wild inconsistency made him tough to rely on. Croskey-Merritt had double the number of RB40 or worse weeks (eight) than he did RB10 or better performances (four).

Although JCM no longer must contend with Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Austin Ekeler for touches following their exits this offseason, Washington brought in several new backs to replace the outgoing incumbents. The key additions were veteran Rachaad White and sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen.

Assuming Croskey-Merritt becomes the nominal starter, White is likely to earn the second-largest workload in 2026. He's been a lackluster back for much of his career, but excels as a pass-catcher and should see notable volume as the team's top third-down option. He was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' starter for much of the 2025 season due to Bucky Irving's injury woes, finishing the year as the RB32 with 143.0 fantasy points.

Allen will likely garner a few touches per game to open his career, especially if he continues to shine throughout the remainder of the preseason. The rookie led the Commanders with 23 carries for 85 yards and a score last week, becoming the first RB in over a decade to log 20-plus totes with no negative plays during an exhibition contest.

While this collective level of talent could help the Commanders remain a force on the ground in 2026, none of the individuals offer real fantasy value. This is a situation that most managers are going to want to stay far away from if possible.

While some of these unheralded prospects will break out early and certain older vets will find a way to stave off Father Time for at least one more season, a few backfield configurations already look doomed before the season even kicks off.
Whether they're too crowded, don't have a strong supporting cast or simply lack talent, these platoons won't have a strong fantasy impact in 2026.
With that in mind, let's highlight a few of these nightmarish backfields and point out why you should try to avoid drafting the running backs who comprise them.
Fantasy points, rankings, average draft position (ADP) and other metrics courtesy of FantasyPros using PPR data.
The Arizona Cardinals finished the 2025 campaign as the second-worst rushing team in football, an issue they prioritized fixing with the selection of Jeremiyah Love at No. 3 overall.

While Love provides Arizona with one of the most exciting running back prospects to enter the league in years—and the earliest drafted since Saquon Barkley went No. 2 overall in 2018—there is real potential for the Notre Dame product to underwhelm in fantasy.

Love already suffered a scary injury in the preseason, a high-ankle sprain that is likely to keep him sidelined until the 2026 opener. The rebuilding Cardinals may opt to further protect their prized investment by limiting Love's snaps and leveraging the immense amount of backfield depth the club has accumulated.

With Tyler Allgeier and James Conner working behind Love, the Cardinals have one of the NFL's deepest backfields. The coaching staff will likely choose to spread the touches around as often as possible, keeping each of these players in the mix on a weekly basis.
While Conner is coming off a major injury ahead of an age-31 season—his 10th in the NFL—he boasts a solid 4.4 yards per carry average for his career and seems to have some tread left on his tires.

Allgeier opened his career with a 1,000-yard rushing season with the Atlanta Falcons before sliding into a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson. Despite working behind one of the game's best running backs, Allgeier still garnered at least 150 touches, 600 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns in each of the last three seasons.

Even Arizona's RB4 spot is far more competitive than most. Regardless of whether Trey Benson—a third-round pick in 2024—or Bam Knight (an eight-game starter for the Cards last year) wins the job in training camp, Arizona will end up with a surprisingly competent fourth option rounding out the backfield.

Because of this platoon approach, it's unlikely that any member of Arizona's backfield will truly stand out in 2026. There aren't enough touches to go around, especially if the Cardinals find themselves playing from behind and abandoning the run as they often did last year.
The Carolina Panthers' ground game was average at best last year, but they at least had a clear-cut fantasy standout with Rico Dowdle leading the way.
With Dowdle departing in free agency, this unit has little clarity and could be one of the toughest to figure out in 2026.

The main candidates to carry the rock this season are Chuba Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks. Each has a fair share of red flags that should give any manager pause before selecting them near their current ADPs.

While Hubbard is only a year removed from finishing as fantasy's RB14, he plummeted to RB32 over the first eight weeks of 2025 before being replaced by Dowdle in the starting lineup and seeing his workload significantly decrease. He tallied a meager 52.4 fantasy points the rest of the way and comes into 2026 with real concern about his ability to return to form.

Brooks is an even riskier option, as injuries have been the unfortunate story of his NFL career. A series of ACL injuries have limited him to just three games in total and his production in those contests was almost non-existent.
Despite missing all of 2025 while recovering from yet another surgery, Brooks is set to see plenty of action in 2026 if he can stay healthy.

It remains to be seen which back will open Week 1 as Carolina's starter. Hubbard seemed to have the inside track due to his experience, but is now dealing with a tricky hamstring injury . That ailment, coupled with Brooks' clean bill of health and a vote of confidence from head coach Dave Canales, gave the backup some momentum heading into the preseason opener.

Expectations should be tempered following Brooks' ugly three-carry, five-yard rushing performance against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday. While he did catch his lone target for nine yards, Brooks has yet to show he's capable of living up to the hype surrounding him when he became the first RB off the board in the 2024 draft.
Given Hubbard's regression last year and recent hamstring injury, along with Brooks' longstanding injury concerns, it's best to avoid this backfield altogether in your fantasy draft.

The Minnesota Vikings backfield is one that managers will want to avoid during their draft. While top options Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason are both lingering until the ninth round or later in most formats, neither profiles as a viable fantasy starter this year.

Jones turned back the clock when he came over from the rival Green Bay Packers in 2024 before struggling last season. The nine-year vet dealt with several injuries that ultimately sidelined him for five games. He was ineffective in the contests he did suit up for, with a 9.9-point average only ranking 33rd at the RB position.

Mason was far healthier last year than his aging counterpart, but he still failed to move the needle. After landing in the Twin Cities following a trade from the San Francisco 49ers, Mason managed to tally just 128.9 points across 16 games. His 8.1 points-per-game average ranked 45th among RBs.

This two-man platoon has an even lower ceiling this season. Jones capped out with a high of 15.7 points in the 2025 opener, while Mason had just one game with more than 12.6 points last year despite being the team's clear lead back in five contests.
No Vikings running back posted a top-five weekly result. Mason's RB7 performance in Week 3 was the unit's only top-10 finish.

While the Vikings opted against making any significant acquisitions to improve their backfield this offseason, sixth-round rookie Demond Claiborne does have a chance to steal some playing time away from the veterans ahead of him on the depth chart. If Minnesota's top backs get injured or are ineffective, he could get some run as the team tries to find a spark.
Consider Claiborne a decent late-round dart throw in deeper leagues, but stay away from the established entities in this backfield unless they slip well past their current ADP.
Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝
The Washington Commanders have several intriguing running backs on their roster, but none project as more than bye-week and injury fill-ins for fantasy purposes.
While the Commanders did rank a stellar No. 4 in rushing last year, the team didn't have a single back finish inside the top-30 at the position in fantasy.

Rookie seventh-rounder Jacory Croskey-Merritt was the most productive with 140.3 points on the year, but his wild inconsistency made him tough to rely on. Croskey-Merritt had double the number of RB40 or worse weeks (eight) than he did RB10 or better performances (four).

Although JCM no longer must contend with Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Austin Ekeler for touches following their exits this offseason, Washington brought in several new backs to replace the outgoing incumbents. The key additions were veteran Rachaad White and sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen.

Assuming Croskey-Merritt becomes the nominal starter, White is likely to earn the second-largest workload in 2026. He's been a lackluster back for much of his career, but excels as a pass-catcher and should see notable volume as the team's top third-down option. He was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' starter for much of the 2025 season due to Bucky Irving's injury woes, finishing the year as the RB32 with 143.0 fantasy points.

Allen will likely garner a few touches per game to open his career, especially if he continues to shine throughout the remainder of the preseason. The rookie led the Commanders with 23 carries for 85 yards and a score last week, becoming the first RB in over a decade to log 20-plus totes with no negative plays during an exhibition contest.

While this collective level of talent could help the Commanders remain a force on the ground in 2026, none of the individuals offer real fantasy value. This is a situation that most managers are going to want to stay far away from if possible.

articles.title: How 2027 NFL Draft Defensive Prospects Stack Up Against Recent Classes
articles.summary: The 2027 NFL draft class is the seventh cycle since the creation of the Bleacher Report Scouting Department. As hype continues to build around next April's group of talent, some context may be necessary to fully understand how good it may or may not be once the event begins in Washington D.C.
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft class is the seventh cycle since the creation of the Bleacher Report Scouting Department. As hype continues to build around next April's group of talent, some context may be necessary to fully understand how good it may or may not be once the event begins in Washington D.C.

"In speaking with scouts and executives this summer, I noticed more excitement than normal, and the upcoming 2027 class might actually live up to that standard-issue statement [of being loaded with talent]," ESPN's Jordan Reid reported .

Excitement has been amped up mainly because of a deep quarterback class that can feature a handful of first-round talents, as well as arguably the best singular talent B/R has evaluated to date. The defense shouldn't be overlooked, though.

Individually, the upcoming crop may not be top-tier across the board. In a vacuum, only one projection right now has a 2027 draft-eligible prospect as the top-rated player at his position compared to those previous six classes.

However, the potential exists within its entirety to be one of the best. The group is loaded with significant upside to place it among some of the top classes within the discussed time frame.

Keep in mind, the current evaluation process is in its infancy. The B/R scouts just finished their summer scouting. How each of the prospects respond during games through the postseason, all-star contests and the combine process will drastically influence perception.

As of now, everyone should be excited based on what the 2027 class can be, though it's not quite there yet.

Top 2027 Prospect : Colin Simmons, Texas (8.6)

B/R Era Best : Will Anderson Jr., Alabama (9.6)

Five edge-rushers have been chosen among the top-five picks between the 2022 and '26 draft classes. If the quarterback position doesn't sit atop a team's wish list, a pass-rusher is usually next in line.

Looking ahead, a couple of organizations should be giddy about the potential found among the '27 crop, particularly at the top.

Texas' Colin Simmons and South Carolina's Dylan Stewart are both true juniors, who will be 21 when drafted. Their skill sets do differ, though each has the ability to be an elite edge-rusher at the next level.

The B/R Scouting Department grades Simmons as the top edge prospect as the 2026 campaign nears.

"The Texas product's motor and increased production last season give him a slight advantage as of now," scout Matt Holder said . "Conversely, the South Carolina product experienced a slight regression from his impressive freshman year."

Simmons produced 21 sacks and 29.5 tackles for loss compared to Stewart's 11 and 22.5 during their first two seasons. The latter is a more traditional hand-in-the-dirt option, while the former will likely be an outside linebacker in odd fronts.

Regardless of how they are aligned, both could work their way into the conversation for the No. 1 overall pick depending on how everything breaks throughout the upcoming collegiate and NFL campaigns.

On average, five edge prospects have been selected in the first round of the last five draft classes.

Clemson's Will Heldt, Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore, Oregon's Matayo Uiagalelei and Miami's Dame Wilson III are also in the first-round mix at this juncture. Increased production this fall will elevate each of their draft stocks going into next spring.

Top 2027 Prospect : Will Echoles, Ole Miss (8.3) B/R Era Best : Jalen Carter, Georgia (9.5)

An interior defender's value skyrockets if they're able to consistently collapse the pocket as a true three-down option. Those options are rare, though. Jalen Carter set the standard as a legitimate difference-maker during the B/R Scouting Department era. No one in this year's class comes close to that level.

Grade-wise, Ole Miss' Will Echoles aligns more with Bryan Bresee, Byron Murphy II and Walter Nolen III among recent draftees. Each of those mentioned were rock-solid first-round options, with the latter two selected among their respective class' top 16 picks.

As DL1, Echoles can increase his status by improving in one key area, even though he's already a disruptive presence.

"The 6'3", 315-pound defender does have room for growth as a pass-rusher," Holder said , "but the Ole Miss product is the class' best run-defender in the trenches." Oklahoma's David Stone is another defensive tackle carrying a first-round grade to open the campaign. He's considered a notch or two below Echoles by B/R, but he displays explosive traits with significant growth potential during his second full season as a starter. Oregon's A'Mauri Washington is a semi-sleeper among this particular group, because his build indicates a traditional nose tackle. However, he displays good burst to go along with immense strength. He's capable of violently shedding blocks and getting into backfields to make plays.

The 320-pound defender may not be on par with Jordan Davis when he came out of Georgia, but an NFL team could easily select the first-team All-American sooner rather than later to anchor the middle of its defense. Conversely, Miami's duo of Ahmad Moten Sr. and Justin Scott can flat out get off the ball. Moten is the position group's best pure pass-rusher, while Scott resets the line of scrimmage. All five defensive tackles can work their way into next April's opening frame, which would be the second time in the last eight draft classes.

Top 2027 Prospect : Chris Cole, Georgia (7.7) B/R Era Best : Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah, Notre Dame/Arvell Reese, Ohio State (8.5)

The linebacker position tends to be situation-dependent. Since it's a devalued position in general, the top linebacker isn't going to be a first-round option at all times. An off-ball linebacker not hearing their name called in the opening frame isn't a surprise.

The opposite also occurs, as in this year, when two elite talents, Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, both become top-10 draft picks. The 2027 crop appears to be much closer to the former than the latter.

Georgia's Chris Cole currently carries the highest grade from the B/R Scouting Department. However, his status is a bet on traits and projection. Cole started one game for the Bulldogs in the last two seasons. He's played more than 30 snaps in a contest only six times. Despite the limited playing time, the underclassman finished fourth on the team with 59 total tackles, second with seven tackles for loss and first with 4.5 sacks.

Obviously, the former 5-star recruit is expected to take on a much more prominent role this fall. His length, athleticism and position flexibility portend a breakout season.

An argument can be made in Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa's favor as the crop's best pure linebacker. Unfortunately, he's dealt with knee injuries since high school. The 20-year-old returned to full-contact practices this week after last year's season-ending ACL tear. Texas' Rasheem Biles, Clemson's Sammy Brown, Texas Tech's Ben Roberts and Georgia's Raylen Wilson comprise the next tier of linebacker options.

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

Top 2027 Prospect : Leonard Moore, Notre Dame (9.0) B/R Era Best : Travis Hunter, Colorado (9.2)

Notre Dame's Leonard Moore is the second-highest graded prospect for the 2027 draft class regardless of position. His inclusion, combined with the depth of the quarterbacks and two premium pass-rushers, helps elevate the entire crop of talent, which is viewed as top-heavy.

To make Moore's standing even more impressive, he's the highest-rated pure cornerback prospect in the B/R Scouting Department era.

Technically, Travis Hunter held the highest grade as the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2025 class. However, he received a bump in grade due to his dual-threat capabilities. For comparison, Patrick Surtain II and Christian Gonzalez finished their draft cycles with 8.4 and 8.3 grades, respectively. Whereas, Moore already sits at a 9.0 (out of 10).

The unanimous All-American has all of the traits to be a No. 1 NFL corner. He's a 6'2", 197-pound defensive back with the length and technique to handle man and zone coverage responsibilities. The true junior has thrived since the moment he put on a Fighting Irish jersey.

"According to PFF's wins above average metric, he ranked as the third-most valuable cornerback in the nation as a true freshman in 2024, trailing only 2025 first-round picks Travis Hunter and Jahdae Barron," Max Chadwick wrote . "Moore earned a nation-leading 91.8 PFF grade as a sophomore." Cornerback is always a loaded position anyway, with an average of 33 drafted over the last five classes. Moore may headline the group, but far more will draw heavy interest throughout the draft process. Currently, B/R also grades Clemson's Ashton Hampton and Alabama's Zabien Brown as first-round options. Georgia's Ellis Robinson IV clearly has the upside to be in that same tier after coming on strong over the second half of the 2025 campaign. Miami's OJ Frederique Jr. is another possibility early in the process, as long as he builds upon last year's performance in limited usage.

Top 2027 Prospect : Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame (7.8)

B/R Era Best : Caleb Downs, Ohio State (9.2)

The 2026 safety class turned out to be the exception, not the rule.

This year, Caleb Downs was the No. 1 overall pick regardless of position. He's an outlier. Even so, the standout defensive back still didn't hear his name called among the top-10 picks. He and Kyle Hamilton are the only two safeties to crack the top 20 in the last five years. Even legitimate first-round talents, like Malaki Starks and Dillon Thieneman, lasted until the 25th slot.

Notre Dame's Brauntae Johnson is graded significantly lower than everyone mentioned. Johnson should be considered a second-tier safety prospect despite being the 2027 class' top-graded option.

His range falls closer to Jaquan Brisker, Brian Branch, Xavier Watts and Nick Emmanwori coming out of college, which places the Notre Dame prospect as a fringe first-to-second round possibility. Everyone mentioned turned into an outstanding NFL defensive back, though they weren't considered elite prospects entering the league.

Georgia's KJ Bolden finds himself in a similar position as Johnson. The two could be competing all season to eventually become the class' top safety.

The group contains more functional deep safeties than dynamic playmakers or versatile hybrid defenders. The safety position isn't generally valued highly anyhow. While the class has promise, it will take a back seat compared to nearly every other positional group in 2027.

articles.title: 1 Bold Prediction for All 8 NFL Divisions Heading into the Season
articles.summary: In three weeks' time, the 2026 NFL campaign will get underway with a Super Bowl rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots at Lumen Field.
articles.body:
In three weeks' time, the 2026 NFL campaign will get underway with a Super Bowl rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots at Lumen Field.

That places us in the heart of prediction season.

With the preseason continuing and training camps entering later stages, here is one bold take per division for 2026.

Prediction: It's a legit four-way fight in December

The Eagles just became the first team to win back-to-back NFC East titles since 2004, but I have a feeling the division will be a four-team race in 2026.

Philadelphia's margin for error has narrowed, and there is a wild-card element to the team, with a rookie essentially replacing veteran receiver A.J. Brown and the Eagles preparing to work with their fifth offensive coordinator in as many seasons.

There's no denying the offensive talent in Dallas, and the Cowboys have at least proactively addressed the defense this offseason.

The John Harbaugh-coached Giants are one of the most enticing young teams in football, with intriguing weapons at quarterback, running back, wide receiver, tight end and edge-rusher.

Let's also not forget that when Jayden Daniels was fully healthy just 20 months ago, the Commanders went all the way to the NFC Championship Game.

The NFC East has produced plenty of Royal Rumble-style races, and another could be on the way. Washington and Dallas should rebound and close the gap on Philadelphia, while New York could take a major step forward to make this a four-team dogfight.

Prediction: The Packers finish last despite a winning record

It is the wrong division at the wrong time for a talented Packers team with the personnel, coaching and experience to remain competitive, but Green Bay could be without superstar Micah Parsons for a significant portion of the 2026 campaign.

The Bears should continue to improve and build on an 11-victory division-winning season in Year 2 for Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams together.

The Lions might actually be the most talented team in football and should bounce back from an off year.

If the Vikings managed to go 9-8 with an inconsistent J.J. McCarthy at quarterback, their ceiling is considerably higher with Kyler Murray expected to have Justin Jefferson for a full season.

Just as we shouldn't forget that Washington made an NFC title game appearance in 2024, we shouldn't overlook the fact that Minnesota went 14-3 that season.

The Packers are a good team, but they still lack a clear-cut No. 1 target. Their offensive line struggled in pass protection last season and underwent changes that are not guaranteed to solve the problem. They also could be without Micah Parsons for a while.

Prediction: The Saints run away with the division as Buccaneers blow it up

The Saints owned this division for much of the Drew Brees era, with the Buccaneers taking over a soft NFC South once Brees retired. Now, each team's trajectory indicates they're about to swap the crown again.

The Bucs are relatively old, as key players from their 2020 Super Bowl team continue to decline or depart. Their coaching staff appears stale, and their quarterback may have reached his ceiling. Those concerns were evident in their 2-7 record after the midseason bye in 2025.

Meanwhile, 2025 second-round pick Tyler Shough posted a 103.8 passer rating in his final four games and frequently showed signs that he could be the long-term option under center in New Orleans as the Saints went 4-1 to wrap up the 2025 campaign.

Technically, the Bucs finished tied for first (despite their 8-9 record) in 2025, while the rebuilding Saints finished last after a slow start.

With quarterback situations still murky in Atlanta and Carolina, and significant issues remaining elsewhere on both rosters, expect New Orleans to climb back to the top of the division. The fading Buccaneers could then be headed for an offseason reset that ends the Todd Bowles era.

Prediction: The Rams do not win the division

Following an offseason acquisition spree, the Rams are a sizable Super Bowl favorite .

But don't forget that they didn't actually win this division despite an MVP performance from quarterback Matthew Stafford in 2025.

The mission should theoretically be easier with Myles Garrett likely providing an upgrade over Jared Verse and the secondary looking stronger, but Stafford is 38 and may have peaked in that campaign.

In 2026, he will be relying on a top-heavy receiving corps led by 33-year-old Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, who has spoken publicly about the positive impact of rehabilitation meetings on his life.

The 49ers matched the Rams' win total last season despite far worse injury luck than the rest of the division. Yet they may not even be Los Angeles' biggest threat, with the defending Super Bowl champion also residing in the NFC West.

I'm expecting Los Angeles to be in the mix as always, but I also believe folks on this hype train will be let down when they see the Rams struggle with what will be a very treacherous path.

Prediction: Only the Bills make the playoffs

This is really an indictment of the Patriots' outlook: They are primed for a post-Super Bowl hangover after a distracting offseason and now face an uphill battle with a target on their back in 2026.

New England benefited from one of the league's easiest schedules in 2025, but it is expected to face a significantly more difficult slate in 2026. The Patriots also ranked as the league's healthiest team by adjusted games lost in 2025, a level of availability that can be difficult to sustain from one season to the next.

They are not even the favorite to win their division, as there's a good chance the Buffalo Bills will bounce back to capture their sixth AFC East crown in a seven-year span in 2026.

And that just may leave New England out of the dance entirely, as I'm expecting the veteran Ravens, Chiefs and Bengals to rebound from off years and join the Broncos, Chargers, Jaguars and Texans in the AFC conference-championship picture.

Right there, the math starts to work against a wild-card Patriots squad.

That said, New England is still better off than the rebuilding Dolphins or a Jets team that has plenty of pieces in place but will be relying on a post-prime turnover machine as a bridge quarterback. Those teams lost a combined 24 games in 2025 and should be expected to join the Pats on the golf course come the middle of January.

The pecking order seems somewhat obvious in the AFC North, with Baltimore widely expected to take care of business, the Bengals and Steelers expected to battle in the middle and Cleveland predicted by many to be one of the worst teams in the NFL following the Myles Garrett trade.

And while that's easy to understand considering that this is a 5-12 team that dealt away the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, don't overlook the return there in 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year Jared Verse.

On top of that, there's new energy surrounding this team with straight-shooting Todd Monken's regime taking over. They at least have several interesting options at quarterback, several intriguing new talents at the skill positions and a shaken-up offensive line.

There will be growing pains, but don't be surprised if this retooled Browns squad takes advantage of a weak schedule and low expectations and performs a lot better than expected in 2026.

The Jaguars finished last season as one of the hottest teams in the NFL and are on a great track entering Liam Coen's second year.

The Texans might have the most skilled defense in the NFL and could be even better than their 12-5 2025 record if C.J. Stroud can rediscover his old groove.

Even the rebuilding Titans looked like they had turned a corner with 2025 No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward late last year before bringing in Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll this offseason.

Where does that leave the Colts in the AFC South?

After their Week 11 bye in 2025, the fast-starting Colts were held to 20 or fewer points five times in seven games. And even before going down with an Achilles injury that could very well impact his play this season, quarterback Daniel Jones had already fallen off a cliff with an 84.2 passer rating in his final five starts last year.

I don't think he's the answer, but the desperate Colts paid him that way anyway. And I'm not sure Shane Steichen is the guy to lead this team out of football purgatory (they've gone 9-8 or 8-9 in four of their last five campaigns).

There's really nothing special about this squad, which featured a bottom-12 scoring defense while sliding late last season.

Watch for it all to hit the fan in 2026 as the Steichen era concludes.

Prediction: Fernando Mendoza is starting by November 1

New Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak continues to back veteran offseason addition Kirk Cousins as the team's No. 1 quarterback, and there has been a sentiment in Las Vegas that the team won't rush things with top pick Fernando Mendoza.

And that makes sense considering Cousins' presence. This is a guy the front office actively pursued, rather than some lingering remnant from the 2025 roster.

Cousins will turn 38 this season and has not consistently played at a high level since his age-35 campaign. The Raiders have plenty of exciting young talent and need to keep their fanbase engaged.

If Cousins hits a rough patch—as he very well could in September or October—the pressure to turn to Mendoza could become difficult to resist.

The schedule is daunting between Weeks 2 and 7 anyway, which is why I'm targeting the team's Nov. 1 Week 8 matchup with the soft Jets for Mendoza's debut as a starter.

That's if they can even hold off that long.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Explains Heated Exchanges With Raiders' Maxx Crosby and Texans, 'Don't Touch My Arm'
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins was not pleased near the end of his team's joint practice with the Houston Texans on Tuesday, and he explained why during a chat with reporters afterward.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins was not pleased near the end of his team's joint practice with the Houston Texans on Tuesday, and he explained why during a chat with reporters afterward.

"My elbow got hit," Cousins said, per Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal . "I joke with [Raiders star defensive end Maxx Crosby], and I say, 'You can touch me anywhere you want, just don't touch my arm.' You want to bump me in the ribs? Fine. I think if anything, hitting me in the hips or the ribs is actually good because it simulates what I need to feel."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Cousins and Crosby got into it at the Raiders' Aug. 7 practice. Per ESPN's Ryan McFadden , Crosby hit Cousins twice during a team period.

Sam Warren of The Athletic provided more insight.

The two players were held out of the following day's practices due to their actions, per head coach Klint Kubiak to reporters .

"We have very clear expectations on how we want to practice and how we want to go about our business and we violated that yesterday, so held those guys out. That's all I'm gonna say about it," Kubiak said.

Fast-forward to this week, and it appears that Cousins simply doesn't want to get hit on the arm. That's understandable with him being a quarterback, of course.

The 38-year-old Cousins is in town on a one-year, $11.3 million contract, per Over the Cap . The four-time Pro Bowler is essentially serving as the veteran bridge quarterback as Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, waits in the wings.

Kubiak told reporters after the Raiders' 27-14 preseason-opening loss to the Arizona Cardinals regarding Cousins that the QB1 job is "his to lose." So at this juncture, the expectation is he'll be leading the Silver and Black when they open the season on Sunday, Sept. 13 at home vs. the Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: Pat McAfee Joins ESPN's 'Monday Night Countdown,' Jason Kelce to Be Analyst for NFL Network Games
articles.summary: ESPN has announced its Sunday and Monday NFL coverage for the 2026 season, which will culminate with the network airing the Super Bowl for the first time in its history.
articles.body:
ESPN has announced its Sunday and Monday NFL coverage for the 2026 season, which will culminate with the network airing the Super Bowl for the first time in its history.

Of note, Pat McAfee is joining ESPN's Monday Night Countdown team for the 2026 season. He and Jason McCourty are the new additions to the desk, which will also consist of host Scott Van Pelt and analysts Jason Kelce and Marcus Spears.

McAfee will make his regular season debut on Monday, Sept. 14 in Kansas City, where the Chiefs will host the Broncos in a pivotal AFC West matchup.

McAfee will continue his other roles at ESPN, including host of The Pat McAfee Show and analyst on College GameDay .

In addition, Kelce will be serving as a commentator for a few games airing on NFL Network. Play-by-play commentator Dave Pasch will call the shots, and Kurt Warner will be a commentator as well.

That trio will call four games: two in London (the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders on Oct. 4 and the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars on Oct. 11) and one in Paris (the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints on Oct. 25). Their final game will be a to-be-determined Week 16 matchup that will be part of NFL Network's Dec. 26 doubleheader.

This is a big year for ESPN's NFL coverage with the addition of the Super Bowl, which will take place in Los Angeles' SoFI Stadium.

The game will be nationally televised on ESPN and ABC on Sunday, Feb. 14.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase, Derrick Henry Named to NFL Top 100, Check Out the Updated 2026 Rankings
articles.summary: The NFL Top 100 is hitting the homestretch with Cincinnati Bengals star Ja'Marr Chase and Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry entering the fray.
articles.body:
The NFL Top 100 is hitting the homestretch with Cincinnati Bengals star Ja'Marr Chase and Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry entering the fray.

Chase was revealed as the No. 16 player on the list, marking his second consecutive year making it into the top 20.

Henry is on the list for the eighth consecutive year, coming in at No. 15 overall in 2026.

Here is the updated top 100 with 86 players having been revealed:

100. New Orleans Saints DE Cameron Jordan

99. Indianapolis Colts OG Quenton Nelson

96. New Orleans Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr.

93. Cleveland Browns LB Carson Schwesinger

87. Carolina Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan

86. Los Angeles Chargers LB Tuli Tuipulotu

77. Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield

62. Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence

52. Tampa Bay Buccaneers OT Tristan Wirfs

50. Los Angeles Chargers S Derwin James Jr.

48. Jacksonville Jaguars DE Josh Hines-Allen

47. Philadelphia Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell

46. San Francisco 49ers TE George Kittle

40. San Francisco 49ers OT Trent Williams

39. Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert

38. Philadelphia Eagles CB Cooper DeJean

34. Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley

28. New England Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez

25. Houston Texans CB Derek Stingley Jr.

19. Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson

18. Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes

17. Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor

Chase has made the Top 100 every year since 2022, when he was coming off a rookie season in which he racked up 1,455 yards and 13 touchdowns to help the Bengals reach the Super Bowl.

Last year marked the high point for Chase on the list thus far at No. 4 overall. Despite slipping 12 spots going into 2026, he remains as good as any receiver in the NFL.

Chase finished 2025 with 125 receptions, 1,412 yards and eight touchdowns. It was his third consecutive season with at least 140 targets, 100 catches and 1,200 yards.

Since entering the NFL, Chase ranks second among all wide receivers in receptions, yards and touchdowns. The Bengals have scored at least 400 points in four of those five seasons.

Prior to the pairing of Chase and Joe Burrow, the Bengals had a total of five seasons with at least 400 points in their franchise history dating back to 1968.

Despite playing a position known for having a short shelf life in the NFL, Henry remains an extreme outlier. He finished the 2025 campaign with 1,595 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns in his age-31 season.

Only two players in NFL history have had more rushing yards in their age-31 season than Henry did. The five-time Pro Bowler has racked up 3,516 yards in two seasons with Baltimore after leaving the Tennessee Titans.

Looking ahead to 2026, the NFL record for most rushing yards by a player in their age-32 season is 1,333 set by Walter Payton in 1986. Henry has surpassed that total three times in the last four years.

Henry was one of three running backs last season with more than 1,000 yards after contact, along with Jonathan Taylor and Bijan Robinson.

There is a lot of intrigue around the Ravens for the upcoming season primarily due to the change in head coach with Jesse Minter replacing John Harbaugh, but the bones of what has made them successful remain in place.

Henry figures to be a huge part of the offense yet again until either he starts slowing down due to age or opposing defenses finally figure out a way to stop him.

articles.title: Patriots' Milton Williams Jokingly Flips Off Former Eagles Teammates on Video at NFL Joint Practice
articles.summary: New England Patriots defensive lineman Milton Williams jokingly greeted his old Philadelphia Eagles teammates with a middle finger upon seeing them in Foxborough, Massachusetts for the beginning of a two-day joint practice.
articles.body:
New England Patriots defensive lineman Milton Williams jokingly greeted his old Philadelphia Eagles teammates with a middle finger upon seeing them in Foxborough, Massachusetts for the beginning of a two-day joint practice.

It was very clear Williams was just messing around.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Williams spent his first four NFL seasons with the Eagles before leaving in free agency for the Pats last offseason for a four-year, $104 million deal ($51 million fully guaranteed).

He helped the Pats enjoy an incredible one-season turnaround, as New England went from 4-13 in 2024 to 14-3 and AFC champions in 2025.

Williams will be seeing his old Eagle friends a lot this week, with the two teams also playing a preseason game on Saturday at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET. The two teams will not play in the regular season.

articles.title: Texans' Jayden Higgins Reportedly Suffers Major Knee Injury in Joint Practice vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Houston Texans wide receiver Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL in Tuesday's joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders, according to ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Houston Texans wide receiver Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL in Tuesday's joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders, according to ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Higgins, a second-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft, caught 41 passes for 525 yards and six touchdowns as a rookie.

He figured to have a fairly sizable role in the passing game for the season ahead.

Nico Collins, who's coming off his third straight 1,000-yard campaign, will be the No. 1 target, but Higgins was likely to be the first option for quarterback C.J. Stroud when Collins is covered.

Tank Dell is a major question mark after missing all of 2025 because of significant knee injuries, while Jaylin Noel is dealing with a hamstring issue.

Now, the Texans will have to forge ahead without Higgins for the entire year.

This is going to put a lot of importance on Dell staying healthy and returning to the form he enjoyed in 2023 and 2024, when he had 1,376 receiving yards in 25 appearances.

Somebody else will need to step up as well, whether it's Noel, Xavier Hutchinson or sixth-round draft pick Lewis Bond.

Stroud is approaching what could be a pivotal season. The Texans have picked up his fifth-year option, and a big 2026 could net him a sizable pay raise. Higgins' injury represents a small blow to those hopes before a down has been played.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley Resurgence Predicted by Lane Johnson in 1st Year Under New Eagles OC Sean Mannion
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Lane Johnson told reporters on Wednesday that he believes running back Saquon Barkley is in line for a season like 2024, when the eight-year veteran earned Associated Press Offensive Player of the Year honors.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Lane Johnson told reporters on Wednesday that he believes running back Saquon Barkley is in line for a season like 2024, when the eight-year veteran earned Associated Press Offensive Player of the Year honors.

Barkley amassed an NFL-high 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024. He also had a career-high 6.0 yards per touch.

In addition, the former Penn State star rushed for 2,005 yards, becoming just the ninth player in NFL history to accomplish the feat in a single season.

However, the 2025 season represented a significant downturn. Barkley went from running for 5.8 yards per carry in 2024 to 4.1 YPC in 2025. His yards per touch went down to 4.5. Overall, he gained 1,413 total yards and scored nine touchdowns.

Philadelphia has undergone major offensive changes since then, parting ways with offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, who took over for OC Kellen Moore in Feb. 2025 after he took the New Orleans Saints' head coaching gig.

Former NFL quarterback Sean Mannion, who was the Green Bay Packers' QB coach last year, has taken over at OC.

He's clearly made a great impression on Eagle players so far, including Johnson and fellow offensive tackle Jordan Mailata.

"Sean is an evil genius. That is my first impression," Mailata said back in June, per ESPN's Tim McManus . "The guy knows ball. If I were to lock the three smartest people in the facility in one room, Sean would be there. And I think Sean would just be by himself. It would just be Sean. He's a wizard. And man, I'm super excited. As the year goes on, we get to display what is in that beautiful mind of his."

McManus gave a glimpse of what Mannion's offense looks like via his training camp observations.

"Jalen Hurts is under center way more," McManus wrote on Aug. 11. "There is motion on almost every play. They are leaning heavily into play-action. And they've implemented a wide-zone blocking scheme, departing from the more vertical attack orchestrated by former offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland."

That could certainly lead to more running room for Barkley. We'll see how Mannion's scheme works soon enough when the Eagles begin the season on Sunday, Sept. 13 at home versus the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Trevon Diggs, Seahawks Contract Details Revealed in New NFL Rumors, Updated Salary Cap
articles.summary: Former Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers cornerback Trevon Diggs is set to get a fresh start in 2026 with the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers cornerback Trevon Diggs is set to get a fresh start in 2026 with the Seattle Seahawks.

Diggs has agreed to a one-year deal with the Seahawks in free agency, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

The Seahawks had $20.6 million in 2026 cap space remaining at the time of the deal, per Spotrac .

The cornerback spent most of the 2025 season with the Cowboys, where he recorded 25 tackles in eight games and six starts before he was placed on injured reserve due to a concussion and knee injury.

Diggs was then activated from IR shortly before he was released by the Cowboys ahead of Week 18.

NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reported at the time Diggs' cut was "the culmination of multiple factors spread over time, including both performance and other elements."

The Cowboys had penalized Diggs ahead of the season with a $500,000 reduction in salary for reported lack of participation in the team's offseason program.

Diggs was claimed off waivers by the Packers in Week 18, playing 34 combined snaps in one regular-season game and the team's Wild Card loss to the Chicago Bears before he was released again.

The cornerback had three years and $57 million in non-guaranteed money remaining on his deal at the time. That move allowed the Packers to free $15.5 million in cap space without taking on any dead cap, per Spotrac .

The Cowboys paid out $5.8 million in dead money from their December decision to waive Diggs.

Diggs established himself as one of the NFL's top cornerbacks with back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons in 2021 and 2022, including an 11-interception campaign in 2021.

His career was derailed by a torn left ACL that held him to just two games in 2023.

Diggs has been limited to 11 games or fewer in two seasons since, and he struggled to limit passing opportunities in coverage in 2025.

The Seahawks will now take a chance on bringing in the 27-year-old in the hope he can bounce back with a healthier campaign in 2026.

articles.title: New DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr. Injury Update on Status for Steelers vs. Falcons Week 1
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receivers DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. both expect to play in the team's opener, according to PennLive's Nick Farabaugh.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receivers DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. both expect to play in the team's opener, according to PennLive's Nick Farabaugh.

Metcalf is dealing with an undisclosed injury, while Pittman is battling a hamstring issue. Neither believes he'll be on the sideline when Pittsburgh hosts the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Metcalf is coming off his worst statistical season, which wasn't what the Steelers envisioned after signing him to a big extension . He caught 59 passes for 850 yards and six touchdowns.

Pittman likewise didn't have a great 2025, finishing with 80 receptions, 784 yards and seven scores. In his case, he had a dip toward the end that coincided with the Indianapolis Colts starting Philip Rivers and Riley Leonard at quarterback.

Pittsburgh needs Metcalf and Pittman to deliver because it's hard to imagine how a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers will be dramatically better in 2026. His 207.6 passing yards per game were his fewest over a full season, and now he's a year older.

If the Steelers' two best wideouts perform up to their best, the passing game might collectively be where it needs for the team to contend for another AFC North title.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Creative Team Names to Bring Excitement to Your League
articles.summary: What's in a name?
articles.body:
Well, for fantasy football managers, maybe everything.

It is, after all, the first impression presented to your league mates. Before they see your roster or the fruits of all of your pre-draft labor, they'll see which team name you selected and what approach you went with it (all business, all funny, team- or player-specific, etc.).

So, while you surely have lots to figure out between now and the start of the 2026 NFL season, let's see if we can get enough creative juices flowing here to lock this decision down and take one item off of your pre-draft plate.

There are countless ways to go if you prefer some punny play on a pop culture reference or star player name. And we will provide lists for both options if you want to go that route.

But maybe you want something a little less generic and a little more you . The type of team name that you can carry along from year to year and never have to worry about a reference going stale.

Now, it's hard to give specific examples, since we're not actually acquainted, and I have no clue on your specifics. As general guides, though, maybe you're known among friends as a grillmaster, so Tight Ends & Burnt Ends might work. Or you're the tech expert of your group, so you lean into that with Ctrl+Alt+Defeat.

You can craft this however you like, but it does give a more personal touch than trying to make the same jokes as everyone else.

articles.title: Jordan Love Talks Packers Mindset for 2026 NFL Season After Playoff Loss to Caleb Williams, Bears
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love revealed that the team is using its Wild Card playoff loss to Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears as fuel heading into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love revealed that the team is using its Wild Card playoff loss to Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears as fuel heading into the 2026 season.

"Definitely a chip. Like you mentioned, just the way we ended the season losing a lot of our last games, obviously the playoff loss, it just leaves a sour taste in your mouth," Love said during a Wednesday appearance on the Rich Eisen Show (13:45 mark). "So I think the mindset for us, going back to OTAs and obviously the start of training camp, is finish. Every day we've gotta find ways to be at our best. As practice goes on and the days get longer and longer, you've gotta find ways to improve and still be at your best and still lock in with the mindset of finishing the day."

The Packers opened their 2025 campaign with a 9-3-1 record, but ended the regular season on a four-game losing streak.

They eventually suffered a 31-27 loss at the hands of Chicago in the playoffs, as Green Bay was unable to maintain a 21-3 lead at halftime and fell to its NFC North rival.

It's worth noting that the Packers' disappointing finish to the year occurred without Micah Parsons, as the star pass-rusher suffered a torn ACL in Week 15.

Now, Love is looking to help lead Green Bay on a deeper playoff run in his fourth season as a full-time starter under center.

In 15 appearances last year, he completed 66.3 percent of his throws for 3,381 yards and 23 touchdowns compared to six interceptions. Love's 72.7 QBR ranked No. 3 among 28 qualified quarterbacks, via ESPN .

The Packers will begin the 2026 season against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 13.
