articles.title: Buying or Selling Fantasy Football's Most Polarizing Players in 2026
articles.summary: Few things energize the fantasy football community more than a good draft-season debate.
articles.body:
Few things energize the fantasy football community more than a good draft-season debate.

Sure, we agree about a few players. Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs and Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson are pretty good. So are Ja'Marr Chase of the Cincinnati Bengals, Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams and Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks at wide receiver.

But that's about it. Five picks in, the disagreements begin.

Fantasy debates inevitably produce differing evaluations. Supporters will be proved right on some polarizing players, while skeptics will be proved right on others. The question is which side has the stronger case for each player.

Here's a closer look at which side of each debate offers the stronger fantasy case.

The first two NFL seasons for Caleb Williams have been something of a roller coaster. But over the second half of last season, the first overall pick in the 2024 draft turned it on.

The 24-year-old averaged over 20 fantasy points per game from Week 9 on and was a top-five fantasy quarterback over that span.

However, despite that hot finish, Williams is coming off draft boards right around where he finished for the season in 2025.

For Eric Patterson of The Score , the skepticism with Williams is borne of inconsistency—and a rough schedule late in the season:

"What's most concerning about Williams is his boom-or-bust style. Last year, the Bears gunslinger had two weeks as the QB1 but also logged eight weeks as the QB15 or worse. Add in the fact that Chicago's fantasy playoff schedule includes three outdoor games (at Buffalo, versus Green Bay, versus Detroit) and Williams could do more to hurt than help your fantasy team's title chances."

There's also a lot to like about Williams this year, though. He's entering his second year in Ben Johnson's offense—a scheme that has perennially produced big-time numbers under center.

There's no shortage of weapons available to him in the passing game. Per Gordon McGuinness of PFF , the Bears have a top-five offensive line. Williams also added almost 400 yards on the ground last year.

Fun fact: In 106 seasons, the Bears have never had a 4,000-yard passer. That longest of dry spells will end this year.

And Williams' ADP is much closer to his fantasy floor than his ceiling.

There is zero question that when Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is on top of his game, he's an elite fantasy option—and then some.

In his first MVP campaign back in 2019, he rushed for a ridiculous 1,206 yards, led the league with 36 touchdown passes and was the highest-scoring fantasy signal-caller by a wide margin.

As recently as two years ago, the 29-year-old threw for almost 4,200 yards and 41 touchdowns, rushed for over 900 yards and again led all fantasy quarterbacks by a sizable amount.

The ceiling is sky-high with Jackson. The problem is that in recent years, the floor has also become lower. In three of the last five seasons, he has missed at least four games.

There's also the matter of those gaudy rushing numbers—or more appropriately the lack of them. Sure, injuries played a part, but last year Jackson averaged just 26.8 yards per game on the ground.

Per BJ Rudell of Touchdown Wire , over the first four seasons of his career, between 37 percent and 43 percent of Jackson's total fantasy points came on the ground. Even in that outstanding 2024 season, that percentage fell to 27 percent. Last year it cratered—rushing accounted for just 22 percent of his fantasy production.

Jackson will be 30 in January, and he's no good to a Ravens team with Super Bowl aspirations if he gets hurt. This isn't to say he won't still run, but his days of 1,000-yard seasons on the ground may be over.

And the more Jackson has to rely purely on passing numbers for fantasy points, the less likely it is he'll be able to live up to his lofty asking price.

In each of the last three seasons, Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams has eclipsed 1,100 rushing yards. He has scored double-digit rushing touchdowns. And he has finished as a top-10 running back in PPR points.

In 2026, though, he is barely being drafted inside the top 15 at his position, and some pundits believe he's overvalued in that spot.

The reason is workload. After playing sparingly as a rookie in 2024, Blake Corum had over 150 carries in 2025. He made the most of those carries, averaging 5.1 yards per carry. He had double-digit carries in four of the last five regular-season games last year.

But while Williams' workload fell by 57 carries last year, as Derek Brown wrote at Fantasy Pros , he made up for the lack of quantity with increased quality:

"Williams had to deal with more work for Blake Corum last year, but he still retained his lead role overall and in the red zone. In Weeks 7-18, Williams still saw 63% of the red zone rushing attempts while Corum helped him with the heavy lifting on early downs in between the 20s. With the workload lightened a tad, Williams did post improved rushing efficiency metrics, ranking 21st in explosive run rate, 25th in missed tackle rate, and 18th in yards after contact per attempt (per Fantasy Points Data)."

Williams actually posted more total yards in 2025 (1,533) than he did the previous season. Even if Corum assumes a larger share of the early-down workload, Williams should retain the high-value touches that have supported his fantasy production and remains a strong bet to finish among the top 10 running backs.

Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane had himself a year in 2025—the third-year pro led the NFL at 5.7 yards per carry, topped 1,800 total yards and finished fifth in PPR points among running backs.

Achane topped 300 touches for the season for the first time in 2025, and while appearing on The Rich Eisen Show new Miami head coach Jeff Hafley said Achane will be a busy back again in 2026:

"I just gave Achane a heads-up this morning and I told him you better be in good shape. I told him there might be some games when I have to pick him up and carry him back to the locker room because he's going to be so tired. I told him I don't ever want to see one of these head taps all year, and he looked me right in the eye and he said, 'You'll never get that head tap from me.' I said, 'Don't worry buddy. After you touch the ball 40-45 times, I might have to pick you up and carry you back into the locker room.'"

Hafley was joking, but Miami's limited supporting cast could again make Achane the focal point of its offense.

The problems with that are twofold. First, Achane is not built like Derrick Henry—he's a 5'9", 191-pound back. Second, if Miami struggles to remain competitive in 2026, positive game scripts could be limited, potentially reducing Achane's rushing volume.

Achane could outplay his asking price in 2026, but the downside risk may be even greater given his workload, smaller frame and Miami's likely game-script limitations.

Despite sharing the Philadelphia Eagles' passing game with A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith has shown he can be a productive fantasy asset. He has topped 1,000 receiving yards in three of his five seasons, including in 2025.

Now, Brown has been traded to the New England Patriots. But despite going from being Robin to Batman in the Eagles passing attack, many fantasy analysts are reluctant to predict a big spike in production from Smith in 2026.

However, as Adam Pfeifer pointed out at A Fantasy Life , when Smith has been the alpha wideout in Philadelphia, the target numbers and production have been encouraging:

"Over the last three years, Smith has been sporting a 28% TPRR (targets per route run) with Brown off the field, which would easily be his highest TPRR rate over an entire season. Meanwhile, in five games with Brown sidelined since 2022, Smith's averages are, as you'd expect, strong—9.0 targets, 6.2 receptions, 87.8 receiving yards, 16.2 PPR PPG and a 31.4% TPRR."

Pfeifer went so far as to call Smith this year's Jaxon Smith-Njigba—a wide receiver who is going to absolutely demolish his ADP. That may be stretching things a little, but in 2022 Smith turned 136 targets into a 95/1,196/7 stat line and a WR9 finish in PPR points. That 16.2 PPR points per game Smith averaged with Brown out the past few years would have ranked inside the top-five at the position in 2025.

Smith being available halfway through Round 3 makes it a lot more palatable to attack the running back position early in drafts this summer.

Last season, Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins caught 71 passes for 1,117 yards and six touchdowns—his third straight season with over 1,000 receiving yards.

The 27-year-old was a top-12 wide receiver in terms of PPR points per game, and told reporters that he expects the Texans offense to rebound in 2026 after a shaky end to last season:

"We're getting better every single day. We're going against the number one defense in the league. This is what you want to compete against every single day in the heat when you're hot and tired. Your legs are burning and they're blitzing; that's when you want to be your best. I feel like as an offense right now, we're humming. We're continuing to put the pieces together and continuing to build every single day."

Quite a few fantasy drafters expect a career year from Collins, especially after Jayden Higgins was lost to a season-ending ACL tear.

For everyone who thinks Collins can finish in the top five, though, there's someone else who believes he will finish outside the top 12. Put me in the latter group.

The two-time Pro Bowler's talent is not in question. However, durability remains a concern: He has missed multiple games in each of his five NFL seasons. His per-game production and advanced metrics declined across the board in 2025, while C.J. Stroud's production has regressed in each of the past two years.

Stroud has also yet to throw 25 touchdown passes in a season, creating legitimate questions about whether Collins has the quarterback play necessary to reach a truly elite fantasy ceiling.

At his current ADP, the path to a top-five finish is narrower than many drafters appear to believe.

For years, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce stood alone as fantasy football's gold standard at tight end and was a legitimate first-round pick.

However, the king's reign is over. In 2026, the 37-year-old is barely being selected in the top 10 at his position—and many believe that's too high a price to pay.

Kelce told reporters he's eager to show he still has something left in the tank after a 2025 campaign where he averaged a career-low 50.1 receiving yards per contest:

"I've still got a lot of love for this game. I still think I can go out and play at a high level, and I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year. I think that's probably the biggest thing for me is making sure that I'm accountable for the guys in this room every single play that I'm out there."

Kelce may not be the player he once was, but that doesn't mean he can't still be productive for fantasy drafters. For all he didn't do in 2025, he was third in PPR points among tight ends. The last time he wasn't a top-five fantasy option was in 2015. That was also the last time he didn't log 100 targets in a season.

Kelce is no longer at his peak, but he remains capable of providing top-five production at the position.

Despite his TE6 asking price, Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta has a less convincing fantasy case than many drafters appear to believe.

Austin Swaim of SI is among those bullish on the 25-year-old in 2026, citing new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's use of multiple-tight-end personnel packages in Arizona last season:

"Petzing's 10.5% usage rate of 13 personnel (or 3 tight ends) was nearly double the league average last year, and he targeted wide receivers at just a 45.0% rate last year -- also well below the league average (60.0%). Some might say, 'that's Trey McBride.' But, this is also LaPorta, a former top-40 pick who posted 889 receiving yards as a rookie to finish as the TE1 in fantasy football. His 2025 was derailed by injuries as he missed 8 games."

Petzing has favored heavier personnel packages, although that approach has become increasingly common across the league. Even so, drafting LaPorta at his current cost requires projecting a substantial rebound in volume and touchdown production.

LaPorta's rookie season remains an outlier. He ranked fifth among tight ends with 120 targets and scored 10 touchdowns that year; across the two seasons since, he has totaled 132 targets and 10 touchdowns.

Yes, the Lions have a prolific offense, but he's the No. 3 option at best in the Detroit passing attack. The target share just isn't going to be high enough to justify this draft-day cost.

Fantasy drafters often overvalue tight ends in this tier when projecting role changes.

As recently as two years ago, the 29-year-old threw for almost 4,200 yards and 41 touchdowns, rushed for over 900 yards and again led all fantasy quarterbacks by a sizable amount.
The ceiling is sky-high with Jackson. The problem is that in recent years, the floor has also become lower. In three of the last five seasons, he has missed at least four games.
There's also the matter of those gaudy rushing numbers—or more appropriately the lack of them. Sure, injuries played a part, but last year Jackson averaged just 26.8 yards per game on the ground.

Per BJ Rudell of Touchdown Wire , over the first four seasons of his career, between 37 percent and 43 percent of Jackson's total fantasy points came on the ground. Even in that outstanding 2024 season, that percentage fell to 27 percent. Last year it cratered—rushing accounted for just 22 percent of his fantasy production.

Jackson will be 30 in January, and he's no good to a Ravens team with Super Bowl aspirations if he gets hurt. This isn't to say he won't still run, but his days of 1,000-yard seasons on the ground may be over.
And the more Jackson has to rely purely on passing numbers for fantasy points, the less likely it is he'll be able to live up to his lofty asking price.

In each of the last three seasons, Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams has eclipsed 1,100 rushing yards. He has scored double-digit rushing touchdowns. And he has finished as a top-10 running back in PPR points.
In 2026, though, he is barely being drafted inside the top 15 at his position, and some pundits believe he's overvalued in that spot.

The reason is workload. After playing sparingly as a rookie in 2024, Blake Corum had over 150 carries in 2025. He made the most of those carries, averaging 5.1 yards per carry. He had double-digit carries in four of the last five regular-season games last year.
But while Williams' workload fell by 57 carries last year, as Derek Brown wrote at Fantasy Pros , he made up for the lack of quantity with increased quality:

"Williams had to deal with more work for Blake Corum last year, but he still retained his lead role overall and in the red zone. In Weeks 7-18, Williams still saw 63% of the red zone rushing attempts while Corum helped him with the heavy lifting on early downs in between the 20s. With the workload lightened a tad, Williams did post improved rushing efficiency metrics, ranking 21st in explosive run rate, 25th in missed tackle rate, and 18th in yards after contact per attempt (per Fantasy Points Data)."

Williams actually posted more total yards in 2025 (1,533) than he did the previous season. Even if Corum assumes a larger share of the early-down workload, Williams should retain the high-value touches that have supported his fantasy production and remains a strong bet to finish among the top 10 running backs.

Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane had himself a year in 2025—the third-year pro led the NFL at 5.7 yards per carry, topped 1,800 total yards and finished fifth in PPR points among running backs.
Achane topped 300 touches for the season for the first time in 2025, and while appearing on The Rich Eisen Show new Miami head coach Jeff Hafley said Achane will be a busy back again in 2026:

"I just gave Achane a heads-up this morning and I told him you better be in good shape. I told him there might be some games when I have to pick him up and carry him back to the locker room because he's going to be so tired. I told him I don't ever want to see one of these head taps all year, and he looked me right in the eye and he said, 'You'll never get that head tap from me.' I said, 'Don't worry buddy. After you touch the ball 40-45 times, I might have to pick you up and carry you back into the locker room.'"
Hafley was joking, but Miami's limited supporting cast could again make Achane the focal point of its offense.

The problems with that are twofold. First, Achane is not built like Derrick Henry—he's a 5'9", 191-pound back. Second, if Miami struggles to remain competitive in 2026, positive game scripts could be limited, potentially reducing Achane's rushing volume.
Achane could outplay his asking price in 2026, but the downside risk may be even greater given his workload, smaller frame and Miami's likely game-script limitations.

Despite sharing the Philadelphia Eagles' passing game with A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith has shown he can be a productive fantasy asset. He has topped 1,000 receiving yards in three of his five seasons, including in 2025.

Now, Brown has been traded to the New England Patriots. But despite going from being Robin to Batman in the Eagles passing attack, many fantasy analysts are reluctant to predict a big spike in production from Smith in 2026.
However, as Adam Pfeifer pointed out at A Fantasy Life , when Smith has been the alpha wideout in Philadelphia, the target numbers and production have been encouraging:

"Over the last three years, Smith has been sporting a 28% TPRR (targets per route run) with Brown off the field, which would easily be his highest TPRR rate over an entire season. Meanwhile, in five games with Brown sidelined since 2022, Smith's averages are, as you'd expect, strong—9.0 targets, 6.2 receptions, 87.8 receiving yards, 16.2 PPR PPG and a 31.4% TPRR."

Pfeifer went so far as to call Smith this year's Jaxon Smith-Njigba—a wide receiver who is going to absolutely demolish his ADP. That may be stretching things a little, but in 2022 Smith turned 136 targets into a 95/1,196/7 stat line and a WR9 finish in PPR points. That 16.2 PPR points per game Smith averaged with Brown out the past few years would have ranked inside the top-five at the position in 2025.
Smith being available halfway through Round 3 makes it a lot more palatable to attack the running back position early in drafts this summer.
Last season, Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins caught 71 passes for 1,117 yards and six touchdowns—his third straight season with over 1,000 receiving yards.
The 27-year-old was a top-12 wide receiver in terms of PPR points per game, and told reporters that he expects the Texans offense to rebound in 2026 after a shaky end to last season:

"We're getting better every single day. We're going against the number one defense in the league. This is what you want to compete against every single day in the heat when you're hot and tired. Your legs are burning and they're blitzing; that's when you want to be your best. I feel like as an offense right now, we're humming. We're continuing to put the pieces together and continuing to build every single day."
Quite a few fantasy drafters expect a career year from Collins, especially after Jayden Higgins was lost to a season-ending ACL tear.
For everyone who thinks Collins can finish in the top five, though, there's someone else who believes he will finish outside the top 12. Put me in the latter group.

The two-time Pro Bowler's talent is not in question. However, durability remains a concern: He has missed multiple games in each of his five NFL seasons. His per-game production and advanced metrics declined across the board in 2025, while C.J. Stroud's production has regressed in each of the past two years.
Stroud has also yet to throw 25 touchdown passes in a season, creating legitimate questions about whether Collins has the quarterback play necessary to reach a truly elite fantasy ceiling.
At his current ADP, the path to a top-five finish is narrower than many drafters appear to believe.
For years, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce stood alone as fantasy football's gold standard at tight end and was a legitimate first-round pick.
However, the king's reign is over. In 2026, the 37-year-old is barely being selected in the top 10 at his position—and many believe that's too high a price to pay.
Kelce told reporters he's eager to show he still has something left in the tank after a 2025 campaign where he averaged a career-low 50.1 receiving yards per contest:

"I've still got a lot of love for this game. I still think I can go out and play at a high level, and I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year. I think that's probably the biggest thing for me is making sure that I'm accountable for the guys in this room every single play that I'm out there."

Kelce may not be the player he once was, but that doesn't mean he can't still be productive for fantasy drafters. For all he didn't do in 2025, he was third in PPR points among tight ends. The last time he wasn't a top-five fantasy option was in 2015. That was also the last time he didn't log 100 targets in a season.
Kelce is no longer at his peak, but he remains capable of providing top-five production at the position.
Despite his TE6 asking price, Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta has a less convincing fantasy case than many drafters appear to believe.
Austin Swaim of SI is among those bullish on the 25-year-old in 2026, citing new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's use of multiple-tight-end personnel packages in Arizona last season:

"Petzing's 10.5% usage rate of 13 personnel (or 3 tight ends) was nearly double the league average last year, and he targeted wide receivers at just a 45.0% rate last year -- also well below the league average (60.0%). Some might say, 'that's Trey McBride.' But, this is also LaPorta, a former top-40 pick who posted 889 receiving yards as a rookie to finish as the TE1 in fantasy football. His 2025 was derailed by injuries as he missed 8 games."

Petzing has favored heavier personnel packages, although that approach has become increasingly common across the league. Even so, drafting LaPorta at his current cost requires projecting a substantial rebound in volume and touchdown production.

LaPorta's rookie season remains an outlier. He ranked fifth among tight ends with 120 targets and scored 10 touchdowns that year; across the two seasons since, he has totaled 132 targets and 10 touchdowns.
Yes, the Lions have a prolific offense, but he's the No. 3 option at best in the Detroit passing attack. The target share just isn't going to be high enough to justify this draft-day cost.
Fantasy drafters often overvalue tight ends in this tier when projecting role changes.

articles.title: Dan Campbell Says Lions' Super Bowl Window 'Is Not Closed' After Disappointing 2025 Season
articles.summary: Coming off their worst season since 2022, the Detroit Lions are looking to rebound despite playing in arguably the deepest division in the NFL.
articles.body:
Coming off their worst season since 2022, the Detroit Lions are looking to rebound despite playing in arguably the deepest division in the NFL.

Even with some questions and roster turnover on the heels of a 9-8 record in 2025, head coach Dan Campbell told ESPN's Eric Woodyard he's confident the Lions' Super Bowl window "is not closed" going into the 2026 campaign:

"Our window is not closed. It's not closed. That was the whole reason why we did this. We fell short last year. But needed to get in [the playoffs], and now it's about the matchups, where you're playing and who you're playing. We want to be able to do that every year, and sometimes, I'm just saying is what happens is, you want to go all-in for one player, well how do you know that one player doesn't get hurt?

"Or how do you know the three players behind him don't get hurt and now you've got no depth. Whereas, let's just get a unit together that we feel like can compete every year and then it's about in that moment, we're making those plays and finding a way to win that game."

The "this" Campbell is referring to is sticking with a lot of the homegrown nucleus that has made the Lions successful in recent years. In particular, giving Jahmyr Gibbs and Jack Campbell long-term extensions.

Detroit now has nine players making at least $20 million annually. Spending at that level does complicate building depth on the roster, which is part of why players like David Montgomery, Alex Anzalone and Taylor Decker are no longer on the roster.

The Lions led the NFL with 27 wins over the 2023 and 2024 seasons, but they fell back to earth last season with nine victories. They did extend their streak of consecutive winning seasons to four, but missed the playoffs due in part to a 2-4 divisional record.

The NFC North was the only division to have all four teams finish over .500, marking just the second time that has happened since the NFL went to the current eight-division format in 2002.

If there's a reason for Campbell to remain optimistic, it's because the bulk of the Lions' offensive core that scored the fourth-most points in the NFL last season remains intact.

The biggest area for the Lions to improve is defense after finishing 22nd in points allowed. The schedule does line up favorably for them to start fast with just one game against a team that had a winning record last season (at Buffalo Bills in Week 2) in the first five weeks before their bye in Week 6.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson's Stance on Ravens' Offense Under Declan Doyle Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: An offseason of change for the Baltimore Ravens involved Lamar Jackson partnering with his fourth different offensive coordinator since becoming the full-time starting quarterback midway through his rookie year in 2018.
articles.body:
An offseason of change for the Baltimore Ravens involved Lamar Jackson partnering with his fourth different offensive coordinator since becoming the full-time starting quarterback midway through his rookie year in 2018.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano , the addition of Declan Doyle as Baltimore's new offensive play-caller has been met with enthusiasm by Jackson throughout the offseason and training camp.

"Jackson, according to multiple sources, has been all-in this offseason, showing an enthusiasm for Doyle's offense and what he can do in it," Graziano wrote.

The hiring of Doyle came after the Ravens replaced John Harbaugh as head coach with Jesse Minter, who previously worked on Harbaugh's staff from 2017 to '20.

This marks Doyle's second season as an offensive coordinator, but his first time as the primary play-caller. He had the title last year with the Chicago Bears, though head coach Ben Johnson held play-calling responsibilities.

Doyle, who turned 30 on March 6, comes from a great coaching tree with experience under Sean Payton and Johnson.

Per ESPN's Ben Solak , some of the difficulties that emerge from the Payton and Johnson systems are the wordiness of the play calls, as well as "long chapters of personnel groupings and on-field adjustments."

There could be a period of adjustment for Jackson in this system, much like there was early last season for Caleb Williams working with Johnson before they finally put the pieces together to help the Chicago Bears win the NFC North.

Jackson's ceiling at this point in his career is higher than Williams in 2025, so even with some potential growing pains, the Ravens should still be able to move the ball and score points.

If the Doyle-Jackson pairing hits right out of the gate, he could easily be in the discussion to win his third MVP award and the Ravens would likely be a strong Super Bowl contender.

articles.title: Raiders Seeking Funds for Allegiant Stadium Improvements, New Photo Rendering Released
articles.summary: Two years away from hosting Super Bowl 63, the Las Vegas Raiders are seeking financial assistance to make upgrades to Allegiant Stadium.
articles.body:
Two years away from hosting Super Bowl 63, the Las Vegas Raiders are seeking financial assistance to make upgrades to Allegiant Stadium.

The Las Vegas Stadium Authority is meeting on Thursday to vote on the Raiders' request for $75 million to help fund a $158 million project that would create a new "front door" to the stadium's north entrance, according to a release.

The "front door" upgrades would include a pedestrian deck, public plaza, event deck and transportation improvements.

The $75 million would come from an existing taxpayer fund allocated specifically for Allegiant Stadium-related improvements. The remaining $83 million would come from private funding.

Allegiant Stadium is tied with SoFi Stadium for the second-youngest active NFL stadium, behind only Highmark Stadium in Buffalo that is opening this year.

The Raiders' stadium opened in 2020 and cost $1.9 billion, making it the second-most expensive stadium construction project in the NFL behind SoFi.

Over the past six years, Allegiant Stadium has hosted several high-profile sporting events, including three Pac-12 Championship Games (2021-23) and Super Bowl 58 between the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers.

The NFL announced in March that Allegiant Stadium would host its second Super Bowl at the end of the 2028 season. Super Bowl 63 will take place on Feb. 11, 2029.

articles.title: Abdul Carter Told Giants He Wants to Be 'Greatest of All Time' in Team Meeting
articles.summary: New York Giants edge-rusher Abdul Carter is setting a high bar for himself on the heels of an underwhelming rookie season in the NFL.
articles.body:
New York Giants edge-rusher Abdul Carter is setting a high bar for himself on the heels of an underwhelming rookie season in the NFL.

Carter told The Athletic's Ian O'Connor he communicated to his teammates his desire to become "the greatest of all time."

"I mean the greatest of all time in terms of just a football player in general," he said.

Carter had 43 tackles, four sacks and seven tackles for loss in 2025. That's not the return a lot of people were expecting from a player widely considered to be one of the most NFL-ready in his draft class.

The arrival of coach John Harbaugh allowed Carter and others to wipe the slate clean in 2026. That's something he's clearly relishing.

"When Harbaugh first got here, everybody had to go in front of the room and speak, and I told everybody that I want to be the greatest of all time," he said to O'Connor. "And I can't just say that. I've got to come out here and work and prove it during games this season. I've got to be that player."

In order to make a big jump in Year 2, Carter will have needed to put in the time to improve during the offseason. Harbaugh told O'Connor he's "practicing at the highest level," while defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson added he's "mastering the technique and fundamentals."

There's no point in seriously entertaining any GOAT-related convos with Carter when he has so much to prove on the field. A big season will at least reassure the Giants and their fans the former Penn State star will live up to his status as a top-five pick.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Mock Draft Strategy, Dynasty and Keeper Cheat Sheet
articles.summary: Week 2 of the 2026 NFL preseason kicks off with a two-game slate Thursday night.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL preseason kicks off with a two-game slate Thursday night.

The fantasy football world is researching the cram-session portion of its pre-draft process.

Mock drafts are firing on all cylinders, rankings are being continually fine-tuned and keeper debates are nearing their decision point. It's a lot , so we're to help share that burden by identifying a couple of key mock draft strategies and finishing with our cheat sheet-style dynasty rankings.

With the sports world growing increasingly focused on efficiency, there has been a general devaluing of volume. That absolutely does not apply, though, to mock drafts.

A single mock can swing wildly toward the individual whims of the specific mock managers involved. The data, then, tells you nothing beyond the particular preferences of those people—which might be not at all applicable to your actual draft room.

So, the aim should be running multiple mocks. And honestly, it's very much a the-more-the-merrier kind of deal. The more mocks you enter, the more data you're able to cobble together and hopefully use to identify patterns and form reasonable takeaways. If you notice a particular player going significantly higher or lower than their average draft position, then that's probably useful information to apply to your draft board.

Plus, this gives you more freedom to experiment with different draft approaches. You might hammer the running position early in one and then avoid it entirely for the first several rounds in another. Even if you have a preference for a strategy going into the mock, you just might come out of it with real interest in changing how you do things.

Strategy: Try different approaches with quarterbacks

Given the wealth of advice available to fantasy managers in this digital world, it's hard to find any kind of consensus on things you should or shouldn't do during your draft. If there is a universal piece of expert advice, though, it's that you shouldn't overpay for a quarterback.

The thinking goes that the production gap between the elites at the position and the good options isn't nearly as wide as what you'd find at wide receiver or running back. So, if you were to spend a second- or third-round pick on someone like Josh Allen or Lamar Jackson, the opportunity cost would be too great to justify that investment.

That's definitely a compelling argument to be made. It's also not necessarily something you need to follow.

Maybe waiting on a quarterback has worked for you in the past. Perhaps it will treat you well again this season. But if you're always doing it—and everyone else seems to be doing it—then you don't really have a feel for how your team might look if you didn't do it. That's one of the main reasons mock drafts exist. They allow you a brief escape to do something different from your norm, and maybe you'll find that you like a roster with an elite quarterback a lot more than you think.

articles.title: Tyler Warren Injured, Latest Rumors on Colts TE's Timeline to Return Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren is reportedly not believed to be in danger of missing the team's regular-season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren is reportedly not believed to be in danger of missing the team's regular-season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Warren is expected to miss "about a week" due to a minor groin injury he suffered during training camp, but there are "no worries" about him being ready for Week 1 of the regular season.

Warren suffered the injury Wednesday during a joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons, per ESPN's Stephen Holder .

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Selected 14th overall in the 2025 NFL draft out of Penn State, Warren instantly established himself as one of the top tight ends in the league as a rookie.

Appearing in all 17 games, Warren recorded 76 receptions for 817 yards and four touchdowns, while also rushing for a touchdown.

Warren led the Colts in receiving yardage and was second in catches, and he was named to the Pro Bowl in his debut campaign.

Entering the 2026 regular season, there are some question marks surrounding the Colts' passing game, as multiple key players are coming off injuries.

Quarterback Daniel Jones' 2025 season was cut short by a torn Achilles, and No. 1 wide receiver Alec Pierce has yet to participate in training camp or the preseason after undergoing offseason ankle surgery.

The Colts signed veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen this week in a move viewed by many as an insurance policy in case Pierce is limited or isn't ready for the start of the regular season.

Until Warren is ready to return to the practice field, the starter reps at tight end during practice figure to go to Mo Alie-Cox.

The 32-year-old Alie-Cox is preparing to enter his ninth NFL season with the Colts, and he has registered 127 receptions for 1,550 yards and 16 touchdowns in 125 career regular-season games.

Quarterback Daniel Jones' 2025 season was cut short by a torn Achilles, and No. 1 wide receiver Alec Pierce has yet to participate in training camp or the preseason after undergoing offseason ankle surgery.
The Colts signed veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen this week in a move viewed by many as an insurance policy in case Pierce is limited or isn't ready for the start of the regular season.
Until Warren is ready to return to the practice field, the starter reps at tight end during practice figure to go to Mo Alie-Cox.
The 32-year-old Alie-Cox is preparing to enter his ninth NFL season with the Colts, and he has registered 127 receptions for 1,550 yards and 16 touchdowns in 125 career regular-season games.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Sleeper Tight Ends to Target and Avoid in Drafts
articles.summary: Tight end is among the trickiest positions in fantasy football, especially for managers who are unable to land one of the premier players at the position in their drafts.
articles.body:
Tight end is among the trickiest positions in fantasy football, especially for managers who are unable to land one of the premier players at the position in their drafts.

When that happens, managers often choose to wait until the later rounds to address tight end based on the idea that there isn't much separation between tight ends just outside the top-five rankings and the rest of the field.

For fantasy football managers who aren't fortunate enough to land Brock Bowers, Trey McBride, Colston Loveland or Tyler Warren, here is a look at the sleeper tight ends to both target and avoid in your drafts.

Once among the top tight ends in football with back-to-back 900-yard seasons in 2022 and 2023, Hockenson is now viewed as a player who is only borderline draftable in most fantasy leagues.

Hockenson has failed to reach 500 receiving yards in each of the past two seasons, as a torn ACL suffered in 2023 delayed the start of his 2024 season, and he then suffered through subpar quarterback play from J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer last season.

Minnesota's quarterbacking should be markedly better in 2026 with Kyler Murray under center, and there is reason to believe he will target Hockenson often after helping McBride achieve a 111-catch, 1,146-yard campaign in 2024.

Okonkwo was steady if unspectacular during his time with the Tennessee Titans, finishing with between 52 and 56 catches, and between 479 and 560 yards each of the past three seasons.

He had to share snaps with Gunnar Helm at tight end last season, though, and all signs point toward Okonkwo being the unquestioned TE1 in Washington in 2026.

During Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels rookie season in 2024, veteran tight end Zach Ertz was second on the team in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, and Okonkwo reap similar benefits this season if Daniels stays healthy.

The aforementioned Helm should have the starting tight end job all to himself in Tennessee this season with Okonkwo making the move to Washington.

Despite playing just over half of the Titans' offensive snaps on average, Helm put up some respectable numbers as a rookie last season, recording 44 receptions for 357 yards and two touchdowns.

Quarterback Cam Ward should be more comfortable in his second NFL campaign, and it won't be a surprise if Helm develops into a reliable security blanket.

There is always a certain amount of excitement among fantasy managers at the prospect of selecting a rookie first-round pick, but discretion may be the better part of valor when it comes to Sadiq.

Sadiq was the only tight end taken in the first round of the NFL draft, but he has already aggravated a hernia issue after undergoing surgery to correct it.

On top of that, he has to contend for targets with fellow tight end Mason Taylor, who had 44 grabs for 369 yards as a rookie last season, so there is no guarantee Sadiq will be a big part of the Jets' offense this season even when healthy.

Given that Njoku is just a few years removed from earning a Pro Bowl nod after setting career highs with 81 receptions for 882 yards and six touchdowns while with the Cleveland Browns, it may be difficult for fantasy managers to turn down the opportunity to draft him late.

Adding to the potential excitement is the fact that he has departed the moribund Browns offense and joined a Chargers offense led by quarterback Justin Herbert.

However, there are too many mouths to feed in the L.A. offense between wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, and running back Omarion Hampton, plus Njoku will be hard-pressed to surpass Oronde Gadsden on the tight end depth chart after Gadsden racked up 664 yards as a rookie last season.

Freiermuth has had his moments during his five-year NFL career, including scoring seven touchdowns in both 2021 and 2024, and recording a career-high 732 yards in 2022.

He has never managed to firmly establish himself as a starting tight end in fantasy football, though, and his first season playing with quarterback Aaron Rodgers didn't yield great results last season.

Freiermuth had just 41 grabs for 486 yards and four touchdowns, and with Michael Pittman Jr. now joining DK Metcalf in the receiving corps, Rodgers' attention may be funneled even more toward his wideouts.

articles.title: 'This S--t Checkdown City,' Bills Defender Shades Browns Amid Shedeur Sanders-Watson QB Competition
articles.summary: At least one Buffalo Bills defender has apparently been unimpressed by the Cleveland Browns offense during joint practices this week in Ohio.
articles.body:
At least one Buffalo Bills defender has apparently been unimpressed by the Cleveland Browns offense during joint practices this week in Ohio.

ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi reported he heard one Bills player refer to the Browns' offense as "checkdown city."

NFL insider Tom Withers reported that Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was one player who had a message for Shedeur Sanders:

Both Sanders and Deshaun Watson, who are competing to start for the Browns in Week 1, got chances to throw against the Bills during Thursday's 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 sessions.

Sanders and Watson each saw mixed results when playing in the Browns' preseason opener last week against the Chicago Bears.

Watson relied mostly on short throws and made no completed passes over 10 air yards against the Bears, while Sanders gave up an interception on a fourth-quarter overthrow.

Both quarterbacks will look to improve on those issues during joint practices before Sanders starts and Watson plays in relief in Saturday's preseason matchup against the Bills.

articles.title: Cowboys, Saints Fined by NFL After Viral Videos from Fight-Filled Joint Practice
articles.summary: Tuesday's brawl-filled practice between the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints apparently caught the attention of the NFL.
articles.body:
Tuesday's brawl-filled practice between the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints apparently caught the attention of the NFL.

The league fined both teams $500,000, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

🎥 Pickens' Trash Talk from Joint Practice

That comes after Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Thursday that the league requested film from the joint practice to determine if any actions warrant discipline.

Per ESPN's Katherine Terrell , at least two fights broke out between the Saints offense and Cowboys defense during the practice. Clarence Hill Jr. of All City DLLS reported that there were at least seven fights overall.

There was also one moment posted online that caught a lot of attention involving Saints tight end Brock Rechsteiner gave Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson something resembling a German suplex.

Terrell noted the incident involving Rechsteiner started after he was punched by Cowboys cornerback Calen Carson.

Schottenheimer said afterward that he and Saints head coach Kellen Moore discussed at one point calling the practice.

"We kind of had agreed that if a couple of other things happened, we would cancel it, but they worked through it," Schottenheimer said. "Again, they settled into it, but again, there's a discipline element to playing this football game, and unfortunately we didn't handle that very well today."

Skirmishes between teams are fairly commonplace during joint practices, but even by that standard what happened between the Cowboys and Saints seemed extreme.

Even though the Cowboys and Saints held a joint practice this week, they won't actually meet in the preseason until Aug. 28. Dallas will play the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on Saturday at 10 p.m. ET.

The Saints will travel to SoFi Stadium to take on the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ravens' Rashod Bateman Talks Jesse Minter's Attention to Details, Did WR Shade John Harbaugh?
articles.summary: At least one Baltimore Ravens player apparently feels there has been more organizational attention to detail since Jesse Minter took over for former head coach John Harbaugh.
articles.body:
At least one Baltimore Ravens player apparently feels there has been more organizational attention to detail since Jesse Minter took over for former head coach John Harbaugh.

Wide receiver Rashod Bateman said the difference with Minter's staff is that "everybody harps on the details" (h/t The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec).

"That's not what we've had here," Bateman added, per Zrebiec.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

The Ravens fired Harbaugh after 18 seasons in January, shortly before promoting Minter from defensive coordinator to head coach.

Harbaugh has since taken over as head coach of the New York Giants, while former Ravens offensive coordinator has left to coach the Cleveland Browns.

This isn't the first time Bateman has hinted at being happy with some changes in the coaching staff after five seasons spent playing under Harbaugh.

Bateman said earlier this month he felt a similar attention to detail while adjusting to schemes drawn up by new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle.

"He's pushing us to be the very best every day," Bateman said earlier this month about Doyle. "I think that's the difference in our offense right now is chasing the small details."

Bateman continued: "I feel like in the past, I've been kind of a one-dimensional receiver. I feel like [Doyle's] seen my talent. He sees everybody's talent. A lot of guys are moving around, and he's playing all strengths."

Bateman is hoping these leadership changes will lead to a bounce-back season for him after posting a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games last season.

A first-round pick out of Minnesota in 2021, Bateman never developed into a clear-cut WR1 with Harbaugh as head coach and Monken or Greg Roman as OC.

Bateman will now hope to find a way to contribute more behind Zay Flowers as he and Doyle work on adding some versatility to his game ahead of his age-27 season.

articles.title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley Hypes Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jonathan Taylor's Historic RB Contracts
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley was excited about the recent contracts signed by fellow top running backs including Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs and Jonathan Taylor.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley was excited about the recent contracts signed by fellow top running backs including Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs and Jonathan Taylor.

"I love it. That's how it's supposed to be," Barkley said Thursday, per Zach Berman of The Athletic (h/t Charean Williams of Pro Football Talk). "Christian [McCaffrey] did it before me. I did it after Christian. And now we have three in a row. I look forward to the next guys to do it. It was like that for every other position besides running back. You can see that coming back to life. Those guys are very deserving of it. They're helluva players, make a lot of impact in games for their teams. Their teams are different when they're not on the field. Hopefully in the next 5-10 years, it keeps going higher. That's how it's supposed to go."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

On Aug. 4, Robinson signed a three-year extension worth up to $75 million with the Atlanta Falcons.

Two days later, Gibbs agreed to a new three-year deal worth $67.5 million with the Detroit Lions while the Indianapolis Colts handed Taylor a two-year, $44 million extension.

Gibbs, Robinson and Taylor are now the three highest-paid players at their position in terms of average annual value while Barkley ranks No. 4 (via Over the Cap ).

Teams haven't always been willing to make a hefty financial commitment to running backs, as Barkley was among several players that held a meeting to discuss the depressed market for the position in July 2023.

At the time, the NFL was coming off a 2022 season in which all 32 teams spent a combined total of $250 million on running backs (via Spotrac ).

For the 2026 season, teams are set to spend $550 million at the position.

While Barkley may no longer own the highest salary among running backs, he's still pleased about the financial future for top backfield options moving forward.

articles.title: Carson Beck Injury Status for Cardinals vs. Cowboys Preseason Game Revealed Amid Rib Issue
articles.summary: After Carson Beck suffered a rib injury earlier in training camp, Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur revealed the quarterback's status for Saturday's preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
After Carson Beck suffered a rib injury earlier in training camp, Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur revealed the quarterback's status for Saturday's preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys.

LaFleur told reporters that Beck "most likely" won't play against Dallas, but he'll throw after practice on Thursday so the Cardinals can determine where he's at.

LaFleur also noted that Jacoby Brissett won't play and Gardner Minshew will get the start.

Beck, a third-round pick out of Miami, had a tremendous showing in the Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown on 15-of-19 passing.

"It feels great to go in and succeed and execute within the offense. And, obviously, again, there's going to be things to fix," Beck told reporters after the game. "You got to go watch the tape and there's always so much room to improve, even just being a rookie, being a new guy and kind of getting my first taste of the league."

Unfortunately for Beck, he suffered a rib injury that forced him to miss last week's game against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Brissett started in that game but Minshew got most of the action, completing 14 of his 16 passes for 101 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Kedon Slovis also got some snaps, throwing for 75 yards on 7-of-9 passing.

With Brissett out and Beck likely to miss as well, Slovis should see plenty of reps this week.

Beck reportedly was in the mix to be the Cardinals' starter for Week 1 early this offseason, and it's unclear where he sits on the depth chart now. Unfortunately, possibly missing another preseason game is just another opportunity missed for Beck to show what he can do.

Nonetheless, Arizona's coaching staff has to be happy with Beck after the way he started the preseason, and he'll look to pick up where he left off when he returns from injury.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Steelers' Joey Porter Jr. Amid Rising CB Contract Market
articles.summary: Multiple teams have "wondered" about Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. as a potential trade target, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
articles.body:
Multiple teams have "wondered" about Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. as a potential trade target, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz .

Per Schultz, opposing front offices have kept an eye on Pittsburgh potentially becoming open to trading Porter due to the current state of the cornerback market.

He'll carry a $4.9 million cap hit for the 2026 season before he's slated to hit free agency in 2027 (via Spotrac ).

Porter has yet to practice in training camp, as he remains on the physically unable to perform list after aggravating a back injury .

He was previously holding in during Pittsburgh's mandatory minicamp in June while he searched for a new contract.

Multiple top cornerbacks have been paid throughout the 2026 offseason, as the Seattle Seahawks handed Devon Witherspoon a four-year extension worth $132 million on Saturday.

The Cleveland Browns also agreed to a two-year, $62.2 million extension with Denzel Ward on July 28.

As for Porter, he's entering his fourth season on the Steelers after they initially selected him with a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft.

He's steadily blossomed into Pittsburgh's No. 1 corner and is coming off a 2025 campaign in which he racked up 52 tackles, 14 passes defended, one sack and one interception.

Porter allowed a mere 56.2 passer rating when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus .

With the lack of an extension agreement as Week 1 continues to draw closer, teams are reportedly monitoring the 26-year-old's availability.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Reacts to His Viral Pick-6 with Raiders QB1 Battle vs. Cousins Set to Continue
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza got a valuable learning moment in the Las Vegas Raiders' 22-20 preseason win over the Houston Texans on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza got a valuable learning moment in the Las Vegas Raiders' 22-20 preseason win over the Houston Texans on Thursday night.

The No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL draft threw a pick-six on the Raiders' first offensive possession when he was trying to connect with Mike Washington Jr., but instead found Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Speaking to reporters after the game, Mendoza lamented the decision and admitted he shouldn't have tried to fit the ball into that tight window.

"I probably should have checked it down to the flat," Mendoza said. "It was not a good throw. We weren't on the same page."

One thing that stands out on the highlight is Washington was at least the third read for Mendoza on that play. His first read is Malik Benson down the field, then Jalen Nailor before he comes back to the middle of the field.

The Athletic's Ted Nguyen pointed out one aspect of the play that may have resulted in the turnover.

Mendoza's postgame assessment about checking down to the flat probably wouldn't have led to a big play. Fullback Connor Heyward did slip out of the backfield, but Texans linebacker Marte Mapu was right with him to make a tackle.

Even though the Texans rested most of their defensive starters, they still have plenty of depth on that side of the ball to make this a rough test for a young quarterback.

Mendoza showed some of the skill that made him the top pick, including a laser to Nailor that picked up 22 yards two plays before the interception. He finished 8-of-15 for 86 yards with no touchdowns and the pick-six. He was also sacked once and pressured six times.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has not announced whether Mendoza or Kirk Cousins, who did not play Thursday, will be the Week 1 starter. It's still assumed Cousins will get the job, but Mendoza has received more reps with the first-team offense recently to keep things open.

"We got another week. I don't want anyone to be comfortable in their job," Kubiak told reporters . "It should always be that way for all positions. So, let's keep going."

Mendoza's full preseason stat line sits at 18-of-31 (58.1 percent), 183 yards, one touchdown and one interception in two games.

The Raiders have one more preseason contest left against the San Francisco 49ers on Aug. 27 before they start to fully prepare for the regular season.

Las Vegas opens the regular season at home against the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 13.
paragraphs: Fernando Mendoza got a valuable learning moment in the Las Vegas Raiders' 22-20 preseason win over the Houston Texans on Thursday night.

The No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL draft threw a pick-six on the Raiders' first offensive possession when he was trying to connect with Mike Washington Jr., but instead found Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz.
Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut
Speaking to reporters after the game, Mendoza lamented the decision and admitted he shouldn't have tried to fit the ball into that tight window.
"I probably should have checked it down to the flat," Mendoza said. "It was not a good throw. We weren't on the same page."

One thing that stands out on the highlight is Washington was at least the third read for Mendoza on that play. His first read is Malik Benson down the field, then Jalen Nailor before he comes back to the middle of the field.
The Athletic's Ted Nguyen pointed out one aspect of the play that may have resulted in the turnover.

Mendoza's postgame assessment about checking down to the flat probably wouldn't have led to a big play. Fullback Connor Heyward did slip out of the backfield, but Texans linebacker Marte Mapu was right with him to make a tackle.
Even though the Texans rested most of their defensive starters, they still have plenty of depth on that side of the ball to make this a rough test for a young quarterback.

Mendoza showed some of the skill that made him the top pick, including a laser to Nailor that picked up 22 yards two plays before the interception. He finished 8-of-15 for 86 yards with no touchdowns and the pick-six. He was also sacked once and pressured six times.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has not announced whether Mendoza or Kirk Cousins, who did not play Thursday, will be the Week 1 starter. It's still assumed Cousins will get the job, but Mendoza has received more reps with the first-team offense recently to keep things open.
"We got another week. I don't want anyone to be comfortable in their job," Kubiak told reporters . "It should always be that way for all positions. So, let's keep going."
Mendoza's full preseason stat line sits at 18-of-31 (58.1 percent), 183 yards, one touchdown and one interception in two games.
The Raiders have one more preseason contest left against the San Francisco 49ers on Aug. 27 before they start to fully prepare for the regular season.
Las Vegas opens the regular season at home against the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Why Peyton Manning's Son Marshall Played Limited Snaps in HSFB Debut and What to Expect in 2026
articles.summary: Marshall Manning, son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning, got his first taste of high school football by playing two snaps for Baylor School in a 38-20 win over Brentwood.
articles.body:
Marshall Manning, son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning, got his first taste of high school football by playing two snaps for Baylor School in a 38-20 win over Brentwood.

Baylor head coach Erik Kimrey explained after the game that Manning's limited usage was part of the development plan as he gets ready to become the starting quarterback in 2027.

"We planned it," Kimrey said. "I want Marshall to play in every game this year, even if it's just two plays like that. Hopefully it'll be a lot more. We need him next year and he needs to be ready."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Baylor School, located in Chattanooga, Tennessee, is opening the season ranked No. 12 nationally by MaxPreps . Manning is only 15 years old and will be part of the 2030 college recruiting class.

Keegan Croucher, a 4-star recruit in the 2027 class who is committed to Mississippi, is the No. 1 quarterback for the Red Raiders.

Manning's two snaps came in the second quarter. He completed a pass to wide receiver Anwtaun Adams on his first play, then handed the ball off to star running back David Gabriel Georges on his final snap.

Thursday's game was a rematch of last year's Tennessee state championship game. Baylor won that contest 28-24 behind 151 rushing yards and a touchdown from Georges, the No. 2 running back recruit in 2027 who will play college football at Tennessee.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Najee Harris Having 'Significant' Role with Giants After 1-Year Contract
articles.summary: Despite being signed just three days ago, the New York Giants are reportedly planning for Najee Harris to be a big factor in their running back rotation this season.
articles.body:
Despite being signed just three days ago, the New York Giants are reportedly planning for Najee Harris to be a big factor in their running back rotation this season.

Per ESPN's Jordan Raanan , the Giants brought Harris in to have a "significant" role in their offense.

"He was brought in under the premise that he's going to be a significant contributor, even though a source told ESPN he signed a one-year minimum salary $1.215 million deal with no guaranteed money," Raanan wrote.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh seemed to indicate Harris would have a chance to elevate his spot on the depth chart throughout the remainder of the preseason if he plays well.

"I mean, football's competitive, the NFL's competitive, and we're building the strongest team we can," Harbaugh said (h/t Raanan). "And [Harris is] a really good football player. So that's it."

Harris signed with the Giants on Tuesday and got three touches in Thursday's joint practice against the Miami Dolphins, per Raanan.

The timing of Harris' deal is notable because there was a lot of criticism aimed at Tyrone Tracy Jr. coming out of New York's preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings on Aug. 15.

In particular, Tracy whiffed on a block in the first quarter that resulted in Jaxson Dart taking a hard hit from Vikings safety Jay Ward.

Dart remained on the turf for a few seconds afterward and had to go through concussion evluation before returning to the game.

There's no indication that Tracy's role with the Giants has changed following the Vikings game. Adam Levitan of Establish the Run even pointed out after Harris was signed that New York had been linked to several running backs during the offseason, including Kenneth Walker III and Jeremiyah Love.

Running back depth is something the Giants needed to be mindful of with Cam Skattebo returning from a right ankle dislocation, open tibia fracture and ruptured deltoid ligament that ended his rookie season in Week 8 last year.

Harris has a strong track record as a running back and receiver. He started 68 consecutive games in his first four seasons, but an Achilles injury in Week 3 ended his 2025 campaign with the Los Angeles Chargers early.

During his four years with the Steelers, Harris ran for more than 1,000 yards in each season. He also averaged 45 receptions per season during that period.

Harris will be part of a Giants backfield that includes Skattebo, Tracy and Devin Singletary.

articles.title: Travis Hunter Used 'Top-of-the-Line Software' in Jaguars' Virtual Meeting Room to Prep for 2026
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter has heavily utilized virtual reality technology during his preparations for the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter has heavily utilized virtual reality technology during his preparations for the 2026 NFL regular season.

Jeff Howe of The Athletic highlighted Hunter's unique methods, writing, "[Jaguars head coach Liam] Coen ordered the construction of a virtual meeting room over the offseason, knocking down a wall and installing top-of-the-line software to aid the team's mental reps. According to those around the Jaguars, Hunter has utilized the room more than anyone, and it's not particularly close. He can walk into the room, listen to the defensive play call, move to his spot within the formation, watch the offense virtually line up and then handle the necessary checks and communication assignments from there."

Selected second overall in the 2025 NFL draft after winning the Heisman Trophy at Colorado, Hunter arrived in Jacksonville with hopes of him being a difference maker on both sides of the ball.

Hunter's rookie campaign was cut short by a knee injury, though, limiting him to only seven games.

He has worked his way back and should be good to go for the start of the regular season, however, as he has been participating heavily in practice for the past few weeks.

Coen has liked what he has seen out of Hunter during the lead up to the Jags' Week 1 game against the Cleveland Browns on Sept. 13, telling Howe, "He's done so much work in the virtual meeting rooms, walkthroughs, [traditional] meeting room. That's been a huge part of his growth and maturation throughout this training camp. He's put in a lot of time and built his body back up in a physical way, especially his upper half. Just getting him playing confident, to really go out and play. He hasn't played football in a long time, so we're really in that ramp-up process."

Although Hunter played 66.7 percent of the offensive snaps compared to 35.9 percent of the defensive snaps last season, all signs point toward him being a bigger contributor at corner than wideout in 2026.

Back in April, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Hunter would primarily be a cornerback and only a part-time wide receiver during his second season:

Coen seemed to confirm as much this week, telling reporters that Hunter is the Jags' "3A, 3B receiver right now." Meanwhile, Hunter is listed as a starting cornerback on the Jaguars' depth chart .

Per Howe, Hunter is "preparing to serve as the team's No. 1 cornerback," although defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile's scheme figures to mostly keep him on one side of the field rather than having him shadow a certain receiver.

articles.title: De'Zhaun Stribling Hyped by Brock Purdy amid Preseason Success, Fantasy Football Buzz
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has been impressed with rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling throughout the opening weeks of training camp.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has been impressed with rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling throughout the opening weeks of training camp.

"Obviously really excited about him," Purdy said during a Friday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (0:25 mark). "He's a smart kid. He's come in, learned our offense. He's got strong hands, great route runner, all the reasons why we drafted him. He's shown it and proven it. Just having him in there with a guy like Mike, Deebo, Demarcus Robinson, we've got a great room of receivers. For him to be able to learn from them but also be able to go out and show that he's willing to be in that starting rotation. He has shown that at camp. We're all really excited about him."

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

The 49ers selected Stribling in the second round of the 2026 NFL draft, adding him with the No. 33 overall pick.

He wrapped up an encouraging performance during San Francisco's 41-17 preseason victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday, catching four of his five targets for 46 yards.

The 23-year-old also hauled in seven receptions for 63 yards during his preseason debut against the Tennessee Titans on Aug. 14.

With Stribling's early production as well as the praise he received from Purdy, it isn't difficult to imagine him immediately becoming a key piece of San Francisco's passing attack. It also makes him an intriguing option for fantasy football managers.

The 49ers will open their 2026 campaign against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10.

articles.title: Drake Maye Ranked 11th-Best NFL Player Under 25 by Coaches & Execs, What Other QBs Made List?
articles.summary: Drake Maye is the best quarterback in the league among players who are under 25 years old, at least in the eyes of NFL coaches and executives.
articles.body:
Drake Maye is the best quarterback in the league among players who are under 25 years old, at least in the eyes of NFL coaches and executives.

Mike Jones of The Athletic shared rankings of players under 25 from coaches and executives around the league Friday, and everyone is looking up at Detroit Lions offensive lineman Penei Sewell.

But in the quarterback department, Maye is ranked highest at No. 11 and ahead of Jayden Daniels (No. 13), C.J. Stroud (No. 19) and Caleb Williams (No. 21).

That Maye is the highest-ranked quarterback isn't that surprising considering he just led the New England Patriots to the Super Bowl and finished second in MVP voting in his second season in the league during the 2025 campaign.

Williams, Daniels and Maye were the first three picks of the 2024 NFL draft in that order, and they have all enjoyed various degrees of success in their first two years. Only Maye has been to the Super Bowl, but Daniels led the Washington Commanders to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie and Williams' Chicago Bears are coming off an NFC North title.

They will be compared to each other throughout the rest of their careers and could end up switching spots on lists like this a number of times moving forward.

And as long as they all continue to play up to their potential and guide their teams to the playoffs, the Patriots, Commanders and Bears will surely be pleased with their franchise quarterbacks no matter which one is ranked ahead of the others on subjective lists.

Perhaps the most notable inclusion is Stroud, who is one of the more intriguing case studies in the NFL at this point.

He wasted no time establishing himself as a star in the league as the Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2023. He also led the Houston Texans to the playoffs in each of his first three years.

However, Stroud failed to replicate his rookie impact in either his second or third year in the league and threw four interceptions in Houston's playoff loss to the Patriots last season. He seems to have taken a step back with more experience, which makes his long-term future a legitimate question.

While he is extension eligible, he and the Texans have not yet agreed to a new deal.

Stroud will have a chance to bounce back in his fourth season, and there may be a new deal and a higher ranking in lists like these waiting for him if he does.

articles.title: Ravens Say They Are Aware of Receiver Rashod Bateman's June Arrest in Georgia Domestic Case
articles.summary: BALTIMORE (AP) — The Baltimore Ravens said Friday they are aware of Rashod Bateman's arrest in June in Georgia over a domestic violence incident and have been in contact with their receiver.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE (AP) — The Baltimore Ravens said Friday they are aware of Rashod Bateman's arrest in June in Georgia over a domestic violence incident and have been in contact with their receiver.

The Ravens have informed the NFL, and league spokesman Brian McCarthy says the case is under review.

"We notified the league office and have been cooperating throughout the process," the team said in a statement. "As this is a pending legal matter, we will not have further comment."

According to TMZ, Bateman was arrested after smashing a window of the vehicle being driven by the mother of his child, with the 3-month-old inside. TMZ cited court documents that said the victim told authorities the incident happened around 6 a.m. on June 6.

According to the arrest warrant, Bateman used an object to smash the driver's side window, and the shattered glass caused multiple small lacerations to the victim's face.

Bateman's representatives said the receiver turned himself in to the Walton County sheriff's office the same day. A court later granted Bateman's request to lift a no-contact order after he said the victim indicated she did want to have contact with him.

"It is unfortunate that a personal family situation has been taken completely out of context for sensational reasons," Bateman attorney Jordan Siev said in a statement to The Associated Press. "We will let the court process play out and the facts will come out at that time."

Walton County authorities didn't immediately respond to a message from the AP.

Last year, Bateman signed a $37 million, three-year contract extension coming off career bests of 756 yards and nine touchdowns receiving in 2024. The 26-year-old Georgia native who played in college at Minnesota dropped off to a career-low 224 yards with two TDs last season.

articles.title: When Shedeur Sanders vs. Deshaun Watson QB1 Battle Will Be Decided Revealed in New Browns Rumors
articles.summary: As Shedeur Sanders prepares to make his first preseason start on Saturday against the Buffalo Bills, the Cleveland Browns could name their Week 1 starting quarterback not long after.
articles.body:
As Shedeur Sanders prepares to make his first preseason start on Saturday against the Buffalo Bills, the Cleveland Browns could name their Week 1 starting quarterback not long after.

Appearing on the Saturday morning SportsCenter , ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Browns head coach Todd Monken could make a decision between Sanders and Deshaun Watson as soon as Monday:

"Shedeur Sanders will get the first half today. I'm told this quarterback battle is still in full swing, even though Deshaun Watson, the veteran, has had some momentum in the last few weeks. What Shedeur does today is a major data point in the process. He won't have all the starters with him, but he will have a few guys with the first-team offense going at it. And I'm told this is how it's going to go; head coach Todd Monken will get through today, he'll get with his staff on Sunday, he'll evaluate all the tape the last few weeks, he'll get input from his staff. I suspect by Monday they should be ready to make a decision on this quarterback battle."

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Watson got the start in Cleveland's preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Aug. 15. He finished 11-of-15 for 126 yards, lost a fumble and led the Browns to 10 points on six drives in the first half.

Sanders came on to start the third quarter and played three drives. He went 6-of-11 for 79 yards with one interception. The Browns went scoreless in the second half with Sanders and Dillon Gabriel running the offense.

Monken has been clear throughout training camp and into preseason that there's not much separating the two quarterbacks. He said on the heels of the Bears game it would be "unfair" not to give Sanders an opportunity to play with at least some of the starters in a game before making a decision:

"Again, I did feel going into last game that it was relatively close in terms of both having an opportunity at the starting position, so it would be unfair to not go into the next game and give Shedeur that same opportunity. Albeit a different team, certainly at home. There's no guarantee the same players will be playing in this game, but it's the closest you have, and we owe it to both players who have handled it well and competed at a high level."

Watson's start against the Bears marked his first appearance in a game since Oct. 20, 2024. He tore his right Achilles two different times, including in January 2025 while rehabbing the original injury.

Sanders started the final seven games for the Browns last season. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight appearances as a rookie.

The Browns do have another preseason game after Saturday when they take on the New England Patriots on Aug. 27, but typically teams won't feature many starters in the last game before the regular season.

Given the quick turnaround for that game, as well, it makes sense the Browns coaches would likely want to settle on their starting quarterback sooner than later so they can begin preparing for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sept. 13.
