Watson's start against the Bears marked his first appearance in a game since Oct. 20, 2024. He tore his right Achilles two different times, including in January 2025 while rehabbing the original injury.
Sanders started the final seven games for the Browns last season. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight appearances as a rookie.

The Browns do have another preseason game after Saturday when they take on the New England Patriots on Aug. 27, but typically teams won't feature many starters in the last game before the regular season.

Given the quick turnaround for that game, as well, it makes sense the Browns coaches would likely want to settle on their starting quarterback sooner than later so they can begin preparing for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Rookie Sleepers Undervalued in Drafts
articles.summary: Some of the most sought-after targets in fantasy football were among the most prominent picks at the 2026 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
Some of the most sought-after targets in fantasy football were among the most prominent picks at the 2026 NFL Draft.

Prized rookie rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is often gone by the end of Round 2, while receiver Carnell Tate is typically snatched by Round 6.

The appeal is obvious with both. Given the draft capital invested in them by the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans, respectively, they will be given every chance to succeed and could have mammoth workloads right away.

These aren't, of course, the only fantasy-relevant rookies we'll see. The reasons might be less obvious, but the following three players all have opportunities to deliver impact production at a bargain draft price.

By trade, KC Concepcion is an NFL wideout. By practice, he's more of a makes-things-happen playmaker.

Over a three-year college career split between NC State and Texas A&M, Concepcion made noise (and put up numbers) as a pass-catcher, ball-carrier and punt returner. During his preseason debut, it was more of the same, as he tallied three catches (on four targets) for 27 yards, a 14-yard touchdown run and a 31-yard punt return.

That versatility definitely helps. It gives him a chance to be more involved, for one, but it also could allow him to make an impact without being entirely dependent on this passing attack, which feels enormously helpful given the state of Cleveland's quarterback room.

He has a dynamic burst, open-field shiftiness and a knack for sniffing out the best path to a big play. He would, admittedly, be even more interesting in a more functional offense, but he'd also probably cost a lot more in a fantasy draft, then.

Little is known and even less is proven about the revamped passing game in Miami. New quarterback Malik Willis has made six career starts in four seasons. Starting receivers Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington have yet to clear 620 receiving yards in a season.

That, admittedly, makes any investment into this aerial attack a true blind leap of faith. That said, it also allows just about anyone to fast-track their way into a prominent role, and it sure sounds like third-round rookie Caleb Douglas is doing exactly that. He snagged a starting spot on the team's first depth chart, then promptly posted what will be one of the best catches we'll see all season.

"He's making plays left and right," veteran tight end Greg Dulcich told reporters . "It's awesome. He's showing up all over the field."

Douglas looks the part of an impact receiver. He has size, a big catch radius, physicality and an intriguing mix of quickness and speed. He had tantalizing moments in college, but it often felt like he was capable of so much more if he ever put it all together. If that's what's happening right now, he could be a real find in fantasy.

De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

While it has been a stock-up preseason so far for the second-round pick, De'Zhaun Stribling still offers significant sleeper appeal.

He could be hard-charging his way toward a prominent role in what should be one of the league's most potent offenses. The 49ers have other playmakers on paper, sure, but they just about all come attached to age and injury concerns. If Stribling simply looks solid, he'd at least be positioned for some by-default duties in place of an injured veteran.

But he looks like he might be a lot more than that. He's had 13 passes thrown his way this preseason and converted those chances into 11 receptions for 109 yards. He runs crisp routes, has great hands, boasts explosive speed (4.36-second 40-yard dash at the Combine) and blocks the way coach Kyle Shanahan demands his receivers to.

At this rate, it feels like Stribling has a navigable path to WR2 duties for the 49ers with if-everything-breaks-right WR1 upside.

articles.body:
Buffalo Bills defensive back Damar Hamlin intercepted Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders on Saturday, and he had some fun at his expense by hitting the watch flex while celebrating with his teammates.

Hamlin's interception came after Sanders threw behind his receiver on a five-yard slant and the ball popped into the air. It was Sanders' second interception of the preseason.

That has been an ongoing issue for Sanders after he threw 10 interceptions in just seven starts as a rookie.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders Slam Browns Fans in Video After Veteran QB Booed in Preseason Game
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson says he felt Cleveland Browns fans were "disrespectful" when they booed him during Saturday's preseason game against the visiting Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson says he felt Cleveland Browns fans were "disrespectful" when they booed him during Saturday's preseason game against the visiting Buffalo Bills.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said after Saturday's preseason action (h/t ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi). "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think that's a disrespectful thing."

"Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles," Watson added. "That same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt.

"What does that have to do with it? What does that have to do anything with my performance? When a person gets hurt, especially from their own city, and they cheer... I had different thoughts on what it was going to be, but it is what it is."

Watson also said prior to Saturday he thought he'd done enough since making his last start for the Browns in October 2024 to help win over the fanbase.

"I thought being away for two years, and working myself back from two Achilles injuries, and putting the time in, and being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them... would help, but I guess it hasn't," Watson said. "It's personal."

Boos could be heard on the broadcast after Watson threw an interception in the third quarter. He finished with 5-of-12 passing for 36 yards.

Shedeur Sanders, who is competing with Watson for the starting job, also threw an interception as the Browns conceded a 31-7 defeat to a Bills squad led by quarterbacks Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele.

"In general, I don't appreciate that at all, regardless of competition. We're all human beings," Sanders said about the boos after the game.

"However y'all feel about the situation, about with Deshaun and everything— still, I think it's more about the bigger purpose of just respect. It's just respect that I feel like should be there, because we're all out there trying to do our best and trying to serve the franchise."

Browns coach Todd Monken said he felt his quarterbacks could get a better reaction from the crowd at Huntington Bank Field with stronger play.

"I don't wanna get booed. It comes with the territory," Monken said. "You don't want to get booed, just play good football. Let's play good at quarterback... and then you don't have to worry about it, because it can turn just like that.

"Win, play good football, and everything will be fine."

Monken also said he would wait to see tape to evaluate Watson's play but he was "proud of the way he's worked to get where he's at."

The Browns have yet to confirm whether it will be Watson or Sanders starting when the team opens the regular season Sept. 13 at the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Monken said Saturday he expects announce Watson or Sanders as the starter before Thursday's preseason finale against the visiting New England Patriots.

articles.title: Eagles' Ja'Quinden Jackson Exits in Ambulance After Injury on Hit During Preseason Game vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles running back Ja'Quinden Jackson was taken off the field in an ambulance after being injured on the opening kickoff during Saturday's preseason matchup against the New England Patriots.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles running back Ja'Quinden Jackson was taken off the field in an ambulance after being injured on the opening kickoff during Saturday's preseason matchup against the New England Patriots.

The Eagles announced that Jackson "has strength and movement in all extremities" and was taken to the hospital for further evaluation.

Jackson's agent, Damien Butler, stated a CT scan came back negative and Jackson was "awake and alert," according to ESPN's Tim McManus .

"Jackson was released from the hospital and joined his teammates for their return trip Saturday night to Philadelphia," according to McManus.

"Tonight, above all else, we thank God that Ja'Quinden is doing well following an incredibly frightening moment during the game," Butler said in a statement obtained by ESPN. "We are extremely grateful to the Philadelphia Eagles' medical staff and the first responders whose swift actions and exceptional care supported Ja'Quinden during this critical moment."

Jackson, 24, went undrafted in 2025 and signed with Jacksonville, spending the season on the team's practice squad. He signed a futures contract with the team in January but was waived in May. He was then signed by the Eagles in August.

In four collegiate seasons between Utah (2021-23) and Arkansas (2024) he rushed for 2,148 yards and 29 touchdowns, adding 23 receptions for 200 yards.

This summer he was battling for a roster spot on the Eagles. Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby are locks to make the roster and Will Shipley seems likely to secure a spot as well, leaving players like Jackson, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele to impress the Eagles enough to either keep four running backs on the 53-man roster or earn a spot on the practice squad.

articles.title: Watch Harrison Butker Hit FG That Would've Set NFL Regular-Season Record on Video in Chiefs-Bucs
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker proved Saturday he has the chops to potentially kick the longest field goal in NFL history.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker proved Saturday he has the chops to potentially kick the longest field goal in NFL history.

Butker made a 69-yard field goal during a Saturday preseason matchup at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The regular-season record for the longest NFL field goal was set last season at 68 yards.

That standard was set last November by the Jacksonville Jaguars' Cam Little, who made a 68-yard kick in a Nov. 2 game against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Little also holds the record for the longest goal kicked in the NFL preseason after hitting a 70-yarder last August against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Butker recorded the longest field goal of his regular-season career in October 2022, when he set a Chiefs franchise record by making a 62-yard kick as time expired in the first half of a matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Butker, who is heading into his 10th season with the Chiefs, went 5-for-8 on field goal attempts from at least 50 yards out last season. He is 35-for-53 from beyond 50 yards in his regular-season career.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' 'Aura' Highlighted by Browns Insiders in Rumors amid QB1 Battle vs. Deshaun Watson
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders has displayed something tangible to his coaches as he tries to claim the starting job ahead of the regular season.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders has displayed something tangible to his coaches as he tries to claim the starting job ahead of the regular season.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday on SportsCenter the QB battle "is essentially over" following the Browns' second preseason game. It's unclear where coach Todd Monken will go, but Sanders has made a positive impression.

"I will say about Shedeur Sanders, when I talk to people with the Browns, the word 'presence,' the word 'aura,' comes up," Fowler said. "Like he has something to him that has certainly helped his cause. And he played well yesterday. So, he's made a compelling case at the very least here. But we'll see, Deshaun Watson has had momentum for a couple of weeks. So, do they just stick with that or did yesterday change things in a big way? Monken's got to find that out."

The NFL insider reported Monken could make up his mind by Monday.

Sanders outplayed Watson in Saturday's 31-7 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He finished 9-of-11 for 74 yards, one touchdown and an interception, while Watson went 5-of-12 for 36 yards and one pick.

But that followed Watson having the stronger showing in Cleveland's preseason opener.

In general, neither quarterback has gone above and beyond between the two games. Here are their total numbers.

Factors unrelated to their performance could play a big role in Monken's decision.

Watson drew boos from the home fans at Huntington Bank Field. They've completely turned against the three-time Pro Bowler thanks to how disastrous his trade to Cleveland has been.

Watson didn't hold back in his post-game press conference when addressing the fan reaction.

"It has nothing to do about the performance," he told reporters . "It's a little bit personal. I think that's a disrespectful thing. I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. Just move on."

Given how much his game has declined since arriving in Cleveland, starting Watson was already a suboptimal solution to the team's quarterback situation. Now, it's even harder to envision him leading the offense.

"This is not the punctuation that [Watson] wanted on this quarterback battle because the feeling out of Cleveland, and I spent a day there this week, because Deshaun Watson had some momentum," Fowler said. "He had a couple of good weeks here, stacked some good plays together, he was getting some prominent reps in the practices against the Bills in that joint practice. So, now the Browns have to weigh what happened on the field with Watson and also what he said at that press conference. Is he in a good space to be the leader for this team?"

Sanders doesn't have the same kind of baggage as Watson, and the 24-year-old may have more upside than he showed as a rookie in 2025.

Maybe Sanders isn't the future of the QB position for the Browns, but starting him in Week 1 is probably the best call at this point.

articles.title: Patriots' Will Campbell Reveals Advice From Eagles Legend After Backlash for Super Bowl Performance
articles.summary: New England Patriots offensive tackle Will Campbell got some helpful guidance from a notable peer heading into the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
New England Patriots offensive tackle Will Campbell got some helpful guidance from a notable peer heading into the 2026 NFL season.

The second-year lineman told ESPN's Mike Reiss that longtime Philadelphia Eagles tackle Lane Johnson suggested to him he had "to be very honest with yourself about the season."

"I felt like before I got hurt [Nov. 23], I was playing some solid ball," Campbell said. "And after that, I didn't play the way I needed to play. So just learning from it, fixing it. After the season, I was just worried about getting healthy, building my strength back to where I knew it needed to be and coming into [spring practices] ready to go, trying to do everything I can to put myself in the best position possible to help the team."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

The criticism toward Campbell was acute following New England's loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl LX. Quarterback Drake Maye was sacked six times and faced steady pressure all game. Across the entire postseason, he absorbed 21 sacks.

After the Super Bowl, Campbell revealed he had been playing through a knee injury, which partially explains his performance against Seattle.

On the whole, the 2025 first-round pick had an encouraging rookie season. Starting at left tackle is a lot to ask of a first-year player, and New England becoming a playoff contender only added to his burden.

Campbell told Reiss he spent a small portion of his offseason working out with Johnson and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Tristan Wirfs, Buffalo Bills' Dion Dawkins and Kansas City Chiefs' Creed Humphrey. He called the group "all super nice to me and welcoming."

"They've played a lot of football at a high level," he said. "Lane and Tristan have both won Super Bowls, so they have everything a young, aspiring tackle in this league wants by the time they're that age. It was not only being able to hang out, but seeing how they work, and just to get in there and compete and soak up anything I can from them."

The Patriots used a top-five selection on Campbell in the hope he becomes an elite outside blocker for a long time to come. It sounds like he put in the time to make that happen.

articles.title: Browns Sign Former 1st-Rounder to Contract After Star DE's Season-Ending Injury, New Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns lost one of their most important defensive players for the 2026 season, but they quickly pivoted to find a replacement.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns lost one of their most important defensive players for the 2026 season, but they quickly pivoted to find a replacement.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Browns defensive end Alex Wright will be placed on season-ending injured reserve after suffering a torn Achilles this past week. Cleveland reportedly will sign veteran defensive end and former first-round pick Derek Barnett to a one-year deal worth up to $5.5 million, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Wright suffered the injury on Thursday during a joint practice with the Buffalo Bills. He went down during a one-on-one drill with Bills offensive tackle Spencer Brown and had to be carted off the field.

The Browns signed Wright to a three-year, $33 million contract extension during the 2025 season, and he finished with career highs of 37 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks. He was expected to play a bigger role this year for a Cleveland defense that will need to replace the production of two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett, who was traded to the Los Angeles Rams.

The No. 14 pick in the 2017 NFL draft by the Philadelphia Eagles, Barnett won a Super Bowl title in his rookie year. He spent the last two-plus seasons with the Houston Texans after being claimed off waivers in 2023. He appeared in all 17 games in 2025 and produced 21 tackles and five sacks.

Per ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi , the Browns were "already scouring the edge rusher market before Wright's injury," and they hosted veterans Jadeveon Clowney and Za'Darius Smith on visits in recent weeks before they signed elsewhere. articles.title: Browns Set to Make QB1 Decision on Shedeur Sanders-Deshaun Watson Battle, HC Todd Monken Says
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters Sunday that he will name a starting quarterback on Monday following Saturday's 31-7 loss to the Buffalo Bills in their second preseason game.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters Sunday that he will name a starting quarterback on Monday following Saturday's 31-7 loss to the Buffalo Bills in their second preseason game.

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

The decision is down to veteran Deshaun Watson and second-year man Shedeur Sanders.

Both Watson and Sanders were given once start each during the preseason. Watson started the first game, finishing 11-of-15 for 126 yards with a sack taken, while Sanders was 6-of-11 for 79 yards and a pick.

Sanders started the second game and finished 9-of-11 for 74 yards with a touchdown, interception and sack taken. Watson was awful, meanwhile, going 5-of-12 for 36 yards and an interception. He was booed during the contest from Cleveland fans and did not take kindly to the act.

"It has nothing to do about the performance. It's a little bit [more] personal than that," Watson told reporters. "Last time I played on this field I tore my Achilles, and that same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt. What does that have to do with anything about performance?"

"I was disappointed for us collectively, that we didn't play well offensively, I'll just put it that way," he told reporters . "When you're behind the chains, it's hard. I know you asked him, 'Hey, how does it feel to get booed?' It's a pretty easy question. It sucks! I don't want to get booed, but it comes with the territory. You don't want to get booed? Play good football."

As for the quarterback battle, the consensus among pundits was that Watson should not be the starter following Sunday's performance, his controversial press conference and years of evidence in Cleveland that he isn't a viable option:

The Browns have two first-round picks next season in a strong quarterback draft. It's a borderline guarantee they will use one of them on the position. But at this point, giving Sanders a second chance to prove whether he can handle a starting gig or not is the most logical option.

Watson had multiple years to prove himself in Cleveland and never did, and that was before Sunday's contentious presser. If he's named the starter anyway, Sundays in Cleveland are going to be awkward affairs.

articles.title: Christian McCaffrey Says Missing 49ers Practice was 'Part of the Plan' amid Injury, Contract Rumors
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey told reporters on Sunday that missing practices this summer was always the plan to keep him fresh for the entire 2026 season, amidst some rumors that perhaps his absences were a contractual hold-in.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey told reporters on Sunday that missing practices this summer was always the plan to keep him fresh for the entire 2026 season, amidst some rumors that perhaps his absences were a contractual hold-in.

"Obviously when you don't practice, the way the media works now it's a firestorm," he said. "But this was kind of part of the plan from the jump was to ramp up pretty big, get nine, 10 practices in, kind of come back down and then ramp back up so we're fresh for the duration. ... And again, I feel great. I feel fresh and it's good to be back out there."

Last week, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that McCaffrey wasn't staging a hold-in and was dealing with "actual tightness."

Head coach Kyle Shanahan said as much this week as well.

"People make a lot of assumptions, and that would be one that they're wrong on," he told reporters regarding the hold-in talk.

For a 49ers team that dealt with massive injury issues last season and is already enduring those same concerns against this summer, keeping McCaffrey healthy and available is the absolute top priority.

The 30-year-old was a beast for the Niners in 2025, rushing for 1,202 yards and 10 touchdowns while adding 102 catches for 924 yards and another seven scores. He was the absolute keystone of the team's offense and helped the beat-up 49ers surprisingly secure a playoff berth.

But his past injury issues, his age and the fact that he's coming off a massive workload in 2025 (413 touches) means managing his health this summer—and during the season—is of the utmost importance.

McCaffrey was back at practice on Sunday, which should put the hold-in talk to rest for good.

articles.title: NFL's Biggest Rumors and Latest Buzz Ahead of 2026 Roster Cuts Deadline
articles.summary: NFL coaches have enough game film and training camp practice evaluations to make key roster decisions before the August 30 cutdown deadline. It's going to be a busy week.
articles.body:
NFL coaches have enough game film and training camp practice evaluations to make key roster decisions before the August 30 cutdown deadline. It's going to be a busy week.

While some players continue to battle for roster spots in the final week of the preseason, coaches will be in their offices looking over the dynamics of prospective depth charts for the regular season.

To get an idea of what could happen in the coming days, let's check in with the latest buzz on potential cuts, trades and roster news.

Who are the notable veterans on the roster bubble? Who might be on the trade block? What are some team concerns ahead of Week 1?

Bills' Notable Free-Agent Acquisitions Are on the Roster Bubble

The Buffalo Bills signed safety Geno Stone and outside linebacker Mike Danna to one-year deals. They've both held starting roles over the last few years with their previous teams.

With the Kansas City Chiefs, Danna worked his way into a lead position at defensive end. Stone earned a first-string role with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023 and started in every game with the Cincinnati Bengals between 2024 and 2025.

But the Bills have a stacked roster. Consequently, Stone and Danna are cut candidates ahead of the deadline.

The Athletic's Joe Buscaglia explained why he left Danna off his latest Bills 53-man roster projection:

" Mike Danna, an early May signing, has over $1 million guaranteed on his one-year deal, but he's faded into the background in the outside linebacker group. With investments in Hoecht, Parker a roster lock and Solomon as one of their best special teams assets, I've got Danna on the outside of this projection ."

Buscaglia believes the Bills could make a decision between Damar Hamlin and Stone at safety, with the former having a slight edge in a battle for one spot.

"While I still have the Bills keeping five safeties, I've switched Hamlin onto the 53-man roster and Stone on the outside looking in," Buscaglia wrote. "Between the two, I think Hamlin has been the more consistent player."

As former starters still younger than 30, Danna and Stone will likely land with new teams before Week 1 if the Bills cut them.

Bengals Might Add Help at Offensive Tackle

The Cincinnati Bengals haven't settled on a primary swing tackle.

After last Saturday's preseason game against the Chicago Bears, head coach Zac Taylor shared his thoughts on the position via Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer .

"I think that's still pretty open," Taylor said. "I think there's guys we're still looking at and I wouldn't say there's any decisions we've made there."

Conway believes the Bengals could be in the market for an offensive tackle after final roster cuts, and it could impact Cody Ford's standing on the depth chart:

" The Bengals could very well be in the market for a reserve tackle over the next few weeks when roster cuts begin around the NFL. It's unlikely the Bengals will move on from Ford ahead of the season because of his experience in the offense, but this doesn't mean if the pro personnel department finds a better option, he wouldn't lose his spot ."

Orlando Brown Jr. and Amarius Mims are the Bengals' starting tackles on the left and right side, respectively. They both started in every game last season but struggled in pass protection.

According to Pro Football Focus, Brown allowed nine sacks over 733 pass-blocking snaps, and Mims allowed 35 pressures over 694 pass-blocking snaps.

The Bengals aren't at a point of benching either of them, but they need reliable reinforcements to protect quarterback Joe Burrow if injuries and/or further decline in performance cost the starters playing time.

Browns TE Dae'Quan Wright Could Become First NFL Player to Return to College

Dae'Quan Wright could be the first to return to the college ranks after an offseason in the NFL.

This year, Wright went undrafted and signed with the Philadelphia Eagles, who waived him on August 10. The Cleveland Browns claimed him, then waived the 22-year-old on Sunday.

Wright's agents, Drew Rosenhaus and Kyle Lincoln, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that their client has an agreement to play at LSU for the 2026 term.

Wright dressed for the Browns' second preseason game, but he didn't play a snap. After the contest, head coach Todd Monken briefly discussed the situation around the rookie tight end.

"Man, isn't this s--t crazy?" Monken said Saturday . "I don't even know what to say. I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out to me a week ago; now I know. I didn't call him back. I guess I should have."

Going forward, we could see more undrafted rookies follow the same pathway as Wright if they're unable to secure roster spots.

Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty Is Nursing a Sprained Ankle

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter, Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty sprained his ankle at practice on Sunday.

The Athletic's Sam Warren provided context to the incident in a post on X:

" Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty left practice early today with an apparent injury. He dove for a ball that was beyond him during team period and went down awkwardly. He was helped off the field by trainers, unable to put weight on his right leg and he did not return ."

Warren also noted rookie fourth-rounder Mike Washington Jr. picked up most of the carries in Jeanty's absence.

With a strong showing at camp and two productive preseason outings, logging 15 carries for 119 yards, Washington has likely earned more touches regardless of Jeanty's status.

Though Jeanty avoided a significant injury, his return timetable remains unclear. The Raiders may ask a little more of Washington if their lead ball-carrier is sidelined for the start of the regular season. They could also add to the running back room to strengthen a backfield platoon.

J.J. McCarthy May Fall to QB3 on Vikings Depth Chart, Trade Questions Brewing

The Minnesota Vikings declared Kyler Murray their starter over J.J. McCarthy early in a quarterback competition.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters that McCarthy still has a "future with the organization" via ESPN's Kevin Seifert . But the third-year signal-caller's short-term outlook is uncertain.

During an ESPN SportsCenter segment (h/t X user @realmnsportsfan), Jeremy Fowler suggested McCarthy may not even be Murray's primary backup and brought up the possibility of a trade.

"Is he QB2 in Minnesota or is he QB3? Because they do have Carson Wentz," Fowler said. "So, could the Minnesota Vikings field a few trade calls? A lot could happen. They have to decide what McCarthy's role is on the team."

After completing 57.6 percent of his passes last season, McCarthy has struggled with his accuracy and ball placement in the preseason. In his last outing against the Baltimore Ravens, he threw a pinpoint 50-yard laser to wideout Tai Felton but failed to connect with wideout Myles Price on a wide-open throw to the end zone and finished with a 50 percent completion rate.

McCarthy's standing on Minnesota's depth chart would become more uncertain if the Vikings list Wentz as their No. 2 quarterback.

Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Blunt About Lack of Roster Depth

NFL teams need reliable backups who can fill in for banged-up starters. In many cases, the healthiest top clubs make deep playoff runs.

Head coach Mike Vrabel gave an honest assessment of his roster's depth and why it was important to protect his starters in the preseason via ESPN's Mike Reiss .

"I do not think we have a very deep team, so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available," Vrabel said.

Coming off a Super Bowl loss, New England bolstered its starting unit, adding wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones and safety Kevin Byard, but the roster still lacks experienced reinforcements outside of the wide receiver and offensive line groups.

If the Patriots have to work around a rash of injuries, it could be a major issue late in the upcoming season. They may be one of the more active teams in acquiring players after roster cuts.

Steelers Might Retain 4 Quarterbacks on 53-Man Roster

The Pittsburgh Steelers may hoard quarterback talent and retain all four of their signal-callers.

Mason Rudolph didn't play in the second preseason game, which is an indication that he's Aaron Rodgers' primary backup, unless the team trades him.

Drew Allar had an impressive preseason debut, going 10-of-13 passing for 153 yards and two touchdowns with a rushing score, but he completed less than 50 percent of his passes last week in a 17-0 loss to the New York Jets. Will Howard struggled in the previous outing, throwing two interceptions.

Allar and Howard probably aren't ready for fill-in duty if Rodgers goes down with an injury, which is why Pittsburgh should keep Rudolph.

ESPN's Brooke Pryor believes the Steelers might trim their offensive line or safeties groups to keep four quarterbacks:

" Unless the Steelers try to sneak Howard through on the practice squad, it seems more and more likely that they'll keep four quarterbacks, and that would mean numbers have to be reduced somewhere else on the roster. Two potential groups to watch are the offensive linemen and safeties because of the position flexibility of veterans such as Brock Hoffman and Jalen Ramsey ."

If the Steelers expose one of their signal-callers to waivers, Howard is the name to watch ahead of the roster cuts deadline.

Howard, a sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft, spent most of his rookie year recovering from a fractured pinky on his throwing hand.

As a rookie third-rounder who's shown some flashes, Allar should be a priority developmental project for the future.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

The 2026 college football season will officially begin this weekend, and some experts are already looking ahead to the 2027 NFL draft.

ESPN NFL draft gurus Mel Kiper Jr. and Field Yates dropped a new video breaking down the top sleeper prospects in college football this season. The full list of prospects is as follows:

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

"You go with guys who could maybe be in the first, early second round discussion, but right now aren't being discussed that way," Kiper explained. articles.title: Mike Vrabel Addresses 'Issues' with Patriots Front Office After Calling Out Roster Depth
articles.summary: After surprisingly declaring that the New England Patriots are lacking depth entering the 2026 season, head coach Mike Vrabel clarified that there isn't a disconnect between him and the team's front office.
articles.body:
After surprisingly declaring that the New England Patriots are lacking depth entering the 2026 season, head coach Mike Vrabel clarified that there isn't a disconnect between him and the team's front office.

"These aren't issues. I'm not in a subtle context -- that wasn't that," Vrabel said Monday in his weekly appearance on sports radio WEEI, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . "They asked why we didn't play the guys, and [the answer is] we have to have everybody we have available and then continue to develop and see some guys that went out and played like they did on Saturday night to build that depth."

The concerns over Vrabel's relationship with New England's front office arose when the second-year coach candidly admitted that he held the defending AFC champion's starters out of the first two preseason games because he isn't confident in the depth of the roster.

"I do not think we have a very deep team, so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available," he said after Saturday's 24-21 preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles, per Reiss .

On Monday, Vrabel made it clear that he was not attempting to send a message or shift blame to anyone else in the organization, as he has been part of key roster decisions since taking over as head coach last year.

"We are the front office. We are all making the decisions. We're all included in this. It was about the young guys we have to develop," Vrabel said. "You can see that the players we kept out of the game, those are the guys. And we have to be able to find some guys behind them to be backups, to be the first guy in … those are the things that we are trying to develop and I guess that's what I was referencing."

The Patriots are hoping to contend for a second straight trip to the Super Bowl, but Vrabel's comments indicate that they may not be worthy of being projected among the elite teams in the NFL this season.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Top Team Names, PPR Rankings and Dynasty Advice
articles.summary: Week 2 of the NFL preseason slate is, by and large, the true test runs for teams ahead of the regular season.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the NFL preseason slate is, by and large, the true test runs for teams ahead of the regular season.

In a lot of ways, it serves the same function for fantasy football managers.

Ahead of the busiest draft weekend on the calendar, it offers the last real opportunity for cram-session studying. Maybe that's mock drafting, rankings analysis or team-name spitballing. Or perhaps it's seeking out an article like this featuring team names to consider, PPR rankings and draft advice for dynasty leagues.

Since dynasty leagues carry rosters over from one season to the next, the setup is as similar to running an NFL franchise as you'll find in the fantasy world. And much like NFL teams, dynasty leagues feature both win-now contenders and long-term rebuilders.

You need to know (and accept) your team's true identity and draft accordingly. If you have a realistic chance of winning big this season, then bump up those tried-and-true (and maybe a little boring) veterans. Safe, reliable production is your friend. Conversely, you should not be paying premiums for mystery-box rookies.

If you're on the other end of the competitive scale, then you should be throwing as many long-term darts as you can. They aren't all going to hit, so that's why you want as many lottery tickets as you can get. You only need a couple of big connections to significantly brighten your future and improve your odds of eventually finding your way to title town.

While injuries can knock out any players at any moment, the trend still shows they impact certain positions more consistently than others. That's especially true when thinking of longevity.

Running backs, by nature, tend to have pretty limited shelf lives. That's one of the biggest reasons caution flags are flying high around Christian McCaffrey this season, since he celebrated his 30th birthday this summer. It's also why if you have an in-prime running back, you would much rather trade them too soon than too late, since their value could be non-existent with the latter.

Young quarterbacks, on the other hand, should get a big boost for their ability to stick around. Aaron Rodgers is a starting NFL quarterback at 42 years old. Matthew Stafford is a fantasy asset at 38. If you hitch your wagon to the right young signal-caller, that's a connection you could realistically keep for a decade-plus.

Surtain set a high bar for himself when he was an All-Pro and the Defensive Player of the Year in 2024.

In 14 games, he had 47 combined tackles with one interception and 12 pass breakups. According to Pro Football Reference , opposing quarterbacks targeted him just 61 times, and they had a 54.1 percent completion rate and 66.6 passer rating when doing so.

The 26-year-old also ranks 10th in the B/R NFL 1000 and beat out the Los Angeles Chargers' Derwin James Jr. to be the top cornerback .

"Surtain is always under control, plays extremely physical without holding, and makes receivers earn every yard," his player summary read. "Only allowing 50-plus yards receiving in a game twice last season, the All-Pro corner collected more pass breakups than catches allowed down the field."

The Broncos signed Surtain to a four-year, $96 million extension before the 2024 campaign kicked off. That deal is looking like a bigger and bigger bargain.

articles.title: NFL Fans Sound Off on Shedeur Sanders Losing to Deshaun Watson in Browns' QB1 Battle
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns finally made a decision on their starting quarterback for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns finally made a decision on their starting quarterback for the 2026 season.

On Monday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that veteran Deshaun Watson has been named the Browns' starter for their Sept. 13 season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, beating out second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders.

Fans on social media had a lot to say about Sanders losing Cleveland's quarterback competition to Watson:

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Sanders and Watson had been engaged in a quarterback competition throughout the offseason. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Cleveland's decision "truly came down to the end," and the team ultimately "leaned toward Watson's experience." Schultz went on to add that Watson "will have to continue earning" his starting role once the 2026 season officially starts.

Still, some are questioning the Browns' decision after watching Sanders and Watson in Saturday's 31-7 preseason loss against the Buffalo Bills. Sanders went 9-of-11 for 74 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Watson was just 5-of-12 for 36 yards and a pick. Watson also drew some attention after the game when he slammed Cleveland fans for booing him while he was on the field.

Before Cleveland's decision on Monday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that Sanders had a different air around him than Watson.

"I will say about Shedeur Sanders, when I talk to people with the Browns, the word 'presence,' the word 'aura,' comes up," Fowler said on Sunday's episode of SportsCenter . "Like he has something to him that has certainly helped his cause."

In the end, the Browns chose experience over aura, and they will be hoping that Watson can prove that they made the right choice by having Sanders start the year as their backup quarterback.

articles.title: Nick Chubb Hyped by Kevin Stefanski After NFL Retirement, 'One of the Greatest I've Been Around'
articles.summary: After announcing his retirement, Nick Chubb is getting high praise from one of his former coaches.
articles.body:
After announcing his retirement, Nick Chubb is getting high praise from one of his former coaches.

"He's one of the greatest I've been around," Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski—who was the coach of the Cleveland Browns from 2020 to 2025—told The MMQB's Albert Breer .

Stefanski also revealed that the running back was his "favorite" player.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

"He was everybody's favorite player—and that's his teammates' favorite, his coaches' favorite," Stefanski told Breer. "I know I'm not supposed to have favorites, but he was my favorite. I always get that question from young kids: Who's your favorite player? And I know you're not supposed to say, kind of like you're not supposed to say who your favorite kid is, but I would always reply, Nick Chubb. He was a joy to coach."

Stefanski also praised Chubb's work ethic, which included the running back working out at 7 a.m.

"He wasn't doing it for anyone to see, I know that to be a fact," Stefanski told Breer. "But, man, it's this quiet, disciplined mentality that I think just permeated through the entire locker room, which is so, so, so rare in this day and age."

Chubb announced his retirement from the NFL on Aug. 21, ending an eight-year career.

Chubb spent seven years with the Cleveland Browns before spending the final year of his career with the Houston Texans in 2025.

In his lone year in Houston, Chubb racked up 506 yards and three touchdowns on 122 carries while also adding 13 catches for 67 yards. Despite his steady production, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reported after the Texans' season ended that he "likely won't" be back with the team in 2026.

Chubb was once regarded as one of the best running backs in the NFL, compiling four straight 1,000-yard seasons from 2019 to 2022. Unfortunately, his career took a turn when he suffered a torn MCL and a damaged ACL just two games into the 2023 campaign, and he's been chasing his old form ever since.

Chubb piled up 7,349 yards and 54 touchdowns on the ground throughout his career, adding 1,109 receiving yards and five touchdown receptions. He earned four straight Pro Bowl nods from 2019 to 2022.

articles.title: 49ers Owner Jed York Pleads No Contest to Two Misdemeanor Charges in Ohio
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York initially was charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He also was fined $1,150.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Records also show that York had his cellphone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email. "You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offenses in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy. Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy. New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was investigated but not punished by the league after he was arrested in Florida in 2019 for allegedly paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. The charge was later dropped after a court ruled that police violated the rights of Kraft and the other customers when they secretly installed video cameras inside massage rooms at the spa.

The team said it would not have any comment on the situation.

"As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time," the team said in a statement.

York took over day-to-day control of the 49ers from his parents in 2008. He became the team's principal owner in 2024. After some initial struggles under York's leadership, the team has been a consistent contender since hiring coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch in 2017.

The Niners have made the Super Bowl three times under York's leadership, losing in the 2012 season under coach Jim Harbaugh and the 2019 and '23 seasons under Shanahan and Lynch.

York also oversaw the building of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. The team moved from San Francisco to the new stadium in 2014. The stadium has hosted two Super Bowls, a World Cup and a College Football Playoff title game.

articles.title: 'Hot Dog Fridge' Eyed by New Cowboys OC Klayton Adams and Explains Full Vision for Break Room
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams has lobbied for a very special addition to the coaching staff's break room.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams has lobbied for a very special addition to the coaching staff's break room.

Adams told reporters earlier this month he wants to get a "hot dog fridge" for himself and his fellow coaches.

"How can you really have a break room or a snack room if you don't have a hot dog fridge?" he said And if you're gonna have a hot dog fridge, you have to have high quality hot dogs in it. And if you're gonna have high quality hot dogs, we have to have brioche buns and maybe some pretzel buns."

🎥 Pickens' Trash Talk from Joint Practice

He suggested the solution could be "an industrial-sized 7-Eleven hot dog roller."

The comments came after the Cowboys shared a video of Adams being mic'd up at practice. At one point, he tells another Cowboys staffer they'd have to add $100 to the hot dog fridge fund.

This is something Adams has carefully considered, down to the science required to getting the perfect dog.

"One of the things I learned from going to Disneyland with my kids, because I was trying to steam the bun, I was trying to toast the bun, and the guy at Disneyland goes, 'No, man, put it in the bun and then wrap it in foil and let the hot dog steam the bun,'" he said. "It's been revolutionary."

The Cowboys had a top-10 offense in yards and points in Adams' first year as the coordinator. If that doesn't earn somebody a hot dog fridge, then what does?

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' time is running out
articles.summary: Sanders had a chance to win the Browns' starting job. He didn't. Now, with Cleveland turning back to Deshaun Watson, the clock is ticking on Sanders' opportu...
articles.body:
Here's a little thought experiment that's going to tie into the Cleveland Browns' decision to start Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders , I promise:

When's the last time you sat down at a specific, prescribed time to watch a TV show? At, say, 8 p.m. on a Thursday or 9 p.m. on a Saturday? Probably been years, even decades, right? We're in an on-demand world now, where viewers hold the power. There's no such thing as prime time — you can see where this is going, I bet — any more.

Sanders arrived in the NFL on a tsunami of hype, whipped up and fueled by his famous father. Now, it's not unusual for dads to overestimate the skills of their sons — that's the foundation of the entire youth sports industrial complex, after all — but when your father is Deion "Prime Time" Sanders, well, dad's bellowing from the sideline carries a whole lot further.

We don't need to re-litigate everything from Shedeur's career that led him from his father's house to the Cleveland sideline — the decent-but-not-spectacular college career, the fifth-round NFL Draft selection that was either a stunning plunge or a proper assessment, the rookie season that pinballed between glory and agony. What's indisputable is this:

Sanders had every chance to claim the Browns' starting QB job for himself. Hell, the Browns surely wanted Sanders to seize the job, if only so that they could start to distance themselves from a frontrunner for the worst trade and worst contract in NFL history. And he didn't get it done.

The opportunity was there. In 2025, Sanders started the final seven games of the Browns' lost season — in Cleveland, is there any other kind? — and led the team to a 3-4 record. Over the course of the offseason, the Browns focused their free-agency efforts on positions other than quarterback, suggesting that new head coach Todd Monken was happy to stand pat with his current hand of QBs — Sanders, Watson, Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green . (Whether this was a defensible strategy is a different question.)

Over the weekend, Sanders, who started against Buffalo on Saturday, was decent but not necessarily spectacular, going 9-of-11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and a behind-the-receiver interception. Watson, meanwhile, went three-and-out on his first two drives, leading to boos from the Browns' grandstands. Watson would later call those boos "disrespectful," not exactly what you want to hear from your starting QB — or your fans — with just a few weeks left until Week 1.

Monken appears to be siding with Watson for his veteran presence and, well, not much else. Watson hasn't played since October 2024. Sidelined by both suspension and injury, he's seen action in just 19 of a possible 85 Browns games since joining Cleveland after the 2020 season. With a contract too massive to escape or pawn off on anyone else, the Browns had little choice but to see what, if anything, they could wring out of Watson.

So where does that leave Sanders? On a rapidly shrinking island.

Already legendary for churning through quarterbacks over the course of its history, Cleveland started an incredible five different QBs in 2023, four in 2024 and three, including Sanders, last season. If Shedeur wasn't able to fight his way out of that dogpile, what does that say about his prospects going forward?

Sanders' supporters love to claim he hasn't received a fair shake — it's the same complaint that Tim Tebow 's disciples lodged, year after subpar year — and the fact that Watson got the majority of first-team reps in preseason will only fuel that ongoing conspiracy. But if Watson struggles — and Monken has made it clear he expects immediate results — Sanders should get yet another opportunity to prove himself. The question now ahead of Sanders: How many more of those opportunities will he squander?

Prime Time is already history. And now Shedeur Sanders is quickly running out of time to carve his own space, too.

articles.title: Mark Davis, Raiders Donate $25M to Help Build Nevada's 1st Standalone Children's Hospital
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders announced Monday that they were making a $25 million donation to help build Nevada's first standalone children's hospital.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders announced Monday that they were making a $25 million donation to help build Nevada's first standalone children's hospital.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Raiders owners Mark Davis, Egon Durban and Michael Meldman each contributed $5 million each. The Raiders as a team donated $10 million.

"The Las Vegas Raiders are making our largest philanthropic commitment in franchise history because we are dedicated to building a healthier future for kids in Nevada," Davis said in a statement . "We want this gift to remind children and families that they have our team backing them and that the support of the entire Raider Nation is in their corner."

"The Raiders are committed to excellence, and this gift is a generational investment that will keep families closer, strengthen our community, and give every kid every chance to thrive," Intermountain Health region president Mitch Cloward added.

The Raiders have played in Las Vegas since 2020.

articles.title: Patriots, Texans Make Surprise Kayshon Boutte Trade After Higgins' Injury, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The New England Patriots are reportedly trading wideout Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are reportedly trading wideout Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported the Patriots will get a seventh-round pick in the deal:

The deal comes in the wake of Houston receiver Jayden Higgins suffering a season-ending ACL tear.

Boutte, 24, caught 78 passes for 1,159 yards and nine touchdowns in his three seasons for the Patriots after being a sixth-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft.

But with the Patriots adding A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs in the offseason, DeMario Douglas set to handle slot duties , Kyle Williams impressing during the preseason and both Mack Hollins and Efton Chism III available as depth, Boutte was clearly expendable. Keeping seven receivers on the roster never seemed likely.

The Texans, meanwhile, very much needed another option after the Higgins loss. Nico Collins will lead the passing attack but there aren't many trustworthy options behind him, with the oft-injured Tank Dell, second-year man Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson the main options in that regard. The team did sign veterans Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones on Friday, however, and Boutte will be expected to carve out a role for himself as well.

Given C.J. Stroud's struggles last season, an uninspiring group of receivers behind Collins and one of the NFL's best defenses, it wouldn't be surprising if the Texans relied heavily on the running back duo of David Montgomery and Woody Marks, hoping to control time of possession and grind out wins.

But when they do need to open up the passing game, adding Boutte should benefit the effort.

articles.title: Matt LaFleur Jokes He'll Fight Brother Mike During Packers-Cardinals Joint Practice
articles.summary: Fights have run rampant during NFL joint practices over the past few weeks, and Matt LaFleur is ready for anything as the Green Bay Packers have a joint practice with the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Fights have run rampant during NFL joint practices over the past few weeks, and Matt LaFleur is ready for anything as the Green Bay Packers have a joint practice with the Arizona Cardinals.

He joked that he'll fight his brother, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur, if it comes to it.

"If there's an issue, I'm going to tell the guys, 'Hey, you come tag me in. They can tag in my brother. And we'll throw down on the 50,'" Matt LaFleur told reporters Monday.

🎥 Pickens' Trash Talk from Joint Practice

Those comments didn't go unnoticed by Mike:

Matt LaFleur is entering his eighth season as the head coach of the Packers, while Mike LaFleur will make his head coaching debut for the Cardinals this season. Matt will, of course, look to pick up a win against his brother in a preseason game on Friday, but he also said he'll be cheering Mike on this year.

"I think it's going to be pretty special, but at the end of the day, we're just looking to try to get good work on both sides," Matt said. "Certainly, always going to prioritize the Green Bay Packers but if there is another team in the National Football League that I'll be rooting for, it will be the Arizona Cardinals."

The Packers have made the playoffs in all but one season since Matt LaFleur took over. Mike LaFleur, who spent the last three seasons as the offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams, is hoping to find similar success in his new role.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Sleepers Generating Buzz After Preseason Week 2
articles.summary: Fantasy football stocks move throughout draft season.
articles.body:
Fantasy football stocks move throughout draft season.

They might be most fluid, however, coming out of the 2026 preseason's Week 2.

With teams fielding the closest proximity to their actual lineup that we'll see in the regular season, there was valuable intel to be gleaned from noticing who took advantage of their opportunity and who did not.

With everyone chasing value propositions right now, let's find out which booming stocks are generating the right kind of noise.

The Packers are big fans of Matthew Golden. That was obvious as soon as they broke from their norm and spent a first-round pick on a wide receiver, taking Golden 23rd overall in last year's draft. It was evident again when Green Bay cleared out some of the obstacles around this summer, trading Dontayvion Wicks and letting Romeo Doubbs walk in free agency.

Golden appears to be rewarding that faith. While his rookie season was quiet, he ended it on a high note, tallying four receptions (on five targets) for 84 yards and a score in the Wild Card Round. And his lone target of the preseason could not have gone any better, as he snared a 19-yard pass from Jordan Love on a 4th-and-1 while beating lockdown corner Patrick Surtain II in the process.

"I think he has elite hands," coach Matt LaFleur told reporters . "That catch he made in Denver on the crossing route that kind of showed to it. It was a good savviness by him, he felt an underneath defender and he bled up the field. I think it was a good ball especially because he changed the angle on Jordan. But to make that catch and not lose stride, a low hands catch, I think that speaks to just how good his hands really are."

The Packers are clearly counting on a sophomore leap from Golden, and they'll give him every opportunity to help make that happen.

After suffering an ankle fracture back in January, Bo Nix carried a lot of question marks into his preseason debut. Would he be limited by the ailment? Would rust be obvious?

Well, so far, so really good. Nix, who might be a real bargain at his average draft cost of QB15 (per FantasyPros), was 6-of-9 passing for 76 yards and a touchdown. He connected on a 35-yard catch-and-run with notable newcomer Jaylen Waddle and a 21-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey.

""I felt like it (was) exactly where I left off," Nix told reporters . "I felt better. ... I felt pretty good, as good as I've felt in a long time."

Through two NFL seasons, Nix has racked up 7,706 passing yards with 54 touchdowns against 23 interceptions, plus another 786 yards and nine scores on the ground. If he is feeling good, this aerial attack could really hum, especially with that Waddle addition.

De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

It's obviously still early, but De'Zhaun Stribling keeps sending signals that he'll be the rare rookie receiver to handle a heavy-usage role for Kyle Shanahan.

Stribling's name has been buzzing throughout camp, and Week 2 only cranked up the volume. He hauled in four of his five targets (three from Brock Purdy) for 64 yards and ran routes all over the field.

"Obviously, really excited about him" Purdy said on The Pat McAfee Show recently. "He's a smart kid. He's come in, learned our offense. He's got strong hands, great route runner, all the things—the reasons why we drafted him. He's showing it and proving it."

With Ricky Pearsall lost for the season, George Kittle working his way back from a torn Achilles and the bulk of San Francisco's playmakers being on the wrong side of 30, Stribling has a real shot to be a featured part of this passing attack. His stock is rising, but it still isn't high enough (ADP: WR50 in PPR leagues).

articles.title: Cowboys HC Hypes Joe Milton's Growth, Says NFL QBs Are More Than 'Carnival' Arm Strength
articles.summary: When Joe Milton was drafted in 2024, the quarterback was known mostly for his cannon of an arm and not much else.
articles.body:
When Joe Milton was drafted in 2024, the quarterback was known mostly for his cannon of an arm and not much else.

Now, Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer believes Milton is more than just his arm. Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Milton has grown tremendously ahead of the 2026 campaign.

"I first remember hearing about Joe Milton when he was at the University of Michigan and everyone applauded him for how hard and how far he could throw the ball. Cool. That's awesome. Go be in a carnival somewhere. That's not what playing an NFL quarterback is. It's not. … You're throwing through small windows, you're throwing over people, you're changing arm slots. So to me, arm strength is cool. Go to the fair and win a teddy bear. But you got to play quarterback. And that's what I think you see Joe learning is he's playing quarterback. And he's playing quarterback at a high level. He's checking the ball down. He's making blitz adjustments. He's solving problems. He's reading from his first, second to third, and even fourth progression at times. It takes time. You don't stop learning as a quarterback. The only way to do it is to play. I'm really, really proud of him."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

During his time at Tennessee, Milton showed flashes of an NFL-starting quarterback but mostly relied on his arm and athleticism to make plays rather than making adjustments on the fly and going through his progressions.

He's played well in preseason this year, throwing for 107 yards and a touchdown on 12-of-15 passing against the Seahawks before recording 179 yards and two touchdowns on 9-of-13 passing against the Cardinals.

If all goes according to plan for the Cowboys this year, Dak Prescott will avoid injury and Milton won't see much playing time. But if he does have to take over under center, it sounds like Schottenheimer will have plenty of faith in him.

articles.summary: NFL News: For Kelli Finglass, leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her .
articles.body: For Kelli Finglass, leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflixâs Americaâs Sweethearts returns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticismKelli Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.âThe words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting... Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. Iâm trusting humanity to help figure this one out because itâs a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.âThat outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys CheerleadersFinglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.âI spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what weâve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and thatâs been an unexpected âahaâ for meâfor these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.âNow entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.âI have, but weâre so busy, we donât have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. Iâve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandmaâ¦I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.âFor now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. Her story has become intertwined with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, but her lasting message may be simpler: perfection is impressive, while vulnerability can be powerful.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Texas Police Reveal No Criminal Findings and Close Case into Death of Bills' DT Ed Oliver's Son
articles.summary: BUFFALO, N.Y. (AP) — A police investigation into the death of Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver's 1-year-old son has resulted in no criminal findings and the case is now considered closed, the Harris County Sheriff's Office in Texas announced on Monday.
articles.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (AP) — A police investigation into the death of Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver's 1-year-old son has resulted in no criminal findings and the case is now considered closed, the Harris County Sheriff's Office in Texas announced on Monday.

The closing of the case comes after the child's death on June 28 was first confirmed on Saturday in a statement from Bills GM Brandon Beane expressing condolences to Oliver .

Police say the toddler, who was a few days shy of his second birthday, was found unresponsive in the swimming pool of a home in a neighborhood community just north of Houston. The boy was transported to the hospital where he was pronounced dead.

"The incident was thoroughly investigated by detectives, and their finding were no criminal findings. The case is now closed," the police statement said.

Oliver has asked for privacy and prayers while still mourning his son, who was also named Ed.

"Obviously, very unfortunate what happened and as a teammate of him, as someone in this locker room, all we can do is love on him," quarterback Josh Allen said following Buffalo's 31-7 preseason win at Cleveland on Saturday .

"There's nothing that you can say to make the situation any better except being there in whatever ways he needs," Allen added. "I can't imagine what he's going through. But the way that he's dealt with it has been unbelievable."

The 28-year-old Oliver is entering his eighth NFL season since being selected by Buffalo in the first round of the 2019 draft out of Houston. He has been with the team since reporting for the start of training camp.

Oliver appeared with the starters in the Bills' preseason-opening 29-14 win over Carolina, but has missed the past week of practice due to an undisclosed injury.

articles.title: Bills Offer Condolences, Support to Defensive Tackle Ed Oliver Following Death of His 1-year-old Son
articles.summary: CLEVELAND (AP) — The Buffalo Bills are giving defensive tackle Ed Oliver support and space following the accidental death of his 1-year-old son.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — The Buffalo Bills are giving defensive tackle Ed Oliver support and space following the accidental death of his 1-year-old son.

Oliver has been grieving throughout training camp and many of his teammates only learned of the tragic accident on Friday. Following Saturday's 31-7 preseason win over the Browns , Bills quarterback Josh Allen said the team is standing with Oliver.

"Obviously, very unfortunate what happened and as a teammate of him, as someone in this locker room, all we can do is love on him," Allen said. "There's nothing that you can say to make the situation any better except being there in whatever ways he needs.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

"That's what we're going to continue to do. That's what teammates do. You love up on each other when we're down, and I can't imagine what he's going through. But the way that he's dealt with it has been unbelievable."

Oliver has asked for privacy and prayers while still mourning his son, who was also named Ed. The toddler was pronounced dead after being found unresponsive in a residential pool in Harris County, Texas, on June 28, a person briefed on what happened told The Associated Press. The person spoke to the AP on the condition of anonymity because the team and player have not revealed that information.

Without providing many details including names or ages, the Harris County Sheriff's department posted a note on its Facebook account that evening regarding the drowning of a toddler in a neighborhood community north of Houston.

"This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the toddler's family during this incredibly difficult time. The investigation is ongoing," the post read.

A sheriff's official told The Associated Press on Saturday that a report was not immediately available.

Before Saturday's game, Bills general manager Brandon Beane issued a statement expressing his and the organization's condolences.

"It's an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we grieve this tragic loss," Beane said .

Bills first-year coach Joe Brady was equally compassionate toward Oliver, who is in his eighth season with Buffalo.

"Ever since I found out the news, I can't fathom what he's going through," Brady said. "As a coach and a father, there really aren't words to describe it. It's all about us loving him and giving him the privacy that he deserves.

"It's hard when I see him. I don't have the words, but all I can do is support him in whatever way he needs."

The 28-year-old Oliver was selected by the Bills in the first round of the 2019 draft out of Houston.

Oliver reported for training camp on time last month and appeared with the starters in the Bills' preseason-opening 29-14 win over Carolina last weekend. He has not practiced this week because of an undisclosed injury.

This story has been corrected. A previous version, relying on information provided at the time by police in Harris County, Texas, reported that Oliver's son was 2 years old when he died. Police subsequently reported that the boy was 1 year old.
