articles.title: Top Potential Trade Packages and Landing Spots for Steelers' Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. could be heading for a breakup.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. could be heading for a breakup.

Last week, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the cornerback has been seen as a "potential trade target" for teams as he enters the final year of his rookie deal and has yet to receive a contract extension from the Steelers.

Head coach Mike McCarthy stopped short of ruling Porter out for Week 1.

Asked whether he needs to see the 26-year-old—who has missed all of training camp with a back injury—practice before clearing him to play, McCarthy instead pointed to the "impasse" between the team and its top corner, according to ESPN's Brooke Pryor .

Porter has maintained his desire to be compensated as a top-level corner, a position that has seen five players reach or eclipse the $30 million per year mark since the start of last offseason, including a record-setting four-year, $133 million contract for Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon.

While Porter probably won't reset the market, he's due for a major raise over the $4 million in base salary he's due in 2026. The corner has been a lynchpin in Pittsburgh's secondary since being drafted No. 32 overall in 2023. In that span, he has appeared in 41 games—starting 41—and recorded 165 tackles, 31 pass defenses and three interceptions.

Because the Steelers have a longstanding organizational policy to not negotiate contracts during the regular season, time is running out for Porter and the club to hammer out a new deal.

If the two sides can't reach a fair agreement—which Spotrac pegs to be in the range of $23-24 million annually, although likely to run a good bit higher when the corner eventually signs—before the team's 2026 NFL season-opener on September 13, it could lead to a shocking trade.

Although trading Porter away represents a worst-case scenario for the Steelers, far more shocking events have happened in the NFL. With that in mind, let's highlight some potential trade packages and landing spots for Porter.

Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks

Chicago Bears receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Chicago Bears go into the 2026 NFL season with hopes of building on a promising 11-6 campaign. Trading for Joey Porter Jr. would greatly assist in that endeavor, adding a top-flight corner to a roster that nearly reached the NFC Championship Game last year.

After ranking bottom-five in total defense and allowing a whopping 32 touchdowns through the air last year, Chicago brought in several veterans—including projected starter Coby Bryant—to reinforce the safety position.

While that should help shore up one of the weak points in the secondary, the club could still heavily benefit from adding a Pro Bowl-caliber corner.

The Bears do have one standout corner already in Jaylon Johnson, although he's maintained that 2026 is a contract year for him despite still having two seasons left on the four-year, $76 million deal he inked following a breakout 2023 campaign.

With Johnson's future with the organization uncertain, Chicago's brass could get ahead of a potential disastrous situation by acquiring Porter and locking him up on a long-term extension.

The rest of the cornerback room in the Windy City leaves something to be desired.

Tyrique Stevenson is serviceable when healthy but is now week-to-week with an injury . Rookie fourth-rounder Malik Muhammad II has potential to be an impact player, but is still a raw, developmental prospect.

Kyler Gordon's status is particularly concerning. Although he was a consistent starter for his first three years in the league, the 2022 second-rounder appeared in just three games last season and is set to open 2026 on the PUP list with a calf injury. It's an ailment that is reportedly frustrating the coaching staff and has led to a "standoff" per The Score's Matt Spiegel during an appearance on Fox 32 Chicago.

With so many question marks for this season and Johnson's status for 2027 and beyond already in doubt, Chicago should make the bold move to trade an upcoming second-round pick for Porter.

A starting cornerback tandem of Johnson and Porter would give the Bears a big leg up in what figures to be a brutally tough NFC North race, and the team needs all the help it can get if it wants to successfully defend its title.

Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 second- and fifth-round draft picks

Green Bay Packers receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Green Bay Packers are in the market for a new corner. According to Easton Butler of Packer Report, the club has inquired about the availability of several veteran defensive backs, a list that includes Kool-Aid McKinstry, Riley Moss and Joey Porter Jr.

Porter would be the splashiest acquisition Green Bay could make, but also the most impactful. He's a borderline Pro Bowler who can immediately slot into the starting lineup for an NFC North squad looking to make a leap in 2026 after back-to-back Wild Card round eliminations.

While Green Bay has a handful of solid veterans at the cornerback spot, none offer the same blend of age, upside and production that Porter provides.

The team's recent depth chart release showed Carrington Valentine and Keisean Nixon starting, with rookie second-rounder Brandon Cisse and Kitan Oladapo serving as backups. Porter represents a large upgrade and his presence alongside star safety Xavier McKinney would give the Packers one of the NFL's most formidable secondary units.

Nixon could potentially be included in a Porter trade as well, given that ESPN's Rob Demovsky called him the most likely candidate to be released or dealt if Green Bay opts for a "high-profile move on cutdown day."

Packaging him and a Day 2 pick would likely be enough to get Pittsburgh to move on from Porter if an extension can't be reached in the next few weeks.

Green Bay doesn't possess a first-rounder in the 2027 draft due to their blockbuster trade for Micah Parsons last year, but is sitting on a second-round selection and a pair of third-rounders.

There's enough capital here to get a deal done for Porter, who could be a long-term building block in Titletown by signing a long-term deal shortly after arriving.

Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 third- and fourth-round draft picks

Miami Dolphins receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Miami Dolphins are in the midst of a rebuild, but adding a star-caliber cornerback like Joey Porter Jr. could help expedite the process. The team is extremely thin in the secondary and is largely lacking impact veterans like Porter who could get the franchise trending in the right direction.

The 'Phins are set to head into the new season with 2025 fifth-rounder Jason Marshall Jr.—a backup on last year's squad—and JuJu Brents, another depth option who spent most of last season on IR, playing large roles alongside first-round rookie Chris Johnson.

The team has been shuffling the deck at the position throughout training camp, most recently parting ways with Nick McCloud and adding Ja'Onte' McMillan off waivers to bolster the position. It's clear that the team isn't satisfied with how the position is faring in the preseason, making a blockbuster trade for Porter a potential path forward.

While giving up draft picks, especially selections likely to fall towards the top of the order, isn't ideal for an organization that needs help at nearly every position, the opportunity to land a proven player of Porter's caliber may be too alluring to pass up.

New York Giants receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The New York Giants have had a transformational offseason and seem ready to emerge as a contender again after some lean years, but their cornerback position still appears to be a bit shaky.

Adding Joey Porter Jr. into the mix would massively improve the secondary and give Big Blue the elite defensive back it needs to contend with the talented NFC East wideouts it is set to come up against in 2026.

The G-Men head into the campaign with incumbent Paulson Adebo remaining a starter on the outside. He largely failed to live up to the three-year, $54 million deal he signed last offseason, earning a paltry 58.4 grade from Pro Football Focus for his lackluster efforts.

The prized free-agent pickup missed five games with injury and struggled when he was on the field—allowing a career-worst 66.3 percent completion rate in coverage .

Fellow veteran Greg Newsome II is projected to be New York's other starting outside corner, but there are legitimate concerns about his consistency after some up-and-down seasons. Rookie Colton Hood oozes potential and has flashed his upside during training camp, but tasking the inexperienced second-rounder with a large role this early could backfire.

Rather than hope Adebo and Newsome return to form and Hood comes out of the gate strong, the Giants could instead trade for Porter and instantly solidify the cornerback position.

Armed with a pair of Day 2 picks in the 2027 draft, the Giants could easily put a fair offer on the table for Porter's services. It's a bold move, but one New York shouldn't hesitate to make if it truly believes it's ready to return to Super Bowl contention under head coach John Harbaugh.

Rather than hope Adebo and Newsome return to form and Hood comes out of the gate strong, the Giants could instead trade for Porter and instantly solidify the cornerback position.

Armed with a pair of Day 2 picks in the 2027 draft, the Giants could easily put a fair offer on the table for Porter's services. It's a bold move, but one New York shouldn't hesitate to make if it truly believes it's ready to return to Super Bowl contention under head coach John Harbaugh.

articles.title: Hallan encefalopatía traumática en 25% de exjugadores muertos de la NFL
articles.summary: Golpes en la cabeza recibidos desde la etapa juvenil acumulan un efecto que termina por ser mortal en jugadores de fútbol americano, sugiere el estudio.
articles.body:
Según un estudio publicado el martes, se determinó que al menos uno de cada cuatro exjugadores de la NFL de fútbol americano fallecidos entre 2016 y 2021 padecía encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC). De los 878 exjugadores que murieron en ese periodo, 235 donaron sus cerebros; los investigadores hallaron ETC en 215 de ellos. La ETC es una enfermedad degenerativa que solo puede diagnosticarse de manera definitiva tras la muerte .

Detrás de cada porcentaje hay historias de deportistas que dedicaron años a competir al máximo nivel. El estudio vuelve a poner el foco en una pregunta que ha perseguido al fútbol americano durante décadas: ¿cuál es el costo a largo plazo de los golpes repetidos en la cabeza ?

Un portavoz de la NFL declaró: "La NFL se esfuerza continuamente por hacer que el fútbol americano sea más seguro, incluso mediante la implementación de estrategias para reducir las conmociones cerebrales y los impactos en la cabeza.

" La NFL mantiene su compromiso de garantizar que la comunidad de la liga tenga acceso a un conjunto sólido —y en expansión— de recursos para mejorar su bienestar físico y mental.

"Animamos a los exjugadores a utilizar estos recursos para identificar problemas y buscar tratamiento cuando les preocupe su salud".

El autor principal del estudio, Daniel Daneshvar —jefe de medicina física y rehabilitación en Mass General Brigham y profesor asociado de la Facultad de Medicina de Harvard—, señaló que las lesiones cerebrales traumáticas recurrentes son un factor conocido en las elevadas tasas de enfermedades neurodegenerativas.

"Asimismo, nosotros y otros investigadores hemos demostrado que, específicamente entre los jugadores de la NFL, la tasa de mortalidad por enfermedades neurodegenerativas es unas cuatro veces mayor que en la población general", añadió.

El estudio, realizado por Mass General Brigham, la Universidad de Boston y la Concussion & CTE Foundation, también reveló que la demencia era frecuente entre los donantes de cerebro; por ello, los investigadores instaron a adoptar medidas preventivas centradas en reducir los impactos repetitivos en la cabeza en todos los niveles de este deporte.

"La mayor parte de los impactos en la cabeza que sufrieron estos exjugadores de la NFL no ocurrieron en el nivel profesional, sino en el universitario... y en el de secundaria, e incluso, en muchos casos, en categorías juveniles. Todos esos golpes acumulados en la cabeza se sumaron para dar lugar a un mayor riesgo", afirmó Daneshvar.

Uno de los hallazgos más llamativos es que el riesgo no se concentra únicamente en la élite deportiva. Según los investigadores, la exposición acumulada comienza años antes de llegar a la NFL, lo que amplía el debate sobre la seguridad de millones de jóvenes que practican este deporte.

El convenio colectivo de la NFL de 2011 limitó el número de entrenamientos con contacto durante la temporada. Cinco años más tarde, la Ivy League prohibió los placajes de contacto total durante los entrenamientos. La Corte Suprema allanó el camino para que la NFL concretara en 2016 el acuerdo de conciliación de las demandas relacionadas con las conmociones cerebrales presentadas por miles de jugadores retirados.

"Si los cambios implementados en la NFL —incluida la reducción de la cantidad de contacto en los entrenamientos a menos de una sesión por semana— se extendieran a los niveles universitario, de escuela secundaria y juvenil, los deportistas saldrían beneficiados", afirmó Daneshvar, quien instó a los atletas actuales y retirados que presenten síntomas cognitivos a buscar una evaluación por parte de un especialista en enfermedades neurodegenerativas. " Sabemos que casi el 70 % de los impactos en la cabeza se producen durante los entrenamientos . Por lo tanto, sin modificar ni un solo minuto de tiempo de juego en ninguno de esos niveles, podemos reducir considerablemente la carga acumulada de impactos en la cabeza que estas personas sufren a lo largo de su vida".

Por lo tanto, sin modificar ni un solo minuto de tiempo de juego en ninguno de esos niveles, podemos reducir considerablemente la carga acumulada de impactos en la cabeza que estas personas sufren a lo largo de su vida".

Mientras los investigadores insisten en que muchos de estos impactos pueden prevenirse, la discusión ya no gira únicamente en torno al rendimiento deportivo, sino al equilibrio entre la pasión por un deporte de contacto y la protección de la salud cerebral a largo plazo. ¿Hasta dónde deberían llegar los cambios para reducir ese riesgo?

articles.title: NFL reveals 2026 Rivalries uniforms for AFC South, NFC North teams
articles.summary: The uniforms will remain a part of the team's rotation for the next three seasons.
articles.body:
The NFL is bringing back rivalry uniforms for the upcoming 2026 season.

After launching the NFL's Rivalries program in 2025, the league has teamed up with Nike and revealed the uniforms the eight teams in the AFC South and NFC North will wear against division rivals this season. Following the on-field debut, the Rivalries uniforms will be a part of the team's rotation for three years along with its existing looks.

Those teams that wore Rivalries uniforms last season will wear them for a game against a divisional rival in 2026. More teams will join the program during the 2027 and 2028 seasons.

Indianapolis Colts : Week 3 vs. Houston Texans

Green Bay Packers : Week 5 vs. Chicago Bears

Detroit Lions : Week 8 vs. Minnesota Vikings

Jacksonville Jaguars : Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts

Tennessee Titans : Week 10 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Houston Texans: Week 11 vs. Indianapolis Colts

Minnesota Vikings: Week 15 vs. Detroit Lions

Chicago Bears: Week 16 vs. Green Bay Packers

The eight NFL teams who were part of the initial launch last season will wear them again in 2026, including the Seahawks and Rams , who will face each other in Week 16 wearing their Rivalries uniforms.

Arizona Cardinals : Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks Buffalo Bills : Week 11 vs. Miami Dolphins New England : Week 13 vs. Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers : Week 14 vs. Los Angeles Rams Seattle Seahawks: Week 16 vs. Los Angeles Rams Los Angeles Rams: Week 16 vs. Seattle Seahawks New York Jets : Week 16 vs. New England Patriots Miami Dolphins: Week 17 vs. Buffalo Bills

In 2027, the AFC West and NFC East will be part of the program, and the AFC North and NFC South will join in 2028.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson Sr. to Start Colts' Preseason Finale amid NFL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. will get one last chance to impress potential trade suitors later this week.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. will get one last chance to impress potential trade suitors later this week.

Per ESPN's Stephen Holder , Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced on Tuesday that Richardson will be the starting quarterback for the team's preseason finale against the Detroit Lions on Saturday.

Holder added that the Colts' starters will likely play "a series or two," though quarterback Daniel Jones and running back Jonathan Taylor will remain on the sidelines. Jones is still targeting a Week 1 return as he recovers from a torn Achilles.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Richardson started Indianapolis' preseason opener against the New England Patriots but played the second half in last week's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Across the two appearances, he completed 14 of his 23 passes for 169 yards and an interception while also rushing for 68 yards and one touchdown.

The No. 4 pick in the 2023 draft should be motivated to go out with a bang on Saturday against the Lions. Richardson requested to be traded this offseason, but Colts general manager Chris Ballard told reporters last month that the team is "not going to give him away."

Despite the lackluster start to his career and the ongoing trade rumors, Richardson expressed optimism that he would be able to produce for the Colts if they retain him and he has to step in for Jones.

"I'm just looking forward to helping the team," Richardson told Holder . "They truly believe that I still have a chance to be on this squad, and I love that. I just want to be able to contribute."

articles.title: Shilo Sanders mother: âIf thatâs not one-sidedâ¦ you have to be blind, dumb, crazy, and stupidâ - Pilar Sandersâ marriage, divorce, and custody battles with Deion Sanders
articles.summary: NFL News: Pilar Sanders met her husband, Super Bowl-winning legendary cornerback Deion Sanders, in the mid-1990s while she was involved in acting.The couple beg.
articles.body: Pilar Sanders met her husband, Super Bowl-winning legendary cornerback Deion Sanders, in the mid-1990s while she was involved in acting.The couple began dating and married in May 1999.Pilar welcomed her first son, Shilo Sanders, in 2001, when she was 27.Two years later, she and Deion welcomed their second son, Shedeur Sanders, in 2003. Their daughter, Shelomi Sanders, was born in 2004.Pilar and Deion Sandersâ reality TV appearancesIn 2008, Pilar and Deion Sanders starred in the Oxygen reality television series Deion and Pilar: Prime Time Love.The show focused on their family and home life, but it was canceled after receiving low ratings.Pilar later appeared on VH1âs Football Wives in 2010.The reality series followed the personal lives and relationships of women married to current and former professional football players.Deion Sanders filed for divorce in 2011The coupleâs marriage took a dramatic turn in 2011 when Deion filed for divorce.According to Celebrity Net Worth, he cited infidelity in the filing and did not inform Pilar directly. She reportedly learned about the divorce through TMZ.The divorce proceedings soon developed into a highly publicized custody and financial dispute involving their three children.Pilar Sanders and Deion Sandersâ custody battleAccording to Net Worth Post, the civil court proceedings following the divorce included claims involving $14,000 per month for child support and mortgage payments,as well as a 24,000 dollar bill including such items as $2,000 for childrenâs lessons, $2,000 for food and restaurants,$1,000 for entertainment and events, $900 for clothing, $750 for child care, $500 for school lunches, $500 for cell phones and $450 for personal care and haircuts.CBS News reported at the time that Deion openly laughed in the courtroom when Pilar estimated his net worth at $250,000,000, and demanded $24,000 a month in payments.The court initially awarded custody of the children to Deion, meaning Pilar did not receive the amounts she had requested.Deion was ordered to pay $275,000 toward her attorneysâ fees. Pilar was granted visitation rights.Pilar Sanders was jailed over the custody disputeThe custody dispute continued for several years.In December 2014, Leahy Cox reported that, according to Deion, Pilar had violated their custody agreement 16 times by keeping the children longer than she was permitted to.On one occasion, she reportedly kept them for more than a week, prompting outside assistance.After Deion petitioned the court to enforce and modify the custody agreement, the former couple appeared in court.Pilar reportedly argued that she did not recognize the courtâs jurisdiction and, therefore, did not follow the custody arrangement.The court granted Deionâs requested modification. Pilar subsequently lost access to her children and was ordered to serve seven days in jail, followed by a year of probation, for contempt of court.The custody battle continued after the divorceThe custody dispute continued even after the coupleâs marriage ended. Pilar was later granted joint custody of some of their children.The former couple also became involved in other legal disputes.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Pilar alleged that domestic violence had occurred during their marriage, while Deion denied the allegations and sued her for defamation.Their conflict became increasingly public as both sides discussed the dispute on social media.When did Pilar and Deion Sanders divorce?After 13 years of marriage, Pilar and Deion Sanders ended their relationship. Their divorce was finalized in June 2013.Following the lengthy and contentious divorce proceedings, Deion was ordered to pay Pilar $10,500 per month in child and spousal support payments and a $3,500 mortgage payment for Pilarâs new home.The former coupleâs highly publicized marriage, divorce, and custody battle remained a significant part of their family history, particularly because they share three children: Shilo, Shedeur, and Shelomi Sanders.Pilar Sanders called the custody decision crazyPilar Sanders was not happy with the courtâs decision. The NFL Hall of Fame cornerback, Deion Sanders, was awarded full custody of their two sons, Shedeur and Shilo, while he and Pilar shared custody of their only daughter, Shelomi.Pilar pointed to several pieces of evidence that she said were not admitted during the proceedings.She called the decision prejudiced and said, âIf thatâs not one-sidedâ¦ you have to be blind, dumb, crazy, and stupid.âDeion said in court that his only goals were for his children to have a normal life, go to college, earn degrees, and become successful individuals.Pilar argued that she had been the primary parent when Deion traveled for work. articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Dynasty Rankings, Cheat Sheet and League Names
articles.summary: While re-draft fantasy football leagues treat each NFL season as their own, unique stories, dynasty leagues are different.
articles.body:
While re-draft fantasy football leagues treat each NFL season as their own, unique stories, dynasty leagues are different.

In a dynasty format, NFL campaigns become mere chapters of a years-long (or, for the real sickos like myself, decades-long) journey.

As such, everything needs adjusting—rankings, position values, draft approaches and even the general character of the league as conveyed through its name. If you're a dynasty-drafter preparing for the upcoming season, we're here to help with overall dynasty rankings, cheat sheet positional breakdowns and finally tips for crafting the right league name.

What's in a name? Well, for fantasy football leagues, quite a bit actually. Or plenty if you craft the right one, at least.

Step one is nailing down the tone and the theme. Do you want something serious and official sounding, or are you going for a chuckle? Then, figure out if you're going for a general, perhaps openly inviting name—newcomers won't feel like they're missing a joke if they're joining the Waiver Warriors or Armchair Experts, for instance—or if you want something more specific. If specifics are the aim, look for something you share, like a location and maybe a specific NFL allegiance, for instance. Say you're all Green Bay Packers fans, then maybe collectively you're the Lambeau Leapers Collective (LLC, for short).

Or maybe you all came together as fans of movies, video games or even non-football sports. If you're a bunch of Marvel fans, maybe the league is as simple as The Multiverse. For old-school gamers, you might be the Tecmo Bowl All-Stars. If baseball is a shared first love, maybe it's The Extra Innings Endzone.

Only you, of course, know the particulars with your league mates, so you'll know better than us what actually works best. But, honestly, give this some real thought. It might seem like such an afterthought when putting a league together, but it can be a legitimate point of pride. And if it gives your league an edge over others played in by fellow managers, that can lead to a more eventful and therefore enjoyable experience.

articles.title: Predicting When Malik Nabers, More Injured NFL Stars Will Make 2026 NFL Debut
articles.summary: The start of the 2026 NFL season is only a few short weeks away, but there won't be a full compliment of stars available when teams take the field in Week 1. Several of the league's top names are still working their way back from injuries picked up both last year and during the offseason.
articles.body:
The start of the 2026 NFL season is only a few short weeks away, but there won't be a full compliment of stars available when teams take the field in Week 1. Several of the league's top names are still working their way back from injuries picked up both last year and during the offseason.

While some of these marquee players have begun practicing in recent weeks, others have yet to be cleared and could be sidelined for an extensive stretch. Most teams have been understandably vague when discussing timelines for potential returns, leaving fans to sift through clues and guess when these headliners will return.

With that in mind, let's highlight some of the NFL's biggest stars who still don't have a concrete timetable to return from a significant injury and predict when they will make their 2026 debut.

George Kittle remains an integral piece of the San Francisco 49ers' offensive plans, but the team has been preparing to go without their veteran tight end and leader for a stretch due to the torn Achilles he suffered back in January. That absence isn't likely to linger beyond the first month of the 2026 NFL season, however, as Kittle has been activated off the PUP list and is trending towards a September return.

The 49ers announced the move on Sunday, with Kittle sitting out team drills but still suiting up in full pads and easing into things with individual work. Had the nine-year veteran remained on the PUP list through cutdown day on August 30, he would have needed to miss the first four games at a minimum.

Kittle has long maintained that he wanted to be ready for San Francisco's much-anticipated opener against the rival Los Angeles Rams, set to take place in Melbourne, Australia on September 11. He's kept that as his desired return date, but recently admitted missing one game during the grind of a long season won't be too devastating.

"I want to play in every football game that I possibly can play in but I'm also aware it's an 18-week season," Kittle said earlier this month (via ESPN's Nick Wagoner ). "If you miss Week 1 and you're playing Week 2, hey, it is what it is. I'm just going to keep that as my goal and then we'll adjust from there if we need to."

Even if he's medically cleared, given the unconventional preparations and lengthy travel involved with San Francisco's opening contest—the team plans to arrive in Australia over a week before kickoff to help players and staff acclimate to a 17-hour time difference—it would make sense for Kittle to delay his return slightly.

The team will settle back into a conventional routine after returning stateside, benefitting from a three-game homestand that begins with a Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. If he ends up sitting out Week 1, expect Kittle to make his 2026 debut during this contest.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 2 vs. Miami Dolphins

The Arizona Cardinals went all-in on overhauling a lackluster and injury-prone running back platoon by selecting Jeremiyah Love at No. 3 overall in the 2026 NFL draft. While Love is still expected to be the focal point of the rebuilding program's offense, his chances of jumping out to a fast start took a major hit when he suffered a high-ankle sprain during his first preseason outing.

Love's injury ended what was a promising 11-carry, 58-yard debut on a sour note. Shortly after the contest ended, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that that the Notre Dame product was likely going to be held out the remainder of the preseason with the hopes of getting healthy in time for the regular season opener on September 13.

It seems that the Cardinals are sticking to the plan Schefter initially reported. Arizona Sports' Tyler Drake provided an update on Love, stating he's making "steady progress" in his recovery but will remain out of practice this week. The Cardinals are slated to take on the Green Bay Packers in the preseason finale on Friday, which follows a joint practice session on Wednesday.

With head coach Mike LaFleur confirming that Love won't be suiting up for any activity this week, it's fair to wonder whether the rising star will actually be ready by Week 1.

The Cardinals would be wise to take an extremely cautious approach with a player set to be a building block for years to come, especially with the amount of depth they've accumulated in the backfield. With incumbent James Conner and free-agent pickup Tyler Allgeier in the mix, Arizona doesn't need to rush the rookie into action if he's not fully healthy.

Given the strength of this platoon coupled with the four-week timetable for recovery from this type of injury, it isn't worth pushing Love into the lineup for Week 1 if he's not 100 percent. Missing an entire week of practice won't help the rookie's case either, so it's more reasonable to expect him to make his NFL debut when the defending champion Seattle Seahawks come to town in Week 2.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks

Malik Nabers' absence for much of the offseason has been one of the more enigmatic stories swirling around head coach John Harbaugh's inaugural season with the New York Giants.

The superstar wideout went down with a severe knee injury in late-September of last year and underwent surgery for the issue approximately one month later. Nabers also had another procedure done earlier this year to clear out scar tissue and address stiffness issues. He only recently returned to practice, initially wearing a no-contact red jersey before shedding it and going on to participate in several 11-on-11 drills earlier this week.

While that training camp activity seems to indicate that Nabers will be ready to go when the G-Men open their 2026 NFL season against the Dallas Cowboys on September 13, Harbaugh only hinted it would be "reasonable to assume" the receiver will be active.

"The only thing I know more than you guys know is what the doctors and trainers tell me as far as his rehab," Harbaugh said Monday , ". And that is he's doing well. He's doing well with that. He's strong, in a good place. How he gets through practice, how ready he is to play and protect himself is really based on practice."

Nabers made one impressive grab during Monday's practice session but also had a drop and was whistled for a false start. While those moments aren't ideal, it's tough to envision the 2024 Pro Bowler failing to make a positive impact upon his much-anticipated return. New York's receiving corps has a good mix of solid veterans and promising young pieces, but none have the ceiling a healthy Nabers provides.

If he's medically cleared and able, Nabers will suit up and play against the Cowboys. He's far too important to Big Blue's 2026 chances to miss any time he's healthy enough to see.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 1 vs. Dallas Cowboys

One of the Indianapolis Colts' biggest offseason moves was to issue a massive contract extension to burgeoning wideout Alec Pierce. While the team paid Pierce on the heels of his best season yet—a 47-catch, 1,003-yard, six-touchdown effort—there are expectations for an expanded role attached to the four-year, $114 million deal.

Considering Pierce has yet to suit up for a training camp practice, the chances of the four-year veteran quickly adapting to this larger role look bleaker than ever. The wideout has been plagued by a lingering ankle injury since late in the 2024 season, attempting to treat the issue with a platelet-rich plasma injection early in the offseason before opting for surgery.

Back in June, Pierce spoke about how the ankle progressed last year and seemed happy to finally have it addressed.

"It definitely got a little bit worse as the (2025) season went," Pierce said. "Probably the last month I'd say I was kind of struggling – (it) affected practice, I'd taken some days off. I'm glad they figured out what the issue was and we were able to fix it."

Pierce's recovery has been slow, as he underwent the procedure in the spring and has since missed all of OTAs and training camp. The Colts initially expected him back in early-August, as Rotowire's Ian Hartitz pointed out that it's now been a month since the club projected a one-to-two week timeline for his return.

According to The Athletic's James Boyd , head coach Shane Steichen confirmed that Pierce wouldn't be back in action on Tuesday, but is still hopeful the wideout can suit up at some point during the coming week.

With little in the way of proven weapons outside of Josh Downs and aging free-agent pickup Keenan Allen to lean on during Pierce's absence, the Colts need Pierce to get back on the field and pick up his new role as soon as possible. Even if Pierce doesn't get many practice reps under his belt, expect Steichen—likely coaching for his job in 2026—to thrust the wideout into action and have him learn on the fly.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 1 vs. Baltimore Ravens

The New Orleans Saints' Jordyn Tyson is set to miss extensive time after going down with a hamstring issue during a joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this month.

Tyson is one of the more promising pass-catchers to enter the league in years, but his selection at No. 8 overall raised eyebrows due to health-related red flags surrounding the prospect. The Arizona State product missed a myriad of games at the previous level, including 11 contests stemming from an ACL tear and three games last season with a hamstring strain.

While Tyson is undeniably tough—notably gritting through multiple hamstring issues to lead Arizona State with 10 catches, 105 yards and a score in a win over Texas Tech last October—he's set to miss approximately half of his rookie season while recovering from his latest injury.

Per ESPN's Katherine Terell , the hamstring injury that Tyson suffered while landing awkwardly after a catch is different in nature to the one that plagued him during his final collegiate season. Head coach Kellen Moore revealed that the previous injury also didn't play a role in causing or worsening the current one.

Prior to the injury, Tyson had been a near-full participant in practices—only avoiding one-on-one drills against defensive backs in an effort to preserve his health and get him up to full strength for his rookie campaign.

With Tyson on the shelf until approximately mid-October at a minimum, a Week 5 return at home against the Minnesota Vikings would be the earliest reasonably expect him back. New Orleans' scheduling isn't too favorable for this target date, however, as the team visits the New York Giants in Week 6 and travels all the way to Paris to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 7 before a Week 8 bye.

Rather than rush Tyson back, have him travel to Europe and chance yet another injury to a player with incredible upside, it would behoove the Saints to keep their prized rookie on ice until a Week 9 bout against the Cleveland Browns at the Superdome.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 9 vs. Cleveland Browns

articles.title: George Pickens' Trash Talk From Cowboys-Saints Joint Practice Revealed in New Mic'd Up Video
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys star receiver George Pickens wasn't shy about letting his voice be heard in last week's joint practice with the New Orleans Saints.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys star receiver George Pickens wasn't shy about letting his voice be heard in last week's joint practice with the New Orleans Saints.

The Cowboys released new videos with Pickens mic'd up during the practice session, and the 2025 Pro Bowler let his trash talk fly:

Pickens is coming off the best year of his young career, but he wasn't signed to the big-money extension he was expecting this offseason. It's safe to say that the 25-year-old is motivated to dominate even more when he takes the field in 2026.

The Cowboys will close out the preseason against the Saints on Friday before opening the year against the New York Giants on Sunday Night Football on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Bill Belichick sends clear message on Steve Belichickâs UNC absence as defensive play calling decision looms
articles.summary: NFL News: Bill Belichick says he is ready to step in if North Carolina needs him to handle defensive play calling while his son, Steve Belichick, remains on med.
articles.body: Bill Belichick says he is ready to step in if North Carolina needs him to handle defensive play calling while his son, Steve Belichick, remains on medical leave. With UNC set to open the 2026 season against TCU in Dublin on August 29, there is still no update on Steveâs return. Bill did not confirm who will call the defense, but made it clear he feels prepared if the job falls to him.Bill Belichick addresses Steve Belichickâs UNC defensive roleDuring his August 24 news conference, Bill Belichick was asked whether he could take over defensive play calling if Steve is unavailable. articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Picks in 2-Round Mock Draft and Top Keeper Rankings Advice
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL season nearing its opening kick, it's almost keeper-submission time for fantasy football managers.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL season nearing its opening kick, it's almost keeper-submission time for fantasy football managers.

While your specific league may require you to weigh thinks like draft-round or salary-cap costs, the general goal is keeping as much talent as possible.

It isn't always as simple as it sounds, though, so you might have come here seeking a few road signs to take you to title town. That's exactly what we have here in the form of a two-round mock draft, dynasty rankings and keeper advice.

This might be the most obvious advice you will hear, but it's also the most important. Because each keeper league has its own set of rules, you need to know exactly what they are, so you can apply them to the general advice you'll find in a place like this.

Universal rankings can be helpful, but they may not settle your debates. If your league uses a salary cap or attaches draft-pick costs to keepers, that changes things a lot. That third-round sleeper you found last season may not look as appealing this year if they jump to a second- or even first-round cost, for instance.

If you keep a big chunk of your roster, then you should have a pretty decent idea of your championship chances this season. Use those odds—the realistic ones, not the optimistic ones that only exist in a best-case scenario—to steer your draft decisions.

Win-right-now rosters need instant-impact, so you'd want to prioritize proven veterans over dart-throw rookies. Long-term rebuilders, on the other hand, have no use for 30-somethings, but they should be collecting as many long-term lottery tickets as possible. It only takes one jackpot prize or two to instantly change your team's trajectory.

articles.title: Dolly Partonâs final message to Travis Kelce is breaking hearts after her death
articles.summary: NFL News: Dolly Parton has died at 80. Her family confirmed she \"died peacefully today in Nashville\" after dealing with health issues for the past few years, an.
articles.body: Dolly Parton has died at 80. Her family confirmed she "died peacefully today in Nashville" after dealing with health issues for the past few years, and no cause of death has been shared yet. And one of her last public moments with Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift is hitting harder now. This one clip, from just weeks ago, where she made a joke about wanting Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's future baby, is doing the rounds for a different reason now.When Dolly Parton joked she wanted Travis Kelce's firstborn, and why that memory now hits so hardBack in early July, Kelce and Swift donated $2 million to Dolly's Imagination Library, as part of a $26 million round of giving to charities tied to cities that mattered to them, announced right before their Madison Square Garden wedding.Dolly didn't just thank them quietly. She filmed a video, saying, "Taylor and Travis, it's Dolly, and I was just told that you two are making a donation of two million dollars to my Imagination Library. Thank you, thank you, thank you," before turning the moment into pure Dolly comedy, joking she wanted their firstborn because "that is gonna be one special baby." Then she sang "I Will Always Love You" straight into the camera, aimed right at them.It was funny then. It's something else entirely now. A woman who spent her whole life turning warmth into a punchline, gifting one more piece of herself to a couple she'd probably never met in person, that's the kind of thing you don't get to see twice.Remembering Dolly, beyond the jokeShe started out singing in church, was on local radio and TV by 13, and made her Grand Ole Opry debut around that same age, where she met Johnny Cash. From there she built one of the great crossover careers in music, releasing dozens of albums and winning 11 Grammys.But the Imagination Library, the same program Kelce and Swift just backed, was always the part of her legacy that felt closest to her heart. It wasn't about the music. It was about kids she'd never meet, getting books they'd never have gotten otherwise.Her family has asked that, instead of flowers, donations go to that same Imagination Library. Fitting, really. Even her goodbye is pointed at the same thing that clip was about - kids, books, and a kind of love that outlasts the person giving it.Kelce and Swift's $2 million didn't just fund a program. It funded a promise Dolly made a long time ago, one she's now handed off for good.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fans think Tom Brady is after Gisele BÃ¼ndchen's job after his latest Instagram post
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady didn't learn his lesson. He committed to it instead. He just posted pictures on Instagram from his latest Gucci campaign: a full leather get.
articles.body: Tom Brady didn't learn his lesson. He committed to it instead. He just posted pictures on Instagram from his latest Gucci campaign: a full leather getup. GQ dropped an exclusive calling Bradyâs look "a leather pants guy at 49," built around his new Gucci Primavera campaign, and the New York Post ran a nearly identical headline within the hour, pairing his new campaign portrait with his May runway look. Side by side, the two photos are basically twins: same all-black leather, same stiff-shouldered pose, same "I dare you to laugh" expression.Tom Brady got roasted for leather pants in May and now he's doing it on purposeBack in May, Brady made his runway debut at Gucci's Cruise 2027 show in Times Square, and fans did not go easy on him. Fans said he walked like RoboCop, compared him to the Terminator, and joked he looked like "Tom BÃ¼ndchen," a dig at ex-wife Gisele building an entire modeling career while Brady, famously, wouldn't hang up his cleats for her.One viral tweet asked, "Divorce cause he wouldn't quit his job but now he wants to do hers????" Antonio Brown, never one to pass up a free shot at his old quarterback, called the look straight-up a "Terminator villain." The internet had a field day, and Brady, to his credit, said nothing back.And now he's doing it again, deliberatelyMost people who get compared to a sci-fi robot online quietly change their stylist. Brady went back to Gucci for a full ad campaign instead, sitting for the exact same leather-on-leather look, this time as one of 10 faces in creative director Demna's debut Primavera campaign alongside Kate Moss, Shawn Mendes, and BTS's Jin.He's photographed seated in a chair, floral wallpaper behind him, leather jacket and trousers on, looking every bit as serious as he did on that Times Square runway three months ago. If the May jokes stung, nothing about this new shoot suggests he cared.It's rare that a meme survives long enough to become the actual headline, but Brady's stiff runway walk did exactly that.Say what you want about the RoboCop jokes, but the man just turned the roasts into publicity, and quite a bit of style. That's not damage control, that's a rebrand. Brady spent 23 years being mocked for looking robotic in a pocket under pressure. Now he's getting mocked for looking robotic in leather pants, and somehow it's landed him a Gucci campaign instead of a playoff loss.Get roasted in May, get immortalized in leather by August. Very on-brand for a guy who's never once looked embarrassed about anything in his life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rams' Sean McVay Jokes About NFL Players Returning to CFB Amid Dae'Quan Wright-LSU Buzz
articles.summary: We live in interesting times, especially when it comes to the world of college football eligibility. Just ask Sean McVay.
articles.body:
We live in interesting times, especially when it comes to the world of college football eligibility. Just ask Sean McVay.

"I feel like I took a freakin' gummy," the Los Angeles Rams head coach told reporters when asked about NFL players returning to the college game after Dae'Quan Wright joined LSU on the transfer portal following short stints with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns this summer.

Wright was one of several athletes who sued for restraining orders that would allow them to play in college for a fifth season. The NCAA granted five years of eligibility over the course of five years going forward in a new ruling this offseason but didn't grandfather in athletes who started college during the 2022-23 academic year. In Louisiana, however, a judge granted such athletes a temporary restraining order that allowed them that fifth year of eligibility.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Wright signed with the Eagles this offseason as an undrafted free agent and suited up for the Browns in a preseason game, though he didn't play. That made his return to college quite controversial, though it's also—at least for the moment—completely legal.

articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce gave two young fans a moment they are unlikely to forget after noticing them in the stands during the Kansas City Chiefsâ preseason game..
articles.body: Travis Kelce gave two young fans a moment they are unlikely to forget after noticing them in the stands during the Kansas City Chiefsâ preseason game. The Chiefs star waved back when he saw the girls, then took off the gloves he had worn during the game and handed them to a team employee for the fans. The girls were thrilled when they received them and quickly returned to their seats to look at the gloves. The gloves also had personal words written inside, making the surprise gift even more special for the young fans.Travis Kelce spots two young fans and gives them his game glovesThe moment was captured in a video shared on TikTok by Ali Kay. Kelce was on the sideline when he noticed the two girls waving at him from the stands. He waved back, and their reaction showed how excited they were to get his attention.Kelce then made the gesture that turned the brief interaction into something much bigger for the girls. He removed his gloves and passed them to a team employee, who took them over to the young fans.Once they received the gloves, the girls immediately ran back to their seats to check out what Kelce had given them. The gloves were not simply a pair of unused items from the Chiefs. They were the ones Kelce had worn during the game.The gloves also carried two personal inscriptions: âHeights Nativeâ and âKilla Trav.â Those details gave the gift an added connection to Kelce and made the keepsake more meaningful for the girls.The video showed the girlsâ excitement as they realized Kelce had not only noticed them but had also decided to give them something he had used during the game.Travis Kelceâs gesture leaves two young fans thrilledKay, who shared the video, explained in the caption how much the moment meant to her niece and her friend.âTravis Kelce is the sweetest to his fans!â Kay wrote.She added: âMy niece and her friendâs lives were made last night at the preseason game when Kelce gave them his gloves he played in the game with.âThe post focused on the simple exchange between Kelce and the two young fans: a wave from the sideline, followed by an unexpected gift that they could take home.The moment also drew positive reactions from people who watched the video. For the two girls, though, the biggest part was getting something directly from one of the Kansas City Chiefsâ biggest stars.Kelceâs decision to hand over his game-worn gloves turned a few seconds of interaction in the stands into a lasting memory. The inscriptions inside the gloves meant the girls were taking home something closely tied to the Chiefs tight end himself, rather than an ordinary piece of team merchandise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Christian Gonzalez Discusses 'Frustrating' Patriots Contract Talks, Noncommittal on Week 1 Status
articles.summary: Christian Gonzalez is certainly frustrated to have not reached an extension with the New England Patriots, but he said Tuesday that his focus is on the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
Christian Gonzalez is certainly frustrated to have not reached an extension with the New England Patriots, but he said Tuesday that his focus is on the 2026 campaign.

"It's frustrating, but I'm focused on the season," Gonzalez told reporters about his contract situation. "I'm focused on here now."

He also was a bit noncommittal when asked whether the contract situation could impact his status for Week 1.

His comments come after Patriots executive vice president Eliot Wolf said the two sides are continuing to have talks about a new deal.

"Each side is trying to do what's right for them. Christian is a tremendous player that we've been on record multiple times saying we want him to be here, and that hasn't changed," he said . "We're going to continue working with his representation to try to get something done."

Gonzalez is entering the final year of his rookie deal, though the Patriots picked up his $18.1 million club option for the 2027 season.

Gonzalez is coming off a tremendous year in which he recorded 69 tackles and 10 pass breakups to earn his first Pro Bowl selection. With Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon resetting the market with a deal that pays him $33 million per year, Gonzalez figures to command a similar number as well.

articles.title: UCLA suggests star transfer Trent Hendrick isn't impacted by new Big Ten NFL player ban
articles.summary: UCLA athletics director Martin Jarmond released a statement that school is complying with all Big Ten rules and all players on its roster are eligible.
articles.body:
UCLA is proceeding as though it landed a massive gift this week, with 2025 Sun Belt player of the year Trent Hendrick joining the Bruins for practices Monday and Tuesday.

Hendrick is among 16 players who sought a Louisiana temporary restraining order allowing them to return to college after entering the NFL draft pool, arguing they would not have left had they know NCAA rules would change granting them an extra year of eligibility.

The temporary restraining order was granted last week, but the Big Ten voted on Tuesday to pass a new rule that prohibited football players who have signed a professional contract, were on a professional roster at any point or declared for the NFL draft as an underclassman without withdrawing, from maintaining eligibility for athletic competition.

Hendrick went undrafted and participated in rookie minicamps with the Cleveland Browns and Kansas City Chiefs , but the linebacker never signed with a team and didn't leave school early to enter the NFL draft.

He also never earned a spot on a roster.

"We support the Big Ten's adoption of the new professional football players rule and understand the importance of having clear and consistent eligibility standards across the conference," UCLA athletic director Martin Jarmond said in a statement on Tuesday. "We have been in communication with the Big Ten throughout this process, and our student-athletes are eligible under the guidelines adopted today. We are excited to turn our full attention to the upcoming season and our opener [versus] California on Sept. 5."

It is unclear whether anyone will contest the Louisiana temporary restraining order.

For now, Hendrick is quickly getting up to speed in a system he learned while competing under head coach Bob Chesney and defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler last season at James Madison.

Chesney was excited on Monday to welcome Hendrick to Westwood. Hitschler told reporters Tuesday he, too, was pleased to see Hendrick on the UCLA roster.

"We had a lot of fun together last year and I think he did a great job where he was," Hitschler said. "I'm glad he got the opportunity for himself to hopefully continue to play college football here. What a special opportunity for him and let's make the most of it."

Both coaches said they faced competition to land Hendrick after last week's restraining order was granted.

The Big Ten is holding schools accountable for compliance with its rule and told the Associated Press restrictions in other sports such as basketball could follow.

A head football coach who plays a former pro will be suspended 50% of the season and his school will be fined, the Big Ten confirmed to the AP on Tuesday.

The topic is a hot one around college athletics. Wake Forest athletic director John Currie, chairman of the Atlantic Coast Conference athletic directors group for the upcoming season, said his colleagues planned to discuss the issue Wednesday.

"I don't think anybody in our league likes the idea of taking away opportunities from existing college students and graduating high school players, which is exactly what is happening when a school signs a player out of an NFL camp to their team," Currie wrote in a text message to the AP.

Duke coach Manny Diaz said the Power Four conferences need to present a unified front. The Southeastern Conference passed a rule later Tuesday banning players who have been drafted by NFL, NBA or WNBA teams or listed on rosters in those leagues.

"I think you'll see more leagues start to govern themselves since we're having such a hard time finding it at a national level," Diaz said. "I think everyone understands it's absolutely absurd. We can enjoy the fact that the players can benefit financially from playing in college now. At the same time, recognize the ultimate truth that we're not a professional sports franchise. We are a collegiate, scholastic school activity, and we've got to rein that in."

Agent Drew Rosenhaus told the AP on Monday that former Mississippi tight end Dae'Quan Wright had been waived by the Cleveland Browns and, if he clears waivers, will join Lane Kiffin's roster at Louisiana State. Wright played two seasons for Kiffin at Ole Miss.

Wright was among a group of players who sued in a Louisiana court, saying the new NCAA rule granting five years of eligibility to most athletes should apply to him and others who were not "grandfathered" into the rule, which did not include the high school Class of 2022.

"Over 100 athletes in multiple sports were cleared and said you could go play. That's a court order," Kiffin said Tuesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" on ESPN. "If you think back on all the different court orders of great players that were granted — whether that's Diego Pavia or, now, Trinidad [Chambliss] that were allowed to play a sixth year, we followed all court orders. I think you get into a really interesting situation as a conference if you're now saying, 'Well, we're not going to follow this court order.' These kids that a court says can go anywhere, we're going to say, 'No you can't.'"

The situation has drawn sharp criticism among coaches in college and the NFL. Rams coach Sean McVay said reversing the college football-to-NFL pipeline was mind-boggling.

"I don't know enough about it, other than the fact guys that can be in NFL camps, if it doesn't go down for them, they can go back to college," McVay said. "I mean, I feel like I took a freaking gummy. I don't even understand it. It's true. I mean, looking at this stuff, I'm like, surely that's not real. But I just try to stay in my lane. But I would say it's very unique and it's very different."

Correspondent Jordan Puente and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

Hendrick is among 16 players who sought a Louisiana temporary restraining order allowing them to return to college after entering the NFL draft pool, arguing they would not have left had they know NCAA rules would change granting them an extra year of eligibility.

articles.title: SEC announces ban for former pros: Does this make Mark Mitchell ineligible?
articles.summary: Mark Mitchell committed to Kentucky, but it just got more difficult for him to actually suit up for the Wildcats.
articles.body:
The SEC is joining the Big Ten in prohibiting players who have moved on to professional sports from returning to play college sports at an SEC school.

On Tuesday, the league announced new bylaws to prevent professional players from returning to school.

Going forward, SEC schools are not permitted to have an athlete on a roster who has:

Previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA Draft, and did not appropriately withdraw,

Signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team, or

Been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate roster).

SEC commissioner Greg Sankey is also now authorized to enforce this expectation with penalties against member institutions.

Further, here is what else the SEC had to say:

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference," the SEC's statement read. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition."

So, what does this mean for Kentucky? It certainly makes it harder for guys like Mark Mitchell to play this season. Mitchell technically declared for the NBA Draft and agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract so he could play in the NBA Summer League for the Denver Nuggets. But at the time, he was effectively forced to do so since his eligibility clock was up.

A Louisville judge recently ruled that Mitchell is eligible for a fifth season of college basketball . Will that ruling hold up against these new SEC bylaws?

That remains to be seen, but one thing is for sure: These new rules implemented by the SEC just made it more difficult for Mitchell and other class of 2022 players to play one more season. It's unclear if these new bylaws mean Mitchell is now ineligible for next season, though the safe bet would be that, as of right now, he would not be allowed to play in games.

One thing Kentucky and Mitchell do have going for them is there's still plenty of time before the season tips off. They're definitely going to need several more weeks at the very least to get this all sorted out and, hopefully, have a final decision made whether Mitchell can play this season.

Expect more lawsuits to be filed and the fight to continue for those 2022 players to get one more season.

articles.title: How bad is the NFL's CTE problem? A new study just answered that and it's grim
articles.summary: NFL News: A study published Tuesday in the British Medical Journal has put a number to what many in football have long feared. At least one in four NFL players .
articles.body: A study published Tuesday in the British Medical Journal has put a number to what many in football have long feared. At least one in four NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the degenerative brain disease better known as CTE. The research, led by scientists from Harvard Medical School, Massachusetts General Hospital, and Boston University, focused on 878 former NFL players who died in that six-year period. Of that group, at least 215 of them, or 24.5 percent, had CTE. And here is the part that should make the NFL uncomfortable: researchers say that 25 percent figure is likely the floor, not the ceiling.What does the new CTE study actually say about NFL players?The estimate of 25 percent is on the "low end," said Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, the study's lead author. The study found that the maximum possible prevalence of CTE was around 97 percent, but the true rate "is somewhere in the middle," Daneshvar said.That range between 25 and 97 percent sounds staggeringly wide, but it reflects a core limitation of CTE research: the disease can only be confirmed in dead tissue. CTE can be diagnosed only after death, so most research has depended on brains donated by players or their families. Of the 878 players in the sample, only 338 actually had their brains examined. The remaining 643 were never studied. Daneshvar's team ran statistical models to estimate what that missing data might look like, which is why the range is so broad.Jesse Mez, a BU CTE Center codirector of clinical research, put it plainly: "If at least 25 percent of NFL players who died had these changes in their brain, then this seems like a call to action for more discussion about risk, more research, and more support for affected families."When applied to active players, that would mean about 400 of the current 1,696 active players could develop CTE. That is not a projection the NFL or the NFLPA can easily dismiss. The NFLPA said in a statement: "This study is a sobering reminder that football carries real risks, and those risks can have lasting consequences for players and their families. The findings should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem."Does the NFL's kickoff rule change make the CTE problem worse?The timing of this study lands in the middle of a live debate inside the league. When the touchback changed to the 35 and teams became incentivized to put more kickoffs in play, concussions spiked. Specifically for the player returning the kick and the player tackling him.That matters because the new BMJ study adds statistical pressure to what some team officials have already been saying privately. As one source put it, it was "the elephant in the room" at the annual league meetings in March. Moving the touchback line from the 30 to the 35 brought more returns, more collisions, and more concussions. Those concussions, accumulated over careers, are precisely what researchers link to CTE development.There is now a camp inside the league that wants the touchback point moved back to the 30. The new study will cause the opponents of the 35-yard touchback point to argue even more loudly that it should return to the 30.There is also an important caveat worth noting. The average age of the former players whose brains were donated was around 66 years old, meaning most of their professional football careers took place before 2005, when CTE was first diagnosed in a former NFL player. One researcher noted this "may not represent the NFL in 2026," given the rule changes and safety improvements made since then. That is a reasonable qualifier. But it does not make the numbers disappear.The NFL has spent years managing this conversation carefully. This study, peer-reviewed and published in one of medicine's most respected journals, makes that harder.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kubiak: Raiders will decide when to start Mendoza based on his play and not the offense as a whole
articles.summary: The Raiders' offensive line is far from proven, no wide receiver has emerged as a true No. 1 and a rookie could be the starting running back entering the sea...
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. (AP) — The Raiders' offensive line is far from proven, no wide receiver has emerged as a true No. 1 and a rookie could be the starting running back entering the season.

Probably not the ideal situation to start a first-year quarterback, but players drafted first overall — as Fernando Mendoza was — usually join a team with a lot more questions than answers.

Could that be a factor for when Raiders coaches decide to start Mendoza? He likely will be the backup to Kirk Cousins when the season opens Sept. 13 against Miami .

"They've all got to get ready," coach Klint Kubiak said. "Whoever is playing quarterback for us, it's a team thing. It's not the QB playing well and everyone else is not or the other way around."

The Raiders' offense last season was statistically the worst in the NFL. Las Vegas' averages of 14.2 points and 245.2 yards per game were each last in the league.

It didn't help that the Raiders' offensive line also was statistically at the bottom, but management hopes that is no longer the case . The club signed three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum to the richest contract ever for an interior offensive lineman. Kolton Miller , who missed all but four games last season because of an ankle injury, is one of the league's best left tackles.

But how much the Raiders improve up front remains a question, particularly at right guard where Jackson Powers-Johnson is competing with Caleb Rogers for the starting role.

Also questionable is how the receiving corps will perform even without a clear-cut first option. Kubiak criticized the receivers after Thursday's 22-20 preseason victory at Houston .

"When you go out and you have trouble with your assignments, I'm going to have an opinion about it, and it's not just them," Kubiak said Tuesday. "We've had plenty of other guys that have got to step up. A lot of young guys, and then guys that we're counting on in that receiver room."

Now there's also the significant question at running back after second-year starter Ashton Jeanty went down with an injury in practice Sunday. He was unable to put pressure on his right leg as he was helped off the field, and the Raiders have been quiet about his prognosis.

Rookie Mike Washington Jr., drafted in the fourth round, is taking first-team snaps in practice. He also has performed well enough in training camp that he was getting some of those repetitions even when Jeanty was healthy.

So the Raiders have some decisions to make, most notably at quarterback and when to turn the offense over to Mendoza, the Heisman Trophy winner last year at Indiana. It seems like a matter of time before Mendoza takes over, and Kubiak continues to insist it's an ongoing competition even with Cousins still quarterbacking the starting offense in practice.

But as Kubiak said, the decision on when to play Mendoza will depend on the quarterback and not the offense around him.

"We're trying to grow in all phases of our offense, every player, every position group," offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said. "Ultimately, coach (Kubiak) has the final say on how and when we're going to play this person, that person, and not just quarterback, but any position group, and how players develop over time. We like to see the guys develop in practice, we like to see what they're doing in these preseason games and then basing decisions on that."

Kubiak was asked several ways Tuesday about Jeanty's health, and he refused to bite.

Raiders players and coach knelt and prayed when Jeanty was hurt.

"I think that says a lot about him being on the mend and us counting on him," Kubiak said, the closest he came to providing an indication on where Jeanty stands. "So really excited to get him back, and I'm a huge believer in the power of prayer."

One of the major questions regarding Mendoza was how he would be able to adjust to taking snaps directly under center. He took snaps out of shotgun almost exclusively at Indiana.

Linderbaum didn't even realize that was the case, an indication of how well Mendoza has adjusted.

"Under center, he's perfect," said Jordan Meredith , the backup center who has worked most closely with Mendoza. "I've had no issues the whole time. He's been detail oriented in the huddle, taking command of every play that he gets. I see that he's ready for anything the coaches ask of him."

The Raiders host San Francisco on Thursday night in the final preseason game for both teams. Kubiak's brother, Klay, is the 49ers' offensive coordinator.

"My brother is the smartest guy in the family, and I'm not kidding," Klint Kubiak said. "He's brilliant, works really hard. I love him. Not going to love him on Thursday night."

articles.title: âWe intentionally didnât do..â: How Patrick Mahomesâ early strategy helped turn his rookie-year restraint into a business empire beyond NFL
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes had endorsement offers waiting for him before he had established himself as the Kansas City Chiefsâ starting quarterback. Yet during h.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had endorsement offers waiting for him before he had established himself as the Kansas City Chiefsâ starting quarterback. Yet during his rookie season in 2017, Mahomes and his representatives deliberately kept those opportunities limited. They wanted his first year to focus on football, the Chiefs locker room and learning from veteran quarterback Alex Smith.That decision looks very different today. Patrick Mahomes has built one of the NFLâs strongest commercial profiles, but his business interests now go beyond advertisements. His portfolio includes sports ownership, investments and partnerships that have helped turn his name into a business brand away from the Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes chose football before endorsements as a rookieThe Chiefs selected Patrick Mahomes with the 10th pick in the 2017 NFL Draft after trading up for him. However, Andy Reid kept Alex Smith as the starter, leaving Mahomes with just one appearance during his first season. He finally started the Week 17 game against the Denver Broncos on December 31, 2017, after Kansas City had already secured the AFC West. Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 284 yards and one interception in the Chiefsâ 27-24 victory.That limited playing time shaped his approach to endorsements. articles.title: Falcons' starting QB post is Michael Penix Jr's to lose amid Tua Tagovailoa's struggles: report
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa's inconsistent play in training camp and preseason has reportedly made the Atlanta Falcons' starting job Michael Penix Jr.'s to lose.
articles.body: Tua Tagovailoa’s next chapter in the NFL isn’t going well at all, so much so that the Atlanta Falcons may have to rush Michael Penix Jr. back faster than they hoped. When Tagovailoa joined the Falcons after being released by the Miami Dolphins ahead of this season, the team reportedly hoped he would play well enough in new head coach Kevin Stefanski’s offense that it would be comfortable starting the season with the veteran left-hander while Penix, coming off an ACL injury, had more time to recover. However, ESPN/NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport is reporting that the Falcons’ starting job is for Penix to lose at this point following Tagovailoa’s inconsistent play in training camp and the first preseason game. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "It really seemed that the goal of the entire organization was to have Tua be the starting quarterback right away to start the season," Rapoport said. "Let Michael Penix come along slow. …Really you’d like him to be inactive for the first several games and really just take his time and make sure he’s fully healthy." Tagovailoa has not set himself apart from the pack in terms of performance at camp, and he went 3-of-5 for 22 yards in the first preseason game against the Denver Broncos before Stefanski moved on to Jack Strand and Cooper Rush at quarterback for the rest of the contest. "Tua’s play made that impossible, not just in the preseason game, which we’ve seen, but it sounds like practice as well. All of which is to say, this is Michael Penix’s job for the taking," Rapoport continued. SEAN PAYTON TAKES VICIOUS SHOT AT FALCONS HOME CROWD AFTER HUMILIATING FIRST HALF In an ideal world, the Falcons hoped a fresh start for Tagovailoa would’ve been just what he needed for a heated training camp competition for the team’s starting job. Instead, with Penix getting back into the fold this week and splitting first-team reps, it appears they’re now hoping he can feel confident and, more importantly, be healthy enough to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1. "Everything we do around this building is competing," Stefanski said. "I know it’s easy to say, ‘position battles,’ and those types of things, but we’re constantly competing. That’s not the focus for our guys. Our guys are pushing each other by showing up and putting in the work." Then again, perhaps Tagovailoa’s play in the final preseason game against his former Dolphins squad can boost his confidence and chances at the starting job this Friday. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It’s not looking too good for him now, though, as Stefanski and his staff have an important decision to make before that Sept. 13 kickoff on the road in Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Tom Brady embraces a new side of himself with Gucci as Dave Portnoy pokes fun at his unexpected fashion turn
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady is showing fans a side of himself they rarely see. At 49, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has stepped into the fashion world as the face .
articles.body: Tom Brady is showing fans a side of himself they rarely see. At 49, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has stepped into the fashion world as the face of a new Gucci campaign, trading his familiar football and broadcasting style for bold leather looks. His transformation quickly caught the attention of Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, who jokingly questioned Bradyâs new image online. While the trolling added some humor to the moment, Brady appears to be genuinely enjoying the experience and has even developed a surprising appreciation for leather.Dave Portnoy wastes no time teasing Tom Brady over his bold Gucci transformationBradyâs Gucci campaign features two very different looks, both far removed from the polished suits fans usually see him wearing during his Fox Sports broadcasts.One outfit features a dark gray and sage-green satin double-breasted jacket with wide peak lapels and matching trousers. Brady wore the jacket without a shirt, giving the look a much more relaxed and fashion-focused feel. A silver cuff bracelet and dark shoes completed the outfit.The second look went even further. Brady appeared in a black leather jacket with broad lapels and structured shoulders, paired with matching leather pants and pointed boots.That particular look gave Portnoy an opening to have some fun. After GQâs interview with Brady was shared by OK! Magazine, Portnoy quote-tweeted the post with a short message aimed at the former quarterback.âBLINK TWICE IF YOU NEED HELP TOMMY!âThe joke quickly added a sports-world perspective to Bradyâs fashion moment. Portnoyâs reaction was playful, but it also highlighted just how unusual it is to see one of footballâs most recognizable figures embracing such a different style.Brady, however, appears to be enjoying the change rather than taking himself too seriously.Tom Brady says stepping outside football led him to discover a surprising love for leatherThe Gucci campaign is not Bradyâs first major step into fashion this year. In May, he made his runway debut during Gucciâs Cruise 2027 show in Times Square, marking a major change from the world he dominated for more than two decades.Interestingly, Brady said he did not have a close relationship with Gucci before the opportunity arrived. The initial phone call caught him off guard, but curiosity eventually replaced the surprise.âNot much, ironically, so it was a fun phone call,â Brady said about his previous connection with Gucci. âAt first, there was a bit of like, âWait, say that again?ââFor Brady, the appeal was not simply about wearing expensive clothes or appearing in a major campaign. He viewed the experience as a chance to try something completely unfamiliar.âYou have these once-in-a-lifetime opportunities, and that's how I saw it,â he said.The former quarterback also discovered that leather was more comfortable than he expected. His Gucci experience has even changed what he keeps in his own closet.âIâd never really done leather on leather before, but there are some leather pants in my closet now,â Brady told GQ. âI thought, âDamn, thatâs actually really comfortable.â I could see why people wear this.âBrady has not committed to becoming a full-time model, but he has left the door open for more fashion work.âI would never say never to doing anything,â Brady said.His reasoning fits the mindset that defined much of his football career. For Brady, trying something new is part of continuing to grow, even when it means stepping far outside familiar territory.âI always say the only place for growth is outside your comfort zone,â Brady said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
